author: Publicación Abierta
title: Turismo masivo y la violación de derechos humanos en pueblos originarios de América Latina
content:
El turismo de masas en América Latina se ha consolidado como un mecanismo de dominación que trasciende su apariencia de actividad económica inocua. Este artículo analiza cómo la práctica turística masiva constituye un vehículo para la violación sistemática de los derechos humanos de las comunidades aborígenes, operando como una colonización silenciosa que afecta sus territorios, culturas, economías y formas de vida. A partir del marco teórico del pensamiento nacional y latinoamericano, y tomando como referencia estudios de caso como la Amazonia brasileña, las islas de Uros en Perú y la situación maya en México, se evidencia un patrón de desposesión, inculturación y vulneración de derechos fundamentales que perpetúa estructuras coloniales bajo el ropaje del desarrollo turístico.


América Latina alberga entre 40 y 50 millones de indígenas, representando entre el 8% y el 10% de la población total de la región. Estos pueblos, descendientes directos de sociedades precoloniales, mantienen un vínculo especial con sus territorios ancestrales y una identidad étnica que los distingue de la sociedad dominante. Sin embargo, la irrupción del turismo masivo ha introducido una nueva dimensión de vulneración de derechos que profundiza cinco siglos de injusticia histórica.


El turismo, concebido desde una perspectiva crítica, no constituye un simple fenómeno de planificación del ocio y el tiempo libre, sino que trae aparejados mecanismos ocultos de dominación, expoliación y colonización. Esta investigación sostiene que el turismo masivo opera como un mecanismo de colonización silenciosa que viola los derechos humanos de las comunidades aborígenes en dimensiones económicas, socioculturales, ideológicas y geopolíticas.


La colonización silenciosa y el poder blando


El concepto de “poder blando” (

soft power

), acuñado por Joseph Nye, se refiere a la capacidad de un país para influir en otro mediante la atracción y la persuasión, en contraposición a la coerción militar o económica. Esta herramienta geopolítica encuentra en el turismo un vehículo privilegiado para la inoculación de valores, modos de vida y formas de consumo que socavan las bases culturales e identitarias de los pueblos originarios.


El filósofo argentino Juan José Hernández Arregui, en su obra Imperialismo y Cultura, advierte sobre cómo las culturas dominantes se imponen sobre las dominadas a través de un proceso sistemático de colonización pedagógica que destruye la autoconciencia de los pueblos y su “ser nacional”. Esta colonización mental constituye el requisito indispensable para la colonización material, tal como sostiene Fermín Chávez.


Rodolfo Kusch desarrolló el concepto de “inculturación” para describir el proceso por el cual una cultura dominante se monta sobre otra dominada, integrándola forzosamente y silenciando sus expresiones propias. En el contexto turístico, este fenómeno se manifiesta cuando las comunidades aborígenes deben abandonar sus economías de subsistencia, sus tradiciones y su cultura para someterse a la industria de los servicios turísticos, adoptando modos de vida ajenos que responden a los deseos y expectativas del visitante extranjero.


La inculturación no es un proceso neutral; implica una relación de poder asimétrica donde la cultura del turista—generalmente de países centrales—se impone sobre la cultura local, generando una nueva creación que, lejos de ser auténtica, constituye una teatralización al servicio del mercado.


La Amazonia brasileña: el pulmón del planeta como mercancía


La Amazonia brasileña constituye un paradigma de explotación extractivista donde el turismo se inserta como herramienta de un mecanismo más amplio de colonización. Esta región, que alberga la mayor concentración de pueblos originarios del mundo, padece un proceso de inculturación acelerado que afecta todos los aspectos de la vida comunitaria.


Las comunidades indígenas de la Amazonia han visto alterada su dieta tradicional, su indumentaria y sus prácticas culturales para satisfacer las expectativas del turista. Los operadores turísticos solicitan que los aborígenes vistan prendas que ocultan su desnudez tradicional y que aprendan lenguas extranjeras para comunicarse directamente con los visitantes. Más grave aún, se fomenta que estas comunidades reciban a turistas para explicar sus modos de vida, transformando su existencia en una mera teatralización donde la autenticidad cultural se sacrifica en el altar del mercado.


El grado de imperialismo …

author: Unknown
title: KCDP: At least 22 women were killed, 33 others died under suspicious circumstances in August
content:
At least 22 women were killed by men in Turkey in August. Another 33 women died under suspicious circumstances, according to the monthly report published on Wednesday by the We Will Stop Femicides Platform (KCDP). Since the beginning of the year, the organization has documented at least 197 femicides and 215 suspicious deaths.


The KCDP has been compiling its own data on femicides since 2010. According to the organization, one reason for doing so is that state authorities do not publish systematic statistics on femicides. The documentation is based on cases reported in the media as well as reports submitted directly to the platform.


Perpetrators mostly from women’s immediate circles


The figures for August once again show that the greatest threat to women often comes from men in their immediate circles. Nine of the 22 women were killed by their husbands. Two women were killed by former partners, one by her ex-husband, two by their sons and one by her father. In other cases, the perpetrators were acquaintances or other relatives. This means that 41 percent of the women killed in August were murdered by their husbands.


The locations of the killings also challenge the notion of the home as a safe space: twelve of the 22 women — 55 percent — were killed in their own homes. Three women were killed on the street, two in isolated locations and two in cars, while others were killed in a hotel, at their workplace or in another public place.


Firearms used in nearly two-thirds of cases


Fourteen of the 22 women — 64 percent — were shot dead with firearms. Three were killed with bladed weapons, two died after being thrown or falling from a height, one woman was burned to death and another was strangled. In one further case, the exact cause of death could not be determined. According to the KCDP, five of the killings were linked to decisions the women had made about their own lives. In one case, an economic motive was identified. In 16 of the 22 femicides, it has not yet been determined what pretext the perpetrators used for their actions.


The platform sees this in particular as a structural problem: “As long as it is not established by whom and why women were killed, legal proceedings are not conducted effectively, perpetrators are not given deterrent sentences, and preventive measures are not implemented, violence will continue to manifest itself in ever new forms,” the report stated.


‘It is not the women’s deaths that remain suspicious, but the truth’


The high number of unresolved deaths is particularly alarming to the KCDP. With 33 cases in August, the figure once again exceeded the number of killings recorded as femicides. Under the heading “It Is Not the Women’s Deaths That Remain Suspicious, but the Truth,” the platform cited, among others, the cases of Rojin Kabaiş, Gülistan Doku and Aysun Yıldırım.


Evidence secured too late, contradictions that were not adequately investigated, and the premature classification of deaths as suicides or accidents have hindered efforts to establish the truth and deepened impunity.


“No woman’s death must remain unresolved. Every suspicious death must be effectively investigated to determine whether male violence was involved,” the KCDP demanded.


At the same time, the report makes clear that existing protection mechanisms repeatedly fail to protect women from lethal violence. Several of the women murdered in August had previously experienced violence and threats or had obtained protective measures against the men who later killed them. The KCDP therefore calls not only for action after a killing has occurred, but also for the consistent implementation of effective protection and prevention mechanisms.

author: Rayén Garance Feil
title: Behördenversagen ist kein Einzelfall
content:
NSU, Neukölln, Hanau. „Futur Drei“-Regisseur Faraz Shariats neuer Justizthriller „Staatsschutz“ zeigt den Kampf gegen rechten Terror und institutionellen Rassismus in der Justiz.

Seyo Kim ist frisch ausgebildete Staatsanwältin in einer ostdeutschen Stadt. Ihre Wohnung hat sie gerade erst bezogen, die Kartons sind noch unausgepackt. In einer der ersten Szenen muss sie in einem Fall für Freispruch plädieren, aus Mangel an Beweisen. Auf der anderen Seite des Gerichtssaals sitzt ein Mann, der aussieht, als könnte er ein Nazi sein. Die Justiz hat ihre Regeln, das muss auch Seyos Idealismus aushalten. Schon bald befindet Seyo sich aber auf der anderen Seite des Justizsystems. Als sie durch einen Park radelt, wird sie von einem anderen Fahrer unter einer Brücke von ihrem Rad gestoßen. Ein Komplize des Angreifers bewirft sie von der Brücke mit einem Molotowcocktail. Schnell befreit sie sich von ihrer brennenden Jacke. Trotz des Schocks und ihrer Verletzungen funktioniert sie sofort, weiß, was jetzt wichtig ist. Der rassistische Anschlag verändert Seyo. Sie schneidet sich die Haare, scheint rougher und unangepasster aufzutreten als zuvor. Ihre Freundin schenkt ihr eine Kette – eine Art Talisman, den sie fortan immer trägt. Seyo schafft es, einen der Täter vor Gericht zu bringen. Entschlossen, sich zu verteidigen und ihre Angreifer zur Rechenschaft zu ziehen, nutzt sie ihren Zugang zu Informationen in der Staatsanwaltschaft. Ein Kollege wirft ihr vor, sie würde versuchen, sich durch ihre Rolle einen Vorteil zu verschaffen. Doch vielmehr versucht Seyo, die Nachteile, denen sie ausgesetzt ist, auszugleichen. Denn wie bald immer deutlicher wird, gibt es Verstrickungen ihrer Behörde mit den Angeklagten und Unklarheiten in alten Fällen, von denen sie einen Zusammenhang mit ihrem vermutet. author: Mag
title: Rassismus, Sexismus und ein Klima der Angst bei der Basler Polizei – nun wissenschaftlich belegt
content:
Dossier


„

Was die unabhängige Personalbefragung der Kantonspolizei Basel-Stadt über die Zustände im Korps aussagt, ist katastrophal: eine Kultur der Angst, eine veraltete Macho-Kultur, ein totaler Vertrauensverlust. (…) Markus Schefer, der Professor für Staats- und Verwaltungsrecht an der Uni Basel ist die erste gewählte Telefonnummer von Journalist*innen, wenn es eine Debatte über das Vorgehen der Polizei bei Demos gibt – er war beauftragt worden, die schiefe Personallage der Polizei zu untersuchen. Unterstützt wurde er von Claudia Puglisi, einer Polizeidirektor*in aus Niedersachsen, die bei der Präsentation neben ihm sass – ihr besorgt wirkender Blick spiegelte die Drastik der Ergebnisse wider. Denn an heftig negativen Begrifflichkeiten mangelt es im 42-seitigen Dokument sicherlich nicht.  (…) Die Kritik konzentriert sich auf Polizeikommandant Martin Roth. Er ist medial angeschlagen, seit linke Politiker*innen im Frühjahr 2023 wegen des

Gummischrot-Einsatzes der Frauentags-Demo


 seinen

Rücktritt


 forderten

…“

Artikel von David Rutschmann vom 21. Juni 2024 in bajour


 („Kein Lodern, ein Flammen“) – u.a. wurden Polizistinnen wurden in «fi**bar» oder «unf**kbar» unterteilt… Siehe dazu mehr Infos:


Das Gummischrot war illegal: Das Basler Appellationsgericht rügt die Polizei wegen eines Einsatzes gegen den feministischen Kampftag 2023


„Jahrelang war es so selten wie eine Fasnacht im Sommer, dass Basler Gerichte der Basler Polizei Grenzen setzen. Das ändert sich glücklicherweise gerade (…). Schritt für Schritt weist die Justiz ein entfesseltes Korps in die Schranken. Das neuste Urteil des Appellationsgerichts, das der WOZ exklusiv vorliegt, ist diesbezüglich ein Meilenstein. Darin erklärt das Gericht das Abfeuern von Gummischrot in eine Menschengruppe, von der keine konkrete Gefahr ausgeht, als illegal. Einen Klassiker der Basler Demobekämpfung. (…) Beurteilt hat das Gericht den Polizeieinsatz gegen den feministischen Kampftag am 8. März 2023. Damals versammelten sich rund 250 Personen vor der Universität. Und wurden, als sie sich in Bewegung setzen wollten, eingekesselt. Kurz darauf begannen die Polizist:innen, mit Gummischrot auf die Demonstrant:innen zu feuern. Doch nur die ersten drei Salven, so das Appellationsgericht, waren verhältnismässig. Diese erfolgten, als sich der Demozug in Richtung der Polizeikette bewegte. Die weiteren Salven waren rechtswidrig. (…) [S]elbst wenn der Mindestabstand eingehalten worden wäre, so das Gericht, hätte das den Gummischroteinsatz nicht gerechtfertigt. Dieser sei rechtswidrig gewesen (…)  In den weiteren Punkten des Urteils zeigt sich dann allerdings, dass auch das Basler Appellationsgericht alten Gewohnheiten nachhängt und noch immer gerne die Argumentation der Polizei übernimmt: Bei der Personenkontrolle sollen Polizistinnen mehreren Demonstrant:innen in die Unterhosen gegriffen haben. Die Polizei bestreitet dies – und das Gericht stellt sich auf ihre Seite. Die objektive Beweislast liege bei den Kläger:innen. In der dritten wichtigen Frage des Urteils geht es um die Rechtmässigkeit des Polizeikessels. Mit einer abenteuerlichen Begründung wischt das Appellationsgericht ein Urteil des Europäischen Gerichtshofs für Menschenrechte (EGMR) vom Tisch, das Anfang 2024 verlangte, dass ein solcher Kessel nicht ohne genau festgelegte Rahmenbedingungen möglich sei, etwa was die Dauer betreffe. In Basel ist das bloss rudimentär geregelt. Mehr sei auch nicht nötig, befindet das Gericht geradezu anmassend: «Diese für eine polizeiliche Technik wie die Einkesselung aussergewöhnlich hohen Anforderungen können für die Schweiz nicht verbindlich sein.» Es reiche aus, dass im Polizeigesetz allgemeines polizeiliches Handeln und Personenkontrollen geregelt seien – auch wenn der Kessel nicht explizit vorkommt. Constanze Seelmann, die die Demonstrant:innen rechtlich vertritt, wird in deren Auftrag den Entscheid ans Bundesgericht weiterziehen. «Das Appellationsgericht hat sich nicht richtig mit dem EGMR-Urteil befasst. Die Schweiz braucht aber ein Grundsatzurteil, ob und falls ja, unter welchen Umständen ein Polizeikessel zulässig ist.» (…) Wie leichtfertig in Basel eingekesselt wird, zeigte sich an der Palästina-Solidemo vergangenen Samstag. (…) Die Demonstrant:innen mussten bis zu zehn Stunden im Kessel ausharren. Dazu ging die Polizei mit Schäferhunden und Pfefferspray auf Personen los, die sich nicht rechtzeitig aus dem gesperrten Perimeter entfernten oder entfernen konnten. Immerhin …

author: Unknown
title: 6 Şubat’ta yakınlarını kaybeden ailelerin nöbeti sürüyor: “Faillerin kollandığını görüyoruz”
content:
Ankara – 6 Şubat depremlerinde yaşamını yitiren yurttaşların ailelerinin oluşturduğu Adalet Peşinde Aileleri Platformu üyelerinin, Adalet Bakanlığı önünde başlattığı adalet nöbeti 6. gününde. Emek Partisi Milletvekili Sevda Karaca ve BİRTEK-SEN Genel Başkanı Mehmet Türkmen aileleri ziyaret etti. Aileler ile basın açıklaması gerçekleştiren Karaca, ailelerin 11 kentte adalet sarayları önünde nöbet tuttuğunu hatırlatarak, yaşanan adaletsizliklerin aileleri Ankara’ya getirdiğini vurguladı.

Deprem davalarında bilirkişi raporlarında ciddi sorunlar yaşandığını belirten Karaca, kamu görevlilerinin yargılanmamasına ve bazı durumlarda soruşturma izni dahi verilmemesine tepki göstererek, “Biz her bir müteahhidin, her bir sorumlunun neredeyse sırtının sıvazlandığı bir adalet mücadelesi veriyoruz” ifadelerini kullandı.

Depremin yıkıcılığından sorumlu kişilerin devlet yetkilileriyle birlikte fotoğraflar verdiğini belirten Karaca şöyle devam etti: “Bizim canlarımızın faili olanların korunup kollandığını, devlet yetkilileri ile poz verdiklerini, devlet bürokrasisi içerisinde pohpohlandıklarını görüyoruz. Fotoğraflar birlikte fotoğraflar vermekten çekinmediklerini görüyoruz. Ve soruyoruz kardeşim: Bizim canlarımızın hesabı henüz verilmemişken neden kamu görevlilerini, neden müteahhitleri, neden inşaat şirketlerini, neden deprem cinayetlerinde parmağı olan katilleri koruyorsunuz.”

Adalet Bakanı’nın farklı davalar üzerinden kamuoyuna adalet mesajı verdiğini hatırlatan Karaca, depremzede ailelerin dosyalardan ibaret olmadığını vurguladı. Karaca, “Adalet Bakanı bugün pek çok yerde, faili meçhul cinayetlerden tutalım kadın cinayetlerine, çocuk istismarı davalarından gazeteci davalarına kadar pek çok şeyi halkın gözünde kendisini gerçek bir Adalet Bakanı gibi göstermek üzere dosyalarının kapaklarını açtığını söyleyerek süslüyor, bize anlatıyor. Biz dosya değiliz, biz canız ve canlarımızın hesabının görülmesi için illaki çeşitli klik savaşlarınızı yaşamanızı beklemek zorunda değiliz” ifadelerini kullandı.

Açıklamada konuşan depremzede ailelerden bir yurttaş, “Burada iki kelime önemli; makul ve etkin. Makul süreden kasıt nedir, bunu duymak isteriz” dedi.

Davalarda sanıkların olmadığı duruşmaların görüldüğünü dile getiren yurttaş, “Bakın, bu bir duruşma olamaz. Sanıkların sağlık ya da makul bir sebebiyle davaya katılmaması da söz konusu değil. Bayağı, bildiğiniz, hakkında bir duruşma olan sanık herhangi bir mazeret bildirmeden, herhangi bir sağlık problemi bildirmeden duruşmaya gelmiyor. Kim var davada, duruşmada? Hakimler var, savcı var, müşteki avukatları var, yaralı, acılı aileler var, platformumuz var. Kim yok? Sanıklar yok. Sanıkların olmadığı bir duruşmada hangi etkinlikten bahsedeceğiz?” dedi.

Bilirkişi raporlarının erken düzenlenmesi için Bakan’dan ve hükümetten yeni bir düzenleme talepleri olduğunu ifade eden yurttaş, “Bir buçuk yıl içerisinde gelmeyen adalet, adalet değildir. Bilirkişi raporu sadece bir buçuk yıl süre alıyorsa, siz varın hesap edin” diye konuştu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Altı Avrupa ülkesi ve BM İnsan Hakları Komiseri'nden Türkiye’ye LGBTİ+ operasyonları tepkisi
content:
Türkiye’de LGBTİ+ örgütleri, hak savunucuları ve aktivistlere yönelik operasyonlara uluslararası tepkiler, altı Avrupa ülkesinin ortak açıklamasıyla genişledi.


Almanya, Fransa, Hollanda, İsveç, Finlandiya ve İzlanda’nın dışişleri teşkilatlarındaki insan hakları ve LGBTİ+ haklarından sorumlu büyükelçi ve özel temsilciler, 12 Eylül’den bu yana özellikle insan hakları savunucuları ve LGBTİ+ örgütlerine yönelik uygulamaları “son derece endişe verici” olarak niteledi. 


Altı ülkenin temsilcileri, Türkiye’nin, taraf olduğu uluslararası insan hakları sözleşmeleri ve Avrupa İnsan Hakları Sözleşmesi’nden (AİHS) doğan yükümlülüklerine işaret ederek, barışçıl toplanma ve örgütlenme hakları ile ifade özgürlüğüne LGBTİ+ kişiler bakımından da tam olarak saygı gösterilmesi çağrısında bulundu.


Ortak açıklamada Türkiye’deki LGBTİ+ kişilerle “tam dayanışma” içinde olunduğu da belirtildi. 


BM: 150’yi aşkın insan gözaltına alındı veya tutuklandı


Birleşmiş Milletler İnsan Hakları Ofisi de operasyonların boyutuna ve gözaltında kötü muamele iddialarına dikkat çekti.


BM, 150’den fazla LGBTİQ+ kişi ve insan hakları savunucusunun gözaltına alındığı veya tutuklandığına ilişkin haberlerden, gözaltında kötü muamele iddialarından ve operasyonların sivil toplum alanı üzerindeki olası etkilerinden “derin endişe” duyulduğunu bildirdi.


BM İnsan Hakları Yüksek Komiseri Volker Türk, Türkiye makamlarını cinsel yönelim veya cinsiyet kimliği dahil hiçbir ayrım gözetmeksizin herkesin insan haklarını korumaya ve keyfi olarak gözaltında tutulanları derhal serbest bırakmaya çağırdı.


En az 81 kişi tutuklandı


Adalet Bakanlığının “Ailem Güvende” adını verdiği soruşturmalar İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir, Aydın ve Mersin başsavcılıklarının koordinasyonunda 15 ili kapsıyor.


Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, soruşturmalar kapsamında 162 kişi, dokuz dernek ve 13 işletme hakkında adli işlem başlatıldığını açıklamıştı. Bakanlık operasyonları çocukların, aile kurumunun ve “toplum düzeninin” korunması gerekçesiyle savunuyor. Şüphelilere yöneltilen suçlamalar arasında “müstehcenlik” ile “fuhşa teşvik, aracılık veya yer temin etme” bulunuyor.


17 Eylül akşamı itibarıyla çeşitli kentlerde en az 81 kişi tutuklandı. Daha geç saatlerde yayımlanan bazı haberlerde sayı 82 olarak verildi. Tutuklananların tamamı LGBTİ+ hak savunucusu değil; soruşturmalar hak örgütleri ve aktivistlerin yanı sıra fuhuş, uyuşturucu ve başka suçlarla itham edilen kişileri de kapsıyor.


İstanbul’da son olarak hakim karşısına çıkarılan 33 kişiden 20’si tutuklandı, 13’ü adli kontrolle serbest bırakıldı. Tutuklananlar arasında Hevi LGBTİ+, Pozitif-iz, SPoD ve Lambdaistanbul gibi örgütlerden en az dokuz kişinin bulunduğu bildirildi. 


Savcılık: “Suçları Türk aile yapısınının mahiyetini zayıflatmak”


İstanbul’daki soruşturmanın tutuklamaya sevk yazılarında LGBTİ+ örgütlerine yöneltilen suçlamaların kapsamı da ortaya çıktı.


Savcılık, örgütlerin LGBTİ+ kimlikleri “özendirdiğini, teşvik ettiğini ve yaygınlaştırdığını” ve faaliyetleriyle “Türk aile yapısının mahiyetini zayıflattığını” ileri sürdü. Savcılık soruşturmanın kişilerin cinsel yönelimleri veya LGBTİ+ haklarını savunmaları nedeniyle yürütülmediğini de belirtti. 


106 protestocu serbest bırakıldı


Operasyonları protesto etmek amacıyla 15 Eylül’de İstanbul Çağlayan Adliyesi önünde yapılmak istenen açıklamaya müdahale sırasında gözaltına alınan 106 kişinin tamamı ise serbest bırakıldı.


Gözaltına alınanlar arasında eylemi izleyen BirGün muhabiri Sarya Toprak ile Alman kamu yayıncısı ARD’nin muhabiri Şener Azak da bulunuyordu. 


Operasyonlarla birlikte LGBTİ+ örgütleri ve aktivistlerin yanı sıra gazeteciler, hak örgütleri ve medya kuruluşlarına ait çok sayıda internet sitesi ve sosyal medya hesabına erişim engeli getirildi. Uluslararası Af Örgütü,


180’den fazla sosyal medya hesabının engellendiğini veya kısıtlandığını bildirdi; bunların arasında örgütün Türkiye şubesinin hesabı da bulunuyor. 


Uluslararası tepkiler genişliyor


Altı Avrupa ülkesinin ortak açıklaması, operasyonların başlamasından bu yana Ankara’ya yöneltilen uluslararası eleştirilerin devletlerarası diplomasi düzeyindeki en belirgin ortak çıkışlarından biri oldu.


Avrupa Konseyi İnsan Hakları Komiseri Michael O’Flaherty daha önce LGBTİ+'ları hedef alan operasyonlardan duyduğu kaygıyı açıklamış ve insan hakları faaliyetleri nedeniyle tutulanların serbest bırakılmasını istemişti. author: Unknown
title: “Jin Jiyan Azadî” win Best Documentary award at 6th Sulaymaniyah International Film Festival
content:
The film “Jin Jiyan Azadî” won the Best Documentary award at the 6th Sulaymaniyah International Film Festival. Directed by Soran Ibrahimi, the film features real-life individuals as its subjects.


Filmed over the course of a few days, the story captures the daily lives of female guerrillas. It also highlights their political and military struggles, their camaraderie, their communal life, and their solidarity. A significant aspect of this story is that it offers the audience an opportunity to gain an intimate understanding of these female guerrillas and their way of life.


The film also aims to showcase the struggle and lives of Kurdish women in the mountains of Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilatê Kurdistan). This struggle is part of a long history of women's resistance and can be viewed as a continuation and complement to the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” movement.


Among these guerrillas are women who have participated in political and military struggles for decades; some have actively taken part in the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” Revolution in Eastern Kurdistan.


The film’s release holds special significance as it coincides with the anniversary of the killing of Jina Amini and the start of the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” Revolution; it directly presents the stories of women whose struggles and resistance are integral to the history of the “Jin Jiyan Azadî” movement.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Santa Fe: Mumalá alertó sobre el aumento de suicidios de mujeres que habían denunciado violencia de género
content:
El Observatorio Nacional Mumalá advirtió que siete de cada diez suicidios de mujeres en el país estuvieron atravesados por situaciones de violencia de género.


Escuchá el reporte de Roque Caballero desde FM Chalet. 


La provincia de Santa Fe atraviesa un escenario crítico en la materia, lo que motivó reclamos urgentes por la declaración de emergencia. Gabriela Sosa, coordinadora de Mumalá en Santa Fe, advirtió sobre la gravedad de la situación de violencia de género en la provincia y reclamó una respuesta urgente de los poderes del Estado.


“Estamos por arriba de la tasa del mundo que mide la Organización Mundial de la Salud cuando hablamos de suicidios, pero en particular a nosotras nos interesaba incorporarle la perspectiva de género, la perspectiva de derechos humanos y la perspectiva de diversidad sexual”.


Según señaló, Santa Fe registra una de las tasas de femicidios más altas del país. Desde el primero de enero del 2020 al 31 de agosto de este año se registraron 79 suicidios femicidas y un 10% que se registraron dentro del personal de seguridad.


“En el caso de las mujeres que se han suicidado, el 71% había denunciado violencia de género previa. También hay otro dato muy particular, es que el 10% pertenecía a las fuerzas de seguridad”, aseguró la coordinadora de Mumalá.


Finalizando, Sosa aseguró que están conformes con el proyecto de ley en emergencia a las violencias de genero: “Ojalá que en buena hora sea aprobado cualquier tipo de proyecto, que sea aprobada la emergencia o que sea aprobado este proyecto que presente el Ejecutivo, porque es asumir lo que nosotros estamos planteando, que estamos en una situación grave”, además, agregó que “aprobar implica un presupuesto, y si algo hacemos las feministas es estar controlando y monitoreando lo que hace el Estado”.

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Parents of Trans Kids Slam Mount Sinai for Permanently Ending Trans Youth Care
content:
“They’re turning away children, and they’re refusing to provide care that is life-saving,” one parent said.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

On September 4, the Mount Sinai hospital system in New York City – one of the largest health networks in the city – agreed in a settlement with President Donald Trump’s Department of Justice (DOJ) to permanently stop providing gender-affirming care for minors.

The settlement also included an agreement that the hospital system will pay an undisclosed financial penalty, and that it will allocate $2 million toward former patients who want to pursue “detransition.”

This marks the latest capitulation to the Trump administration that has left parents of transgender youth worrying what comes next.

Mount Sinai has claimed that the settlement was reached to protect trans youth, as the DOJ subpoenaed multiple NYC hospital systems in May, demanding the names and medical records of transgender minors who have received care at the networks. But others have pointed out that a court order was put in place in June blocking the release of these records, so the hospital system would not have needed to take this step. In addition, the hospital had preemptively, and quietly, stopped providing care to trans youth in February – meaning the September settlement has simply formalized what the hospital had already largely enacted.

Truthout spoke to two parents of transgender children who had received care from the Mount Sinai system, who spoke on the condition of anonymity.

“I was shocked,” one parent, who we’ll call S, told Truthout. “The first thing I heard about was that Mount Sinai had been subpoenaed and that they were told to hand over records of any minors who had gotten care at the hospital, which would include my son. He was 15 when he started getting gender-affirming care at Mount Sinai.”

S told Truthout that she was shocked to be seeing such rapid changes in a state like New York, which is “supposed to be a sanctuary state for trans people.”

When S found out that Mount Sinai would be cancelling youth gender-affirming care entirely, she was “outraged,” she said. “When I think about my son, in his own words, he said that if he had not received gender-affirming care, he would be dead. He was so distressed. He wanted his body to match his understanding of himself, and without taking testosterone, he wouldn’t have that.”

Now that her son has been on hormone replacement therapy for six years, “he says he feels like a whole person,” S said.

Another parent, J, had just managed to start care for her 12-year-old daughter at Mount Sinai. “She had a lot of hoops to jump through to even be seen by the doctor, so we went through a lot of appointments and tests to even get started,” J told Truthout. “And on our first appointment, we were informed that they were going to end these youth services. So we got one treatment before we had to find another provider.”

Trying to access trans youth care in the Trump era has been “dystopian,” J said – and difficult to explain to her 12-year-old child. “I don’t want to scare her. All of this stuff is happening around her and we’re just doing our best to protect her. But when we hear things like [the DOJ is asking the hospital for] a list, we imagine the worst. Are we going to get rounded up and thrown in a cage like what ICE is doing? That’s the kind of stuff your mind goes to.”

J added that health insurance companies are now denying coverage of her daughter’s gender-affirming medication. “The medication that she takes is $50,000 for one dose, which she needs twice a year,” she said.

Mount Sinai is not the only hospital system in a Democratic-leaning state to stop offering gender-affirming care for trans youth. This year, hospital systems in New York, Connecticut, and Massachusetts have agreed to stop providing gender-affirming care to youth due to DOJ pressure and threats to their funding. Hospitals in Washington, Michigan, and California have also restricted or cut their transgender youth programs, and a court battle on such care is currently underway in Colorado.

“I think it’s totally outrageous,” S told Truthout. The hospital systems are “failing their patients,” and “caving in to an authoritarian government that is trying to take away basic rights and bodily autonomy from people. It’s up to a family and a child to make those …

author: By Andra Amber Nikolayi, Contributor
title: Berlin’s Queer Communities Reflect on Pride Attack
content:
Berlin, Germany — On Saturday, July 25, 2026 a white van rammed into the crowd at one of Europe’s largest pride celebrations, the Christopher Street Day (CSD) in Berlin Germany. One woman was killed and 29 others were injured. On Sunday, Germany’s Minister of Interior Alexander Dobrindt described it as an “Islamist terrorist attack.”


The suspect, 21 year old Berlin-born Abdul Ballout, of Lebanese descent, was shot and killed while the police were trying to apprehend him on July 26, after allegedly threatening the officers with a blade,

according

 to Al Jazeera. The suspect has been on the authorities radar for several years now, having been radicalized online and frequenting a particular extremist mosque in Berlin known for their radical beliefs that was also being monitored. The Economist

reported

 Ballout had been recently sentenced and was ordered to attend a deradicalization course after numerous attempts to join the Islamic State group.


Mainstream Media Response


While these facts have been repeated across a large number of mainstream media platforms who picked up the story, a deeper look at the story reveals a much more complex and nuanced picture. The fact that such a crime against the LGBT+ community could happen in a city that has proudly built a reputation as a safe haven for diversity and personal freedom — and

arguably the birthplace

 of the modern Western gay identity — had a huge impact both in local and international media.


The Left Berlin

 called it “a hate attack” targeting “the LGBTQIA+ community” and “a direct consequence of the rise in political violence and anti-LGBTQIA+ rhetoric promoted by the far right,” in particular the AfD and the Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Both parties currently occupy a significant number of positions both in local administration and federal government.


Politicians were quick to use this incident as a way to further their agenda, instrumentalizing the death of an LGBT+ person to push their own anti-immigrant, pro-police stance and call for further surveillance, while carefully avoiding to use words such as “gay” or “queer” and focusing on the racialized profile of the assailant. Berlin’s current Mayor

Kai Wagner

 framed it as “an attack on our free and cosmopolitan society” and thanked the police in a speech at Tiergarten. “We are open and freedom-loving — and we will preserve and defend that. The crime will be investigated and prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law,” chancellor Friedrich Merz from the

Christian Democrat Party


wrote on X

.


In an essay on

their Patreon

, queer Jewish pro-Palestine activist and author

Udi Raz

 argues that the politicians are only mourning the loss of queer bodies when it suits their political needs, saying that they weaponized the tragic incident as a general threat to people’s freedoms in order to push anti-immigrant and increased surveillance measures, while deliberately leaving out any direct LGBT+ reference. They also document how Merz and the CDU, the government elected in

February 2025

 have consistently taken measures or made policies against queer people, from

refusing to honor

 the Pride tradition of flying the rainbow flag over Germany’s Parliament, the Bundestag, and a larger debate over

acceptable symbols

 to

siding with Trump

 on gender essentialism. “A Germany that needs its queers dead and grants us nothing but the promise that our death will smooth the flow of genocide,” they write.


Two Prides, Separate Goals


What most of the larger outlets failed to report is the fact that CSD was not the only LGBT+ pride parade taking place in Berlin at that time. In 2021, local queers and activists, particularly those belonging to other marginalized groups, who felt like the CSD doesn’t represent their values anymore, created

Internationalist Queer Pride

 or IQP. “We fight for a world free from oppression, where sexualities, gender expressions and identities are lived freely, boldly and without fear, shame or permission,” said their 2026

manifesto

. The IQP is also known in activist circles for having a pro Palestine bloc.


Since October 7, it has been widely reported that activists expressing solidarity with the Palestinian people are coming under increased state surveillance and pressure. From the Palestine conference organized in 2024 by Udi Raz that got canceled and

led to their arrest

, to suppressive measures prohibiting protest speech in Arabic mandating that

translators …

1886 -1894 : A burning black flame

Chronological List of Anarchist Women Active in Brussels

This text is the first part of three zines on the history of anarchism in Brussels, in an effort to promote its memory both here and abroad.

It is part of the history of the international social movements, the local proletariat, the different emancipatory struggles and the revolutionary processes in Belgium. It is based on a collection of pre-existing resources, combined into a digestible, coherent narrative. Because this was just meant to be a zine, there was little research done based on primary sources (to generate new information) or particular effort paid to settling historical contradictions and debates. You’ll forgive me if you find that some information is incomplete or missing. My aim was to bring you a basic understanding of our local history, without immediately turning this into a fat book. Choices were made, certainly influenced by my stronger identification with anarcho-communism.

The following text is unfortunately very dominated by cis men. This is due to several reasons: Prevailing sexism within different anarchist movements, societal pressures keeping women and queer people out of public politics, a lack of available sources on figures less in the spotlight, the patriarchal reflexes of anarchist historiography (including my own), and the absence of archives due to political repression of anarchist, queer and feminist movements. I hope that this text will inspire new research into overlooked organisers and forgotten groups. For those interested in picking up this task, you can find a list of anarchist women active in Brussels at the end of this zine. As we live in a time of increasing hopelessness and despair, we remember the past to imagine the future. We are inspired by the revolutionary dreams and struggles that have lived, just like we will inspire new generations.

I am not sure if it is possible to give a real “definition” of anarchism. It is often said that there are just as many anarchism-s as there are anarchists. As we will see in this zine/booklet, there are many different ideological currents. Each have their own histories, even if they are often intertwined. Thus, the following explanation is my own interpretation.

The word “Anarchism” comes from the greek terms “an-arkos”, meaning the absence of power or domination. Originally used to refer to a state of chaos and lawlessness, it was appropriated by the first libertarian socialist or “anarchist” thinkers. Indeed, they had realised that the violence and suffering rife in their societies was not the result of an absence of “order” or “power”. Instead, it came forth from the structures of oppression and inequality. Domination of humans over humans (and humans over non-human nature) created inequality, hatred and suffering. title: Zone d'occupation des enfants
content:
Le dimanche 27 septembre, rejoignez-nous pour une Zone d'occupation des enfants, pour imaginer concrètement à quoi ressemblerait une société enfantiste, libérée de la domination des adultes, et s'organiser pour la faire advenir.


Les violences faites aux enfants sont partout


En juin dernier, le meurtre de Lyhanna, une enfant de 11 ans, nous a indigné·es et a renforcé notre détermination à éradiquer les violences sexistes et sexuelles, soi-disant grande cause nationale, en réalité préoccupation des seules organisations féministes. Les révélations d'inceste et de violences pédocriminelles dans cette affaire ont également rappelé la situation catastrophique des droits des enfants en France, sur laquelle les organisations enfantistes alertent depuis des années, sans réel changement politique.


Les violences contre les enfants et les adolescent·es sont pourtant bien plus répandues et ne font pas toujours les gros titres pour autant.


Des piscines crevées par la police dans les quartiers populaires en pleine canicule, à la mort au travail de lycéens et d'apprentis lors de stages professionnels, en passant par les violences au sein de l'Aide sociale à l'enfance, ou encore les enfants du Samu Social de Paris laissé·es à la rue cet été, la hausse de la mortalité infantile faute de services publics fonctionnels... La liste semble ne jamais s'arrêter.


La prison n'est pas la solution


Mettre les agresseurs en prison à perpétuité ne permet pas de réduire les violences. Donner davantage de moyens à la justice et à la police, qui protègent déjà l'ordre bourgeois, patriarcal, adultiste et raciste, non plus. Loin des appels au durcissement des peines et autres mesures répressives, nous pensons qu'il est plus qu'urgent de repenser radicalement la place des enfants dans notre société


Construire une société véritablement enfantiste


Pour cela, il faut imaginer concrètement à quoi ressemblerait une société enfantiste, libérée de la domination des adultes, et s'organiser pour la faire advenir.


C'est le projet de la

Zone d'Occupation des Enfants

 qui, le

dimanche 27 septembre sur la Place des Fêtes

, laissera le champ et l'espace libre aux enfants et aux ados, afin qu'elles et ils s'organisent, se forment (et s'amusent

 

!), loin de la violence et de l'ingérence des adultes.


Au programme :

 Assemblée générale des enfants

 Ateliers de formation et de pratique politique pour les enfants, ados et jeunes

 Des ateliers sportifs, créatifs et récréatifs

 Une cantine solidaire et un goûter

 Et un coin garderie pour les parents

title: Bienvenue en France : Lyon 2 applique la mesure raciste et empêche les étudiants étrangers de payer en trois fois
content:
Alors que depuis septembre le gouvernement a imposé par décret le dispositif Bienvenue en France, qui oblige les étudiants étrangers à payer 2 800 euros la licence et 3 900 le master pour s'inscrire à la fac, à Lyon 2 cette mesure raciste s'appliquait déjà depuis la rentrée précédente. En cette rentrée, la fac a pourtant décidé de renforcer la pression sur les étudiants étrangers, et tente coûte que coûte de leur empêcher d'intégrer l'université.


Lors du premier comité d'action contre Bienvenue en France organisé à Lyon ce vendredi, de nombreux étudiants étrangers ont en effet témoigné de la détérioration de leur situation auprès du Poing Levé. Zinedine*, étudiant algérien en master, explique que l'université lui interdit de payer son inscription de 3 900 euros en trois fois, comme la loi l'y autorise pourtant. Tandis que pour l'année 2025-2026 il a payé un tiers (1 300 euros) de son inscription et comptait sur le salaire de son job d'été pour payer la somme restante de 2 600 euros, il doit finalement débourser 6 500 euros d'un coup, comme la fac refuse le paiement en trois fois de l'inscription 2026-2027. Une situation qui le plonge dans une grande incertitude : «

 

si on m'autorise à payer en trois fois, je peux m'en sortir. Mais pour tout payer d'un coup, j'ai pas de solution

 

».


De la même façon, Ibrahim*, étudiant sénégalais doit débourser 3 900 euros alors qu'il n'a pas d'argent de côté et qu'une partie de sa famille n'habite pas en France. Son père a dû vendre un terrain au Sénégal pour qu'il puisse payer le premier acompte des droits d'inscription (1300€). Pourtant, ce n'est pas suffisant pour Lyon 2 : «

 

aujourd'hui, la fac refuse de me donner un certificat de scolarité tant que je n'ai pas payé le reste des frais. Je me suis rendu auprès des gestionnaires de scolarité qui sont bloqués pour éditer le certificat, car le comptable de la fac refuse de débloquer la situation

 

». Un choix scandaleux de l'université, qui décide délibérément de rendre la vie impossible aux étudiants étrangers.


Ce blocage administratif fait risquer à l'étudiant de perdre son statut étudiant. En effet, il explique «

 

j'ai un délai de trois mois avant que mon visa n'expire, c'est le temps laissé par la préfecture pour que je fasse toutes les démarches administratives

 

». Et évidemment «

 

sans certificat d'inscription, je ne peux ni trouver de travail, ni ouvrir un compte en banque, ni demander un logement

CROUS

 

».


Cette politique de l'université s'accompagne d'un véritable racket mis en place cet été. La fac de Lyon a en effet lancé des saisies administratives sur les comptes d'étudiants étrangers n'ayant pas pu payer l'intégralité de leurs frais d'inscripton.Un choix scandaleux de l'université Lyon 2, qui veut donner des gages au ministère en appliquant fermement le dispositif raciste Bienvenue en France, au mépris des conditions de vie des étudiants.


Alice* par exemple, a du payer les frais d'inscription pour la première fois cette année, avec tout l'argent qu'elle a gagné en travaillant cet été. Sans économies, elle est en situation de précarité financière et peine à se nourrir sans se ruiner. D'autant qu'elle vit avec une pression considérable, comme elle nous l'explique «

 

si je rate mon année à cause de ce rythme épuisant, je risque de recevoir une

OQTF

 et d'être expulsée

 

».


A Lyon, un premier comité d'action s'est réuni ce vendredi, pour organiser la mobilisation contre Bienvenue en France et le projet du gouvernement d'augmenter les frais d'inscription pour tous les étudiants. Le comité a décidé de rejoindre la date de mobilisation du 15 septembre, et participer à des actions sur les campus, en vue d'une grande journée de mobilisation le 29 septembre, au côté des pompiers et travailleurs de la fonction publique en grève. Pour construire la mobilisation, soyons nombreux dès mardi 15 septembre, à 11h30 devant le rectorat, 92 rue de Marseille (métro Jean Macé).


Un article initialement publié sur le site du Poing Levé.

title: Dutch cops have killed another black man.
content:
Dutch cops have killed another black man.

On 12 September 2026

Juan Alfredo Goeloe

and his 7-month pregnant wife were holding a baby shower in Rotterdam when Juan left by bike to retrieve his medication. On his way he was stopped by police who claimed they were looking for a bike thief. He was detained because he did not carry an ID card. Eyewitnesses report that 7 cops sat on top of Juan while he screamed for help, that he was diabetic and that he couldn’t breath. Eventually he stopped moving. He died within walking distance of the baby shower where his wife was waiting for him to cut the cake.

(source

,

source

)

Crowd funding for his family: https://www.gofundme.com/f/justice-for-alfredo-jwxjk

This is far from the first time the cops have murdered an innocent, unarmed black man. Black men, immigrants and people with mental disabilities in the Netherlands are far more likely to be murdered by cop than any other demographic. Famous examples of men of color killed by Dutch cops include Mitch Henriquez, Tommy Holten, Sammy Baker, and Jerryson Noor (15 years old).

title: Justice4Nzoy – gemeinsam gegen Rassismus und Polizei!
content:
Samstag, 12. September 2026, 14 Uhr Landesmuseum Zürich: Justice4Nzoy! Demonstration gegen Rassismus, Polizeigewalt und die Aufrüstung der Herrschenden.


Roger Nzoy Wilhelm wurde am 30. August 2021 von einem Polizisten erschossen. Sein Tod ist kein Einzelfall. Bei Polizeieinsätzen allein im Kanton Waadt wurden in den letzten Jahren auch Lamin Fatty, Hervé Mandundu, Mike Ben Peter, Michael Kenechukwu Ekemezie, die 14-jährige Camila und der 17-jährige Marvin getötet.


Rassistische Polizeigewalt hat System: Sie beginnt bei den Polizeischikanen, denen People of Color täglich ausgesetzt sind, und endet immer wieder bei tödlicher Gewalt. Der Kampf für Gerechtigkeit für Nzoy ist deshalb auch ein Kampf gegen alle Formen des staatlichen Rassismus.


Die diesjährige Demonstration steht im Zeichen der Militarisierung. Rassistische Polizeigewalt und die aktuelle Aufrüstung der Herrschenden gehören zusammen. So beruht der Kapitalismus auf der Ausbeutung von Ressourcen und Arbeitskraft – hier und besonders gewaltsam im globalen Süden. Für diese Ausbeutung benötigt er rassistische Gewalt, die von kolonialer Dominanz über die globale Ausbeutung bis zum hochgerüsteten Migrationsregime reicht. Der Genozid in Palästina zeigt aktuell, welche Brutalität die imperialistische Dynamik des Kapitalismus entfesseln kann.


In Europa schreitet die Militarisierung voran. In der kapitalistischen Krise verschärfen sich die gesellschaftlichen Widersprüche und der Staat setzt zur Sicherung seiner Interessen vermehrt auf militärische Gewalt: Kriege gegen aussen und Repression gegen innen. Rassismus ist dabei ein wichtiges Machtmittel. Zur Klassengesellschaft gehören nicht nur die Widersprüche zwischen herrschender und arbeitender Klasse, sondern auch rassistische Spaltungen innerhalb der ausgebeuteten Klasse. People of Color werden systematisch in prekäre Arbeitsverhältnisse gedrängt. Antimuslimischer Rassismus normalisiert den Genozid in Gaza und die Repression gegen die Palästina-Solidarität. Polizeigewalt setzt die Klassenherrschaft durch und wird dabei von rassistischer Ideologie gestützt.


Doch dieser Unterdrückung steht eine reiche Geschichte des Widerstands entgegen. In Europa reicht sie von migrantischem Widerstand an den Grenzen und in den Knästen bis zu Kämpfen gegen Polizeibrutalität wie der Kampagne für Oury Jalloh. In den USA verbinden sich die Erfahrungen der Black Panthers, der Black-Lives-Matter-Bewegung und des Widerstands gegen ICE. In all diesen Kämpfen zeigt sich die zentrale Bedeutung der Community-Arbeit: der Organisierung in den Quartieren und dem Aufbau solidarischer Strukturen. Von diesen Erfahrungen können wir lernen. Das beste Mittel gegen rassistische Gewalt ist Klassenkampf – von unten nach oben! Die Kampagne Justice4Nzoy greift diese Praxis auf, wenn sie sich im Kreis 4 und darüber hinaus vernetzt.


Organisieren wir antirassistische Solidarität in den Quartieren und Betrieben! Wehren wir uns, wenn unsere Angehörigen, Nachbar:innen, Freund:innen und Arbeitskolleg:innen von Polizei und Migrationsämtern bedroht, erniedrigt und angegriffen werden!

author: Politisches Cafe in der K9
title: 50 Jahre Rock against Racism im Rückblick
content:
in der K9, Kinzigstraße 9 (Hinterhaus),


Berlin Friedrichshain, (Nähe U-Bahnhof Samariterstrasse)


Mittwoch, 16.09.2026, 19.30 Uhr


Runde Jahrestage werden ja eigentlich gern zur Identitätsvergewisserung genutzt. Etwas mag es da schon überraschen, dass es im Fall von 50 Jahre Punk, so der Eindruck nicht täuscht, doch eher ruhig geblieben ist. Sicher, auf arte und anderswo wird die für die Subkultur charakteristische rebellische Haltung abgefeiert und die üblichen Verdächtigen verlegen auf die musikalische Dimension fokussierte Erinnerungsliteratur. Blass bleiben hingegen die gesellschaftlichen Kontexte von Punk. Wir laden, mit dem bekannten Hintergrundbild des alten Clash-Promovideos zu ‚White Riot‘ aus dem Jahr 1976 im Hinterkopf, das randalierende Polizisten während des Notting Hill Carnivals im August 1976 zeigt, zu zwei kleinen Ausflügen in die ‚Kulissen‘.


Abend 1: White Riot? ‚Rock against Racism‘ im Rückblick


Who Shot the Sheriff? (Alan Miles, UK 2005, 66‘, OF)


Punk konstituierte sich im Moment einer tiefgreifenden Krise des fordistischen fixes in Großbritannien, in deren Rahmen erstmals in Europa, wenn wir von Italien mal absehen, rassistische und neofaschistische Kräfte wie die National Front bedrohlich an Raum in Politik, aber auch in Popular- und Jugendkultur zu gewinnen schienen. Hiergegen formierte sich ab Herbst 1976 von London ausgehend mit ‚Rock against Racism‘ eine Kampagne, die den Kampf auf dem Feld von Musik und (Jugend)Kultur selbst aufzunehmen trachtete und von Stuart Hall in seinem ersten Thatcherismus-Aufsatz „The Great Moving Right Show“ bereits 1979 als „one of the timeliest and best constructed of cultural interventions, repaying serious and extended analysis“ eingeschätzt wurde.


Alan Miles, im Hauptberuf bei der Londoner Feuerwehr beschäftigt, rekonstruierte die Geschichte der „Rock against Racism“- Kampagne der Jahre 1976/81 rückblickend im Moment ihrer Neuauflage unter dem Motto ‚Love Music Hate Racism‘ (2002) von ihrer Londoner Zentrale aus und mit Fokus auf die musikalische Dimension der Geschichte.


Zwar wurde die Kampagne in der BRD 1979/80 unter dem Motto ‚Rock gegen rechts‘ aufgegriffen, doch entwickelten sich diese Mobilisierungen in andere Richtungen; die wenigen deutschsprachigen Reflexionen zu RaR führen, von einem neueren Aufsatz von Gerd-Rainer Horn mal abgesehen, dementsprechend eher auf Abwege. Werfen wir also einen ersten Blick auf den Film (und vielleicht noch etwas Kleinkram) und schauen, was es mit RAR auf sich hatte, inwieweit die Geschichte noch relevant ist, was vielleicht davon gelernt werden könnte und ob es sich lohnen könnte, die Thematik zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt evt. noch einmal zu vertiefen.


(Beachtet bitte: Film in Englisch ohne Untertitel).

author: Chris Walker
title: Vance Invokes Racist Tropes as GOP Convention Speakers Stoke Fear and Loyalty
content:
“This is what has become the norm in our politics,” one Democratic candidate said in reaction to the GOP event.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The second night of the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, Texas, this week featured racist remarks from speakers and a call for violence against Democrats from an audience member — before concluding with President Donald Trump demanding a loyalty oath from viewers.

At one point, while arguing why voters should back Republicans in the midterms, Vice President JD Vance objected to the GOP being described as racist. While attempting to refute that idea, Vance invoked several racist tropes about immigrants.

“We were tired of being called ‘racist’ for noticing that our country was becoming dirtier, and poor, and less safe, and less prosperous,” Vance said.

Texas Sen. Ted Cruz used his speech to vilify specific Democratic figures, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and others.

Cruz complained that Mamdani “wants to seize the means of production,” a reference to his democratic socialist beliefs. Cruz also made bigoted remarks about El-Sayed, baselessly suggesting that El-Sayed’s past comments on his own personal religious views mean that he has an “obligation to Sharia Law.”

During those comments, a member of the audience shouted out that both Mamdani and El-Sayed “should be shot.” Despite brief pauses in his speech affording him the opportunity, Cruz did not object to that person’s calls for political violence.

In an appearance on CNN Thursday evening, El-Sayed condemned the senator’s refusal to rebut those interjections.

“This is what has become the norm in our politics,” El-Sayed said, adding that politicians like Cruz should “learn to disagree agreeably.”

The event concluded with a speech from President Donald Trump, who urged audience members and television viewers to pledge their loyalty to him.

“Please raise your right hand,” Trump said. “I pledge to the greatest president in the history of the United States that loves us so much he can’t even breathe that I will go out with my family, my friends, I will do it any way — I don’t care if I’m registered or not, I’m going to try and cheat like hell…to vote on November 3.”

Trump also issued an existential warning to his followers. “You know what happens if you don’t vote, you go to hell, you know that, okay?” the president said.

The do-or-die commentaries from Republican speakers at their unprecedented midterm convention is perhaps demonstrative of their desperation in the final two months before voters go to the polls. Indeed, polling over the summer has consistently shown that Democrats are likely to win control of the House of Representatives, with the Senate in toss-up status, despite the fact that this year’s races featured contests that, traditionally, have favored Republicans.

According to an aggregate of polling data compiled by FiftyPlusOne, 49.9 percent of voters say they plan to vote for the Democratic option on their ballots, while only 43.5 percent say they will back the Republican choice.

El orginal, en catalán

 En Manresa hay violencias que debemos combatir y transformar, aunque sea una ciudad segura.

Del mismo modo que confrontamos la violencia institucional, tampoco podemos ni queremos aceptar que haya personas que son víctimas directas de violencias en nuestra ciudad.

title: Uygur: We are prepared to bear our pain for peace
content:
Families who were unable for years to commemorate their children and siblings lost in the Kurdish Freedom Struggle because of intense state repression are now remembering them at condolence gatherings held across Kurdistan and Turkey. At commemorations organised in Istanbul under the leadership of the Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture for Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilisations (MEBYA-DER), the tears shed and laments sung by mothers are as heartbreaking as the life stories left behind by the guerrillas. At a condolence gathering in Gülsuyu, Maltepe, photographs of three siblings from the Uygur family stood side by side. Ali Uygur spoke to ANF about his siblings Yaşar, Yadigar and Abdulkadir Uygur, who were martyred at different times and in different places.


He could not accept the racist abuse and torture during an ID check


Ali Uygur said his older brother Yaşar was the first member of the family to join the Kurdish Freedom Movement. Explaining that the family comes from the village of Barman in Savur (Stewrê), Mardin (Mêrdîn), Uygur said: “Our family first became acquainted with the movement through my brother. After finishing high school, he was preparing to study mechanical engineering, but financial difficulties forced him to go to Istanbul to work. During an identity check there, police officers saw that he was registered in Mardin and subjected him to racist insults and torture. Unable to accept this racist attack, my brother joined the movement in 1991. He was only 19 at the time. He crossed from the Serhed region into Xakurkê. His achievements within the guerrilla forces led to him becoming a platoon commander. In 1997, during a withdrawal in Xakurkê, an operation was launched in the area where they were positioned. That day, he and 24 comrades held Lêlikan Hill, a strategic position, until the guerrilla force had withdrawn. They were eventually ordered to withdraw as well. To save his 24 comrades during the retreat, my brother stayed behind until the very end and found himself alone, surrounded by KDP peshmerga forces and Turkish soldiers. He fought there until his last bullet and, rather than be captured alive, detonated the explosive he was carrying and was martyred.”


My sister Yadigar was either tortured to death or died from blood loss


Uygur said that after his brother Yaşar, his sister Yadigar became a target of the state: “In 1994, comrade Şoreş was followed while coming to our home in Mardin, and special operations forces and plainclothes police raided the house. I was six years old at the time. Şoreş resisted during the raid and was martyred there, while my sister was wounded. Uygur said: “The special operations officers stripped her naked, wrapped her in a blanket that had been bought for her dowry and put her in an armoured vehicle. My sister was alive when they put her inside because her hand was moving. But we were later informed that she had died. She was either tortured to death or died from blood loss. I believe the plainclothes officers who came to the house with the special operations forces were members of the Gendarmerie Intelligence and Counter-Terrorism (JITEM), because the same team had previously raided homes in Kızıltepe, Mardin, and devastated families like ours.”


They buried her with comrade Şoreş without performing any religious rites


Uygur said: “At first, we could not locate my sister’s grave. We later learned that she had been buried together with her comrade Şoreş in the cemetery where Mehmet Sincar, the murdered Mardin MP for the Democracy Party (DEP), was buried, without any religious rites being performed. They dug the ground with an excavator and placed both of them in the same grave. They are still buried together in that cemetery.”


My 14-year-old brother Kadir was tortured for two months, my mother gave birth in custody


Uygur said that on the day his wounded sister was taken away in an armoured vehicle, his brother Abdülkadir, who was only 14 at the time, and his pregnant mother were also detained and subjected to torture. He noted that his younger sister was born while their mother was in custody. His mother was released after giving birth, while his brother Kadir Uygur, still a child, was subjected to severe torture. author: Ibrahim Hirsi
title: Minnesotans Aren’t Going to Let “Operation Metro Surge” Be Forgotten
content:
Documentation projects are capturing the brutality of the ICE crackdown and the grassroots resistance that followed.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Sabrina Rucker wasn’t just focused on protecting her immigrant neighbors and coordinating with activists in grassroots response networks during “Operation Metro Surge,” the aggressive federal immigration crackdown that rocked Minnesota this past winter.

Rucker, co-founder and CEO of a local publishing company, StoryForge, conceived the idea to document the crackdown after she tried — to no avail — to get a cousin to understand its intensity in the suburbs, especially in her affluent Apple Valley home, about 20 miles south of Minneapolis. Then it hit her: If her cousin couldn’t grasp what was happening, others probably couldn’t either. So in February, during the peak of the surge, Rucker started the Metro Surge Anthology, a project that documents stories from impacted individuals and families in immigrant and non-immigrant communities.

“Personal stories have the power to reach people in a way that big, flashy news stories don’t,” she told Truthout. “My hope is that compiling a bunch of real people and their experiences in one place will be more compelling to sharing what the reality of Operation Metro Surge was like to a broader audience who really didn’t understand. Having an accurate picture of what it was like is really important.”

Today, she’s hardly alone. State officials, nonprofit groups, and independent oral historians are also recording experiences from Operation Metro Surge and the related but little-known Operation Post-Admission Refugee Reverification and Integrity Strengthening (PARRIS), which targeted about 5,600 refugees in Minnesota. While their motives vary, these projects share one goal: to capture both the brutality of the crackdown and the grassroots resistance that emerged in response.

Llana Barber, a history professor and director of the Immigration History Research Center at the University of Minnesota, has collaborated with some of those documenting the experiences. She says these initiatives aren’t just crucial archival records for future researchers; they also inform ongoing political and grassroots work nationwide.

“The immense outpouring of community care and mutual responsibility that happened during the surge — to me, it’s really important to document that for what it was and not let it get misread or misrepresented as something nefarious,” she told Truthout. “It was such an inspiring community response: the way that people developed all of these elaborate networks to take care of their neighbors, make sure that their rent was paid, that they had food to eat, that their kids were safe going to school, and that schools were open — all of the ways in which communities came together to protect one another was one of the most powerful things I’ve ever seen in my life. And making sure that the truth of that gets recorded and that the power of that gets recorded is why these documenting projects are so important.”

The Minnesota state government is leading the largest effort to collect stories about the crackdown. In the spring, Gov. Tim Walz signed an executive order establishing the Governor’s Council on Recording the Truth of Operation Metro Surge and Operation PARRIS on Minnesotans, or the Minnesota Truth Council, to create a comprehensive public record. This includes gathering oral histories, testimonies, and documents from affected residents and state agents. The council will then produce a final report with recommendations to prevent similar federal abuse and violations in the future.

“Minnesotans know what happened in their communities, but too many stories have yet to be heard, documented, and shared,” Walz stated in a press release. “For months, families lived in fear, children were separated from their parents, and our neighbors were subjected to racial profiling and unlawful detentions. At the same time, people showed up for one another with compassion, courage, and resilience. This council will make sure we document Minnesota’s history.”

“Being able to document what our truth is — our individual or collective truth — is really an important part of both knowing what happened and being able to prevent its recurrence … and of healing as a community.”

author: Giulia Messmer
title: Sea-Watch gewinnt vor Gericht: Festsetzung der Sea-Watch 5 in Neapel aufgehoben
content:
Neapel, Italien: Das Gericht in Neapel hat die 45-tägige Festsetzung der Sea-Watch 5 und das Bußgeld in Höhe von 7.500 Euro aufgehoben. Die Sanktionen waren mit dem Vorwurf verhängt worden, Sea-Watch habe während eines Rettungseinsatzes im August nicht mit den libyschen Behörden kommuniziert. Sea-Watch hält das Vorgehen für unrechtmäßig und legte dagegen Klage ein. In einer vorläufigen Entscheidung folgte das Gericht der Argumentation von Sea-Watch und hob sowohl die Festsetzung als auch das Bußgeld auf. Die Sea-Watch 5 kann nun wieder auslaufen, um Rettungseinsätze durchzuführen.

Die Sanktionen gegen Sea-Watch wurden verhängt im Anschluss an einen Rettungseinsatz am 13. August, bei dem die Crew der Sea-Watch 5 sechs Menschen in internationalen Gewässern aus dem Wasser rettete. Nachdem die italienischen Behörden das Schiff angewiesen hatten, den weit entfernten Hafen von Neapel anzulaufen, wurde der Crew bei ihrer Ankunft vorgeworfen, die libyschen Behörden nicht über die Rettung informiert zu haben. Daraufhin wurde das Schiff festgesetzt.

Sea-Watch begrüßt die Entscheidung des Gerichts als jüngsten Erfolg in einer Reihe erfolgreicher rechtlicher Schritte gegen Blockaden ziviler Seenotrettungsschiffe auf Grundlage des sogenannten Piantedosi-Dekrets. Dieses verpflichtet Rettungscrews, den Anweisungen der italienischen Behörden Folge zu leisten, während Rettungseinsätzen mit der sogenannten libyschen Küstenwache zu kommunizieren. Sea-Watch ist Teil der Justice Fleet, eines Bündnisses ziviler Seenotrettungsorganisationen, das die Zusammenarbeit mit libyschen Akteuren, die in schwere Menschenrechtsverletzungen involviert sind, kategorisch ablehnt.

Sea-Watch-Sprecherin Julia Winkler erklärt:

„Diese Entscheidung bringt ein Gesetz ins Wanken, das von Anfang an illegitim war. Libyen ist kein sicherer Ort. Die sogenannte libysche Küstenwache ist Teil der Gewalt, vor der Menschen fliehen – und kein legitimer Akteur der Seenotrettung. Die Zusammenarbeit der EU mit Libyen zur Externalisierung von Migrationsabwehr ist ein Verbrechen gegen die Menschenrechte. Punkt.“

Juristische Erfolge können verlorene Rettungszeit nicht zurückbringen. Seit 2023 haben die italienischen Behörden zivile Rettungsschiffe mehr als 40 Mal festgesetzt und ihnen damit insgesamt mehr als 900 Einsatztage genommen. Die Festsetzung der Sea-Watch 5 war allein im Jahr 2026 bereits die achte derartige Maßnahme. Bis Mitte September waren zivile Rettungsschiffe in diesem Jahr bereits mehr als 200 Tage lang daran gehindert worden, Einsätze durchzuführen.

Das sind Tage, an denen Rettungsschiffe gezwungen waren, im Hafen zu bleiben, während weiterhin Menschen auf See starben: Im Jahr 2026 sind auf den Fluchtrouten über das Mittelmeer bereits mehr als 1.700 Menschen gestorben oder werden vermisst. Seit Giorgia Meloni im Amt ist, haben mehr als 10.000 Menschen im Mittelmeer ihr Leben verloren.

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: UK Lawyers for Israel Want Doctors Without Borders Branded a Terror Group
content:
A group of pro-Israel lawyers is urging the UK government to label Doctors Without Borders a terrorist organisation over its work in Gaza. 


UK Lawyers for Israel (UKLFI) allege that the charity – which provides life-saving medical aid to people in warzones – has links to militant groups, and have called on home secretary Shabana Mahmood to proscribe the charity.


If acted on, the move would see the Nobel Peace prize-winning NGO – also known as Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) – categorised the same way as Isis in UK law. It would also make donating to or expressing support for the group a criminal offence. 


Throughout its genocide in Gaza, Israel’s military has

killed 15 MSF employees

, as well as over 1,000 other humanitarian workers,

according to the UN

. 


On Monday, MSF said Israel had bombed one of its buses, injuring one of 10 humanitarian workers on board. The bus was clearly marked as an MSF vehicle, the charity said in a statement. 


“Once again, Israeli forces have shown a blatant disregard for the safety of humanitarian and medical personnel. Nowhere is safe in Gaza. Civilians, healthcare workers and humanitarian staff must be protected,” it added.


UKLFI allege links between people working for MSF in Palestine and militant organisations. 


In a report shared with the home secretary, they note the example of Fadi Al-Wadiya, who worked as a physiotherapist with MSF and was killed in an airstrike by Israeli forces on Gaza City on 25 June 2024. In February 2026, the militant group Palestine Islamic Jihad stated that Al-Wadiya had been a member of the group. 


MSF has denied any links to militant organisations in Palestine and said it had no knowledge of Al-Wadiya participating in military activity. It added that Israeli authorities never provided accurate information to the NGO about his alleged involvement. 


The Israeli government has repeatedly claimed MSF has links with militant groups in Palestine and has looked to restrict the charity’s work within the occupied Palestinian territories, including by limiting imports of medicine and other supplies. 


Earlier this year, Israel expelled MSF’s international staff from Gaza, along with people from other NGOs, saying they had failed to provide a list of names of individuals working for the charity. 


In a piece published on

MSF’s website

 in March, Rocío Simón Martínez, a nursing manager with MSF in Gaza, said the move to expel international staff “will have catastrophic consequences for people who depend almost entirely on humanitarian assistance”.

In Isfahan kehren Sittenpatrouillen zurück, in Rasht und Mashhad werden Kontrollen verschärft. Das Regime kann den Preis des Widerspruchs erhöhen. Diese Sätze beschreiben keine politische Organisation. Sie beschreiben etwas Hartnäckigeres: eine veränderte gesellschaftliche Haltung.


Doch genau hier liegt das ungelöste Problem. Was sich unter einer gemeinsamen Losung verbinden lässt, ergibt noch keine gemeinsame Vorstellung davon, wie eine politische Ordnung nach der Islamischen Republik aussehen soll. Die Januarproteste 2026 machten das erneut deutlich. (…)

title: Gościmy, nie dzielimy !
content:
Gościmy, nie dzielimy!

 już za nami.


Spotkaliśmy się w ten weekend, 12-13 września, w Katowicach na wydarzeniu organizowanym przez

Federacja Anarchistyczna Slask

 i

No Borders Team


Przez te dwa dni rozmawialiśmy o migracji, ale w trochę inny sposób niż ten, do jakiego przyzwyczaiły nas media, zarówno te prawicowe jak i lewicowe. Wspieranie osób, które migrują, i polityczna walka o sprawiedliwość to dla środowiska anarchistycznego jak i dla ruchu antyfaszystowskiego ta sama walka. To rzeczy, które w głębi serca rozumie każdy przedstawiciel i przedstawicielka klasy pracującej. Jeśli tylko zastanowi się nad tym niezależnie od propagandowej wizji, na którą skazują nas media i politycy.


Ale po kolei.


W sobotę w świetnej, oddolnej miejscówce, jaką jest katowicki

Banhof

, odbyły się trzy spotkania. Najpierw znany śląski pisarz i historyk

Dariusz Zalega

 opowiadał o Górnym Śląsku i tutejszej mozaice, gdzie na przestrzeni lat migranci ekonomiczni z różnych zakątków Europy utworzyli społeczność zwartą i zorganizowaną. Społeczność tradycyjną – ale tradycja ta była wykuwana na bieżąco w procesach migracyjnych, industrializacji i w kontrze do zabiegów polityków kolejnych rodzących się państw o kontrolę nad tym wszystkim. Trudno o ciekawszy przykład tego, że wszystkie “tradycyjne” i “odwieczne” struktury, takie jak choćby narody, są znacznie młodsze, niż by mogło się nam wydawać.


Darek, jak zwykle, historyczne fakty przedstawiał bardzo przystępnym językiem. Charakterystyczna dla jego książek i prezentacji jest wyczuwalna pogarda dla samozwańczych autorytetów. Dla pana, plebana i policjanta. Bardzo ważna perspektywa, o której zapomniano w III RP, to to, że ludzie pracy tworzą wszystko. Kadra kierowniczo-nadzorczo-rentierska to nadbudowa, która żyje z pracy innych. Niby proste i oczywiste. Ale nieobecne we współczesnym dyskursie.


Następnie rozmawialiśmy z Komisją Pracowników i Pracownic z Ameryki Łacińskiej w Polsce (

Sindicato de Trabajadores Latinoamericanos en Polonia

).

 Pionierki i pionierzy migranckiej syndykalizacji opowiedzieli o walce z wyzyskiem, którego doświadczają w Polsce. Było to wstrząsające spotkanie dla wielu z nas, ponieważ jeszcze kilkanaście lat temu to Polacy i Polki byli tymi, którzy – migrując w poszukiwaniu pracy – byli w ten sam sposób traktowani na Zachodzie. Praca po siedemnaście godzin na dobę, koszarowanie w obozach pracy, fizyczne zastraszanie w mafijnym stylu i całkowita zależność od pracodawcy wynikająca z założenia dyskryminującego prawa, przypomniała nam polskie historie wyzysku. Skrajna prawica starająca się udawać przyjaciela klasy pracującej, czyli absolutnej większości naszego społeczeństwa, próbuje antagonizować nas z osobami migranckimi. Prawda jest jednak taka, że podział przebiega w zupełnie innym miejscu niż próbuje się nam to sprzedać. Nie deklaracje polityczne ani narodowość jest tutaj tą linią. Prawa pracownicze migrantów są gwarantem praw pracowniczych nas wszystkich. Proste i prawdziwe. Ale nieobecne we współczesnym dyskursie.


Na koniec tego dnia porozmawialiśmy z

Jacek Gemzik

, członkiem FA Kraków i

Folkowisko Festiwal

, na temat budowania relacji polsko-ukraińskich. Ludzie działający przy stowarzyszeniu to przykład oddolnego ruchu, który powstał po ataku Rosji na Ukrainę i który po raz kolejny potwierdził tezę, że najbardziej wartościowe działania rodzą się oddolnie i nie mogą być sterowane.


Niedziela była dniem na czilu.

Piknik zorganizowany w centrum Katowic był okazją do swobodnego porozmawiania o poważnych sprawach w niezobowiązującej atmosferze. Podczas tego wydarzenia zorganizowaliśmy Żywą Bibliotekę. Pewnie część z Was wie, o co chodzi. Dla tych, którzy nie mieli wcześniej doświadczenia z tą formą – jest to możliwość porozmawiania z osobami na temat ich doświadczeń i przemyśleń. Osoby nie są przypadkowe, zazwyczaj reprezentują konkretne grupy społeczne, często wykluczone. Tym razem mieliśmy okazję porozmawiać z tymi mającymi doświadczenie migracji.


Była też muzyka. I to jaka!

Na scenie przez większą część wydarzenia królował DJ Alfred – hip-hopowa legenda z Poznania, absolutny ultras, jeśli chodzi o winylowe płyty, i inspiracja dla wielu kultowych wykonawców tej sceny. Wspaniały koncert dał niezastąpiony Szela. Bardzo energetyczne, choć krótkie seciki zapodały osoby ze składu NMCP, Ini oraz DJ Lefthand.

No i

Konvalia Stowarzyszenie Międzynarodowe

 – niesamowity ukraiński chór, w tym występ trzech dziewczynek, które mimo młodego wieku …

content:

“, Αντιρατσιστικός Συντονισμός Αθήνας, στις 19.00, στο Αφρικανικό στέκι Εξαρχείων Mwasi – Hayat – Houria, Αθήνα.

Αναλυτικά:


“Η εξέγερση των μεταναστών στη Σιντική και η αλληλεγγύη μας

“


Εκδήλωση-συζήτηση για την εξέγερση και τον πολύμηνο αγώνα των μεταναστών στο στρατόπεδο συγκέντρωσης της Σιντικής, και το πώς μπορούμε να δείξουμε την έμπρακτη αλληλεγγύη μας.


[Ελληνικά/Αγγλικά]


[Greek/English]


Στις 29 Αυγούστου, μετανάστες/πρόσφυγες που κρατούνται στο κέντρο κράτησης του Σιντικής Σερρών οργάνωσαν μια μεγάλη δράση συλλογικής αντίστασης, συγκρούστηκαν με την ελληνική αστυνομία και τους φύλακες και επιχείρησαν να σπάσουν τον κλοιό και να δραπετεύσουν. Αυτή ήταν η έκτη εξέγερση μεταναστών/προσφύγων στη Σιντική από τον Νοέμβριο του 2025. Μόλις μία εβδομάδα νωρίτερα, στις 22 Αυγούστου, είχε πραγματοποιηθεί η πέμπτη εξέγερση κρατούμενων μεταναστών/προσφύγων στην ίδια δομή.


Μετά από σύγκρουση με την αστυνομία και πετροπόλεμο και αφού κόπηκε ο φράχτης, 40 άνθρωποι κατάφεραν να διαφύγουν από το κολαστήριο της Σιντικής. Τις επόμενες ημέρες πραγματοποιήθηκαν πολυάριθμες συλλήψεις, όμως 15 άνθρωποι κατάφεραν να διαφύγουν. 23 από τους συλληφθέντες καταδικάστηκαν σε ποινές φυλάκισης τουλάχιστον δύο ετών. Κατά τη διάρκεια της δίκης, η εισαγγελία αναγνώρισε τις απάνθρωπες συνθήκες που επικρατούν στη δομή ως ελαφρυντικό παράγοντα. Με άλλα λόγια, το δικαστήριο αναγνώρισε εν μέρει το δικαίωμα των ανθρώπων να αντιστέκονται στις συνθήκες βασανιστηρίου υπό τις οποίες κρατούνται επ’ αόριστον χωρίς να έχουν διαπράξει κάποιο έγκλημα, ενώ ταυτόχρονα αναπαρήγαγε το σύστημα ποινικοποίησης και μαζικής φυλάκισης μεταναστών/προσφύγων, καταδικάζοντάς τους σε φυλάκιση. Συνολικά, περισσότεροι από 50 άνθρωποι έχουν καταδικαστεί σε ποινές τουλάχιστον δύο ετών για τις διαδοχικές εξεγέρσεις στη Σιντική.


Η μερική καταστροφή του καμπ Σιντικής και οι αγώνες στα στρατόπεδα σε ολόκληρη την Ελλάδα μας δείχνουν ότι όσοι κρατούνται, απομονώνονται και καταπιέζονται μπορούν να οργανώνονται, να απαντούν και να αντιστέκονται. Ο ασυμβίβαστος αγώνας τους για την ελευθερία, που περιλαμβάνει την οργάνωση και την κινητοποίηση πέρα από εθνοτικές και πολιτικές διαχωριστικές γραμμές, τη δημιουργική παραγωγή των μέσων του αγώνα μέσα στις συνθήκες απόλυτης στέρησης και τη δράση ως ένα σώμα απέναντι σε όλες τις αντιξοότητες, θα έπρεπε να αποτελεί ένα σημαντικό πολιτικό μάθημα για το αντιρατσιστικό κίνημα στην Ελλάδα, τόσο ως προς το πολιτικό πλαίσιο των διεκδικήσεών μας όσο και ως προς τη δράση μας. Μας θυμίζουν ότι το σύστημα σύνορο-στρατόπεδο-φυλακή δεν μπορεί να μεταρρυθμιστεί, πρέπει να καταστραφεί. Είναι καιρός να ακούσουμε και να ακολουθήσουμε τις θαρραλέες πολιτικές πράξεις των μεταναστών/προσφύγων στη Σιντική και αλλού, να ενωθούμε με αυτόν τον αγώνα, να τον ενισχύσουμε και να τον διαδώσουμε.
