title: Organizzare la lotta contro la guerra sui territori: pratiche, idee e strumenti dall’esperienza del Movimento No Base
content:
Proponiamo un contributo sugli strumenti messi in campo a partire dalla lotta del

Movimento No Base

, per costruire un movimento popolare antimilitarista e per far fronte alla complessità dei territori investiti dalle infrastrutture di guerra.


Introduzione


In ogni territorio i tentacoli della guerra hanno la forma delle infrastrutture militari, delle esercitazioni, dei confini, delle servitù, degli spazi sottratti all’uso delle comunità e tutte quelle trasformazioni che, poco alla volta, fanno entrare la presenza militare nella vita quotidiana. La militarizzazione può assumere forme molto diverse e proprio per questo non è sempre visibile immediatamente: può diventare qualcosa a cui ci si abitua, fino a non riconoscerla più come un problema. Per affrontare questa complessità, un movimento contro la guerra e la militarizzazione deve poter disporre di strumenti ed attività diversi, capaci di adattarsi ai territori e alle situazioni. Informarsi, fare inchiesta, costruire relazioni, comunicare, osservare ciò che accade e organizzare iniziative sono tutte forme di azione contro la guerra. Si tratta di modi attraverso cui impariamo a conoscere sempre più in profondità i territori e a capire come la guerra li attraversa e li trasforma, ma anche come riscoprire il legame reciso con i territori stessi e le comunità che li abitano.


Per questo è importante non concentrare lo sguardo in un solo punto. La forza di un movimento può risiedere nella capacità di moltiplicare i punti di osservazione e di iniziativa, lasciando che siano i territori stessi a produrre conoscenza, relazioni e pratiche. Muoversi in molti campi significa anche riconoscere che non esiste un’unica forma di partecipazione. Questa diversità di modi è la possibilità concreta che ciascuno trovi un modo per contribuire. Scoprire e riscoprire i territori significa sottrarli alla rappresentazione della guerra come qualcosa di inevitabile e tornare a interrogarsi su chi li decide, chi li attraversa e chi ne paga i costi. Significa anche disabituarsi alla guerra, interrompere la normalizzazione della sua presenza e riaprire uno spazio per immaginare territori sottratti alla logica militare.


Monitoraggio del territorio


La natura ha occhi e orecchie nel cuore dell’HUB militare


1. Breve storia del monitoraggio no base


2023.

 Abbiamo iniziato a sentire l’esigenza di fare un monitoraggio continuativo intorno all’area prevista per la costruzione della base militare nel 2023, quando abbiamo scoperto che il progetto sarebbe stato spostato a San Piero a Grado e Pontedera, non più a Coltano. È stato l’anno in cui abbiamo fatto il primo campeggio e in cui abbiamo occupato il Presidio dei “Tre Pini” per la prima volta per renderlo un punto stabile di attraversamento del movimento no base. 


2024.

 A settembre di quell’anno è stato poi confermato dal tavolo inter-istituzionale che il progetto sarebbe stato proprio a San Piero a Grado e Pontedera e di conseguenza abbiamo organizzato diverse attività fino al 2 giugno del 2024 in cui è stato inaugurato il Presidio di Pace dei “Tre Pini”. C’era l’esigenza di percorrere il territorio su cui hanno intenzione di costruire un’infrastruttura devastante, conoscerlo, ed essere sempre pronti ad interferire con le movimentazioni belliche. Questo ha tutta una serie di specificità nel momento in cui ci troviamo davanti a delle reti che ci sono già, in un territorio già militarizzato. La sfida era di essere lì, di vedere cosa succedeva, di starci e di capire anche in che modalità quel Parco possa cambiare di fatto: perché a 50 m dalle reti militari c’è il Parco, ma questo Parco è anche dentro le reti e quindi il punto per noi è capire come tutto quel territorio può essere vissuto al di là della militarizzazione. Quindi, ciò che si fa ai “Tre Pini”, il progetto che si porta avanti sul Parco e nei Poderi lì intorno, vale in prospettiva per tutta un’area che vogliamo che sia restituita interamente alla natura. 


2024-2025.

 Tra il 2024 e il 2025 eravamo ogni settimana ai “Tre Pini” a fare lavori e passeggiate di monitoraggio, percorrendo il territorio, guardando oltre le reti per vedere se ci fossero dei cambiamenti. Era stato annunciato che i lavori sarebbero cominciati proprio a fine 2024 nonostante non vi fossero i documenti. Per tenere il passo di quello che sembrava il potenziale inizio di un cantiere, noi eravamo lì ogni settimana. Questo aveva due scopi: da una parte continuare a costruire il presidio, sistemarlo …

author: David Swanson
title: Don’t Look Away
content:
Displaced Palestinians staying in flimsy tents. Photo by Zyad Abu Mariam, courtesy of Norwegian Refugee Council.

By Kathy Kelly, World BEYOND War, September 15, 2026

Over the past two years, World BEYOND War members have been grateful to ally with a coalition called Global Solidarity for Peace in Palestine. In weekly online meetings, Palestinians living in the West Bank update our coordinating committee about their experiences amidst ongoing, U.S. provisioned Israeli genocide against Palestinians. They speak with anguish about people in the West Bank and Gaza enduring siege, hunger, disease, forcible displacement, bereavement, poisoning, contamination, and the frustrations of an Occupying force that constantly wages pogrom-style attacks.

Our Palestinian coalition members living in the West Bank long to extend a helping hand to people trapped in Gaza. They recently raised the dilemma of Gazan children who have already lost years of education. Many live in wretched tent encampments, lack adequate food and medicine, and struggle with psycho-social traumas because of having lost their loved ones.

In June of 2026, the Norwegian Refugee Council estimated that 170,000 households in Gaza, equivalent to nearly one million people, were living in tents. “Another 5,000 households sleep outdoors,” they reported, “while 52,000 households live in overcrowded shelters.” As Gazans enter the rainy and cold months of winter, they still lack emergency shelter items. They need plastic sheeting, plywood, and rope. Genocidal war and siege drive the crisis they face as the Israelis continue destroying Gazan homes and shelters and imposing restrictions which block desperately needed relief.

A Palestinian NGO, PYALARA, (Palestinian Youth Association for Leadership and Rights) suggested that our coalition could assist with practical measures to assist Gazan children who are eager to learn but who lack basic school supplies. The children are bereft of paper, pencils, pens, books, desks, and bookbags.

Recently, for UN News, an interviewer spoke with Julia Dicon, the Director of Education for UNRWA (United Nations Relief and Works Association). Dicon described what education means for Palestine refugee children and why sustained support is critical. She expressed deep respect for the many ways that Palestinians maintain capacities to educate their children, even in dire times.

The interviewer asked her to tell a story about Palestinian young people who represent courage in the face of unspeakable adversity as they continue efforts to learn and teach.

Dicon talked about two Gazan sisters, 17-year-old Tala Mousa and her 15-year-old sister, Farah Mousa, who were recently named winners of the 2026 Middle East Earth Prize. The young women regularly looked at rubble surrounding their home which Israel had bombed. They longed to rebuild, but how? Together, using their scientific knowledge, they developed a practical way to transform rubble into reusable blocks for garden beds, pavement, and partitions.

Tala and Farah represent the potential of Gazan youth to make a significant difference in their community’s lives and futures. We have an opportunity to assist Gazan youth through supporting their education, in practical ways. In doing so, we can also help build community among Palestinians living in the West Bank and those who are under siege in Gaza.

We are living in harsh, dark times. Daily, we witness Israel’s war crimes, imposing siege, pogroms, and vicious attacks that traumatize Palestinians. PYALARA, conscious of how children are suffering, encourages us not to turn away. Their guidance and testimony are indispensable.

If you select to make a recurring contribution of at least $15 per month, you may select a thank-you gift. We thank our recurring donors on our website.

author: GPT
title: Kutschpferde ohne Schutz: Vorstösse in Stadt, Kanton und Bund
content:
Anwohner:innen dokumentierten diesen Sommer in Interlaken

Kutschpferde im Dauereinsatz

: dasselbe Pferd um 14 und um 21 Uhr desselben Tages, bei 31 Grad. Das kantonale Veterinäramt erklärte zu einer Temperaturlimite, die Tierschutzgesetzgebung biete

«keine Grundlage für derartige Anordnungen»

. An dieser Lücke setzen die drei Vorstösse an.


Die

Tierschutzverordnung

 regelt, wie viel Bewegung ein Pferd mindestens braucht – nicht, wie lange es vor der Kutsche arbeiten darf. Hitzeschutz schreibt sie für Wasserbüffel, Yaks und Schweine vor, für Pferde im Geschirr fehlt jede Bestimmung. Die Motion von Nationalrätin Meret Schneider (Grüne) beauftragt den Bundesrat deshalb, die Verordnung zu ergänzen: mit einer Höchstdauer des täglichen Einsatzes und Ruhezeiten, Einsatzgrenzen bei Hitze und einem Fachkundenachweis für das gewerbliche Kutschieren.


«Die Tierschutzverordnung kennt Hitzeschutz für Wasserbüffel, Yaks und Schweine – nur für Pferde, die bei grosser Hitze Kutschen über den Asphalt ziehen, fehlt jede Regel», sagt Meret Schneider. «Diese Lücke kann der Bundesrat auf dem Verordnungsweg schliessen, ohne Gesetzesänderung.»


Wie gross die Risiken auch für Menschen sind, zeigte der

Unfall im Val Roseg

 vom 16. August: Die Bremsleistung einer Kutsche reichte nicht mehr aus, ein Pferd stürzte, das Fuhrwerk prallte gegen einen Baum. Eine 73-jährige Frau starb, zwölf Mitfahrende wurden verletzt. Wer ein Tierfuhrwerk lenkt, braucht nach Bundesrecht einzig das vollendete vierzehnte Altersjahr, eine Prüfung besteht nicht.


Im Grossen Rat verlangt Susanne Clauss (SP) mit der Interpellation «Hitzefrei für Kutschpferde?» Auskunft darüber, wie viele Pferde im Kanton Bern für gewerbliche Kutschfahrten eingesetzt werden, wie der Kanton kontrolliert und was aus den Meldungen aus der Bevölkerung wird.


«Verbindliche Regeln nehmen den sorgfältigen Betrieben nichts weg», sagt Susanne Clauss. «Sie stoppen die Betriebe, die ihr Pferd von Mittag bis Mitternacht durcharbeiten lassen.»


In der Stadt Bern fragt Tobias Sennhauser, Stadtrat von Tier im Fokus (TIF), welche Bewilligungen die Stadt für Kutschenbetriebe erteilt, welche Vorgaben für die Kutschenfahrten des städtischen Tierparks gelten und wie weit ihr Handlungsspielraum reicht – bis hin zu einem Verbot.


«Die Kutsche ist Unterhaltung auf Kosten der Tiere», sagt Tobias Sennhauser. «Wir wollen von der Stadt wissen, ob sie im 21. Jahrhundert daran festhalten will, Pferde zwischen Tram, Bussen und Menschenmengen einzuspannen.»


Andere Städte sind weiter:

Berlin

 lässt seit 2019 ab 30 Grad im Schatten keine Kutschfahrten mehr zu, Barcelona, Madrid und Málaga haben den gewerblichen Kutschenbetrieb ganz beendet.


Der Beitrag

Kutschpferde ohne Schutz: Vorstösse in Stadt, Kanton und Bund

 erschien zuerst auf

Tier im Fokus (TIF)

.

author: Animal Rising Press
title: Chris Packham Joins Woman Living In Pig Crate During 21-Day Stand Against Factory Farming
content:
Wildlife presenter and former RSPCA president Chris Packham joined Michelle Farnham inside a pig farrowing crate outside the National Gallery today, where she has been living for over a week to highlight suffering on British factory farms.

Animal Rising campaign lead Michelle Farnham is living inside the crate 24 hours a day as part of a living art installation outside the National Gallery. She does not leave the crate at any point, day or night, from 1 to 22 September. [1]

Animal Rising campaign lead Michelle Farnham is living inside the crate 24 hours a day as part of a living art installation outside the National Gallery. She does not leave the crate at any point, day or night, from 1 to 22 September. [1]

Farrowing crates are still used in approximately 92% of indoor pig production systems, confining more than 200,000 mother pigs each year [2] - but Animal Rising says the crates are just one part of a much wider problem, and is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040.

Farrowing crates are still used in approximately 92% of indoor pig production systems, confining more than 200,000 mother pigs each year [2] - but Animal Rising says the crates are just one part of a much wider problem, and is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040.

The action follows Animal Rising’s release of hidden-camera footage documenting the life of Luna, a mother pig kept in a farrowing crate on a Suffolk factory farm. Over 19,000 people have now signed a petition calling for her release to sanctuary. [3] [4]

The action follows Animal Rising’s release of hidden-camera footage documenting the life of Luna, a mother pig kept in a farrowing crate on a Suffolk factory farm. Over 19,000 people have now signed a petition calling for her release to sanctuary. [3] [4]

Chris Packham joined Michelle in the crate today (09/09/26) on her ninth consecutive day living inside behind its bars in Trafalgar Square.

Animal Rising is now calling on the government to commit to the end of factory farming by 2040, arguing the scale of suffering in intensive farming systems can no longer be ignored.

Visiting today, Chris Packham said:

Packham stepped down as president of the RSPCA in December 2024 following Animal Rising investigations into RSPCA Assured farms and slaughterhouses, saying he had seen “no meaningful change” in response to the findings. [5] [6]

Michelle Farnham has spent years examining conditions inside British animal farms. She studied Animal Management for two years and has since reviewed hundreds of hours of undercover footage recorded inside UK pig farms, working alongside veterinary and animal welfare law experts to assess conditions, including during Animal Rising’s investigations into RSPCA Assured farms and slaughterhouses.

Farrowing crates can confine mother pigs for four to five weeks at a time around giving birth and nursing their piglets, leaving them unable to turn around or take more than a step forward or back. Sows are put through this cycle repeatedly, returning to the crates with successive litters until they are eventually culled.

Animal Rising released its investigation into Luna’s life last week, after documenting her for a month on a factory farm in Suffolk. Hidden-camera footage narrated by Michelle shows Luna giving birth and nursing her piglets while confined inside a farrowing crate, unable to turn around or freely interact with her piglets. Animal Rising is calling for Luna to be released to a sanctuary home that has been offered to her, alongside its wider call for the Government to commit to ending factory farming by 2040.

Over 19,000 people have signed the petition since Luna’s story was released.

Michelle and Animal Rising spokespeople are available for interviews and comment at the crate outside the National Gallery. Please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691 to arrange.

author: webadmin
title: Convicted Huntsman ‘Bloods’ A Young Child At The Flint & Denbigh Hunt
content:
At the beginning of this year the Hunt Saboteurs Association was sent some of the most disturbing images we have seen in over sixty years of campaigning against bloodsports.


They show a young child having their face smeared with the blood of a freshly slaughtered fox by huntsman Conall McGrath, then of the Flint & Denbigh Hunt who operate in North Wales.


On receiving the images, the HSA immediately forwarded them to the police but, many months on, we are not aware of any action being taken.


Conall McGrath holds a dead fox aloft as a small child approaches. Terrier men smile behind them, one is holding a terrier.


The practice shown in the images is known as ‘blooding’. Blooding is an initiation ritual practised by hunts which ‘celebrate’ a hunter’s first successful kill. Prince Harry wrote about being ‘blooded’ after stalking a stag as a 15 year old boy.


Blooding relies on the animal being freshly killed as – obviously – the blood needs to be wet. The images show a fox whose blood is still fresh. It is inconceivable that the fox in the image is anything other than a fox killed moments earlier by the hunt.


In the first image, McGrath can be seen holding the body of the fox and encouraging the hounds to attack it as the child approaches. Behind the child stand two grinning terrier men: Rob Smith Jnr on the left, and Joe Scillario on the right, holding a terrier.


In the second image, McGrath grabs the child’s hair with one hand and smears blood on their face with the other.


The photographs are believed to have been taken on the 17th January 2026. On this same date, hounds from the hunt were filmed out of control on the busy A55, footage which we published at the time. You can watch the video sent in by an

unsuspecting motorist here

.


To protect their welfare, the HSA is concealing the identity of the child.


McGrath smears the dead fox’s blood on the child’s face


Incredibly, McGrath was convicted of illegal hunting just a few months before the images were taken, when he was a whipper-in for the

Blackmore and Sparkford Vale Hunt

. This incident made national news when the hunt were caught on camera hunting and killing a fox by North Dorset Hunt Sabs.


McGrath was one of four men convicted for his role in illegal fox hunting at Pelsham Farm in December 2023.


An HSA spokesperson commented:


“Over twenty years on from the passing of the Hunting Act, these harrowing images show continued illegal hunting and the utter determination of today’s hunters to induct a new generation of vulnerable youngsters into their sick and criminal activities.


This week we have already highlighted safeguarding concerns in relation to a private school whose ‘Games Coach’ was recently convicted of illegal hunting, whilst pupils of the school were present.These failings are a direct result of a Hunting Act that is not fit for purpose – we need much stiffer penalties to deter the likes of McGrath.


Following the recent consultation on trail hunting the government must immediately follow through on its manifesto promise and come down hard on those who break the law and hunt wildlife with packs of dogs”.


The post

Convicted Huntsman ‘Bloods’ A Young Child At The Flint & Denbigh Hunt

 appeared first on

Hunt Saboteurs Association

title: Ni mare, ni ciel, ni terre pour les canards de Carrefour
content:
Une enquête de L214 a filmé, en juillet et en août 2026, un élevage de canards de Barbarie de Sèvremoine (49) dont la viande est vendue sous la marque Carrefour Extra. Onze mille cinq cents oiseaux aquatiques y sont enfermés sur un caillebotis de plastique, sans litière, sans aucun dispositif leur permettant de plonger la tête dans l'eau. On les mutile pour qu'ils arrivent à survivre assez longtemps dans ces conditions ; Ils arrivent dans l'élevage le bec épointé. Leurs griffes sont coupées. Au ramassage, ils sont empoignés brutalement par le cou et balancés dans les caisses de transport.

Votre charte éthique fournisseurs engage pourtant chacun de vos fournisseurs à respecter les réglementations en matière de bien-être animal et à bannir les actes de cruauté envers les animaux.

Je vous demande d'écarter de vos rayons les produits de cet élevage et de tout élevage de canards conduit de la même façon. Et je vous demande de signer le Plant Protein Pact, pour réduire de moitié le nombre d'animaux tués pour vos approvisionnements d'ici 2030.

Ces images ont été filmées en juillet et en août 2026 dans un élevage de canards de Barbarie de Sèvremoine, dans le Maine-et-Loire. 11 500 oiseaux y sont enfermés dans un seul bâtiment fermé.

Les canards de Barbarie sont des oiseaux aquatiques de forêt marécageuse. Ici, ils vivent sur un caillebotis de plastique qui couvre toute la surface, sans un mètre carré de litière, avec environ 700 cm² pour chacun, à peine plus qu'une feuille A4. Pour toute eau, une pipette au-dessus d'une coupelle de quelques centimètres : rien qui permette de plonger, ne serait-ce que la tête.

Les canetons arrivent dans l'élevage le bec épointé. Ils ont aussi les griffes coupées. Les animaux ont le plumage souillé et les pattes couvertes de plaques brunes et croûteuses. Certains, pattes écartées, ne se déplacent plus par eux-mêmes. Des cadavres restent au sol parmi les vivants.

Au bout des 83 jours d'engraissement, les ramasseurs vident le bâtiment en une heure et demie. Les canards sont empoignés brutalement par le cou, plusieurs à la fois dans chaque main, puis balancés dans les caisses de transport, entassés les uns sur les autres.

Leur viande est vendue sous la marque Carrefour Extra. La comédienne Aure Atika, qui commente ces images, demande à l'enseigne d'écarter ces produits de ses rayons et de s'engager à signer le Plant Protein Pact.

author: GPT
title: Tierschutz kritisiert den Abbau der Taubenschläge
content:
Gemeinsame Medienmitteilung von Stadttauben Schweiz und Tier im Fokus (TIF)


Bern, 7. September 2026 – Die Stadt Bern muss sparen. Das bekommen nun auch die Tauben zu spüren: Von 2027 bis 2030 will der Gemeinderat beim Taubenmanagement jährlich 81’254 Franken einsparen. Betroffen ist der Tierpark Bern, der die Stadttauben im Auftrag der Stadt in mehreren Schlägen betreut. Er soll

«Teile dieses Angebots» einstellen

, wie es im Finanzplan des Gemeinderats heisst.


Der Verein Stadttauben Schweiz kritisiert diesen Abbau. «Betreute Taubenschläge sind das wirksamste Mittel, um die Zahl der Stadttauben tief und die Tiere gesund zu halten», sagt Nina Bachellerie, Präsidentin des Vereins.


Seit der Gemeinderat die Taubenkontrolle 2010 dem Tierpark Bern übertragen hat, ist die Population von über 10’000 Tieren auf rund 1’500 gesunken – betreut in acht Schlägen in der Altstadt und den Quartieren. Die Tiere werden

jährlich geimpft und tierärztlich kontrolliert

, ihr Kot fällt im Schlag an statt an Fassaden und Haltestellen: rechnerisch rund 85 Tonnen weniger pro Jahr. Das Berner Konzept gilt als «weltweit einzigartig», wie kürzlich

im «Bund» zu lesen war

 – Städte aus ganz Europa lassen sich die Praxis erklären.


Interpellation verlangt eine Bilanz


Was das Taubenmanagement kostet, ist bekannt: rund 240’000 Franken pro Jahr (Stand 2022). Was es der Stadt erspart, hat der Gemeinderat hingegen nie beziffert. Tier im Fokus (TIF) hat deshalb die Interpellation «Was leistet das Berner Taubenmanagement für die Stadt?» im Berner Stadtrat eingereicht. Sie verlangt Auskunft über die vermiedenen Reinigungs- und Instandsetzungskosten sowie über den Beitrag der Taubenschläge an den Gesundheitsschutz, den Tourismus und den Erhalt des UNESCO-Welterbes.


«Der Gemeinderat kennt die Kosten des Taubenmanagements, aber nicht seinen Nutzen», sagt Tobias Sennhauser, Stadtrat von Tier im Fokus (TIF). «Mit dem Abbau der Taubenschläge steigt das Risiko, dass die Verschmutzungen an den Fassaden wieder zunehmen.»


Der Stadtrat entscheidet in der Budgetdebatte vom 10. und 17. September über die Kürzung.


Der Beitrag

Tierschutz kritisiert den Abbau der Taubenschläge

 erschien zuerst auf

Tier im Fokus (TIF)

.

author: winter oak
title: The Blind Mirror
content:
by

Mike Driver


Humanity is trapped in the space between peace and flow: a permanent agitation. The main culprit is in front of your face right now. The blind mirror, a mirror that only reflects half of reality. The dead half. A mirror that can only present what is constructed, forced, labelled, modelled, politicised, propagandised, manufactured, verified, certified, credentialed, seductive, selective, sensationalised, tampered, re-represented, reified, reduced, separated, digitised, financialised, corporatized, sexualised, compartmentalised, decontextualised, formalised, processed, objectified, artificial, hollow, desacralized, corrupted, depraved, perverted and unfeeling.


A mirror reflecting only the past or an absent future but never now. All the time, every day. A blind mirror that only reflects half of you: the restless, tense, anxious half. The addict. What is propagandised as connection is disconnecting the contextual, grounded, present, relational, quiet, calm, loving half. The half that hosts that feeling of peace we all crave. The half that lives in the reverie of flow. 


There are two states to wish for in this life: peace and flow. The trouble is you can’t aim yourself right at them, they arise as a side effect of doing something else. Agitation on the other hand is an easy target to hit. Just turn your phone on and let the algorithm manipulate your synapses. 


So, what is peace and where do we find it? The recently deceased Wendell Berry (RIP),

pictured

, answers that question for us here:


The Peace Of Wild Things


When despair grows in me

and I wake in the night at the least sound

in fear of what my life and my children’s lives may be,

I go and lie down where the wood drake

rests in his beauty on the water, and the great heron feeds.

I come into the peace of wild things

who do not tax their lives with forethought

of grief. I come into the presence of still water.

And I feel above me the day-blind stars

waiting for their light. 

For a time, I rest in the grace of the world,

and am free.


Where do we ‘rest in the grace of the world’ today? If we were visited by particularly cultured aliens, might they consider annihilation of grace to be the purpose of our modern society? We inhabit environments where the aesthetics are relentlessly ugly and utilitarian, what the architect Chris Alexander describes as ‘these faceless things’’. Where would we go to live what Alexander called ‘the sanctified life’?


Consider the difference between a library and a data centre. The library contains life, warmth, wholeness and beauty, it is connected to history and tradition, it has a quality you struggle to name. A peace you can access. The data centre on the other hand is dis-harmonious, ugly, voracious, atomised, the noise unnatural, the electronic howl of something from the depths of madness.


We’re draining the resources of the planet to build the latter while the former becomes a museum of our lost minds.


McLuhan famously said ‘the medium is the message’ – are we the medium and if so have we become the message? Have we lost ourselves? Has something removed our internal life and replaced our minds with an artificial imposter? What effect does the method of storage and accessibility of knowledge have on us? What happens if we outsource the processing of this knowledge? What is the consequence of the loss of unmediated experience? What is left?


Denise Levertov steps in to explain the problem here: 


Contraband 


The tree of knowledge was the tree of reason.

That’s why the taste of it

drove us from Eden. That fruit

was meant to be dried and milled to a fine powder

for use a pinch at a time, a condiment.

God had probably planned to tell us later

about this new pleasure.

                                  We stuffed our mouths full of it,

gorged on

but

 and

if

 and

how

 and again

but

, knowing no better.

It’s toxic in large quantities; fumes

swirled in our heads and around us

to form a dense cloud that hardened to steel,

a wall between us and God, Who was Paradise.

Not that God is unreasonable – but reason

in such excess was tyranny

and locked us into its own limits, a polished cell

reflecting our own faces. God lives

on the other side of that mirror,

but through the slit where the barrier doesn’t

quite touch ground, manages still

to squeeze in – as filtered light,

splinters of fire, a strain of music heard

then lost, then heard again.


The storage and instant …

author: Katie Surma
title: Every 3 Days an Environmental Defender Is Murdered
content:
Trump’s 2025 dismantling of the US Agency for International Development had serious implications for defenders.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Every three days someone is killed for defending nature.

In 2025, watchdog group Global Witness documented 124 such deaths worldwide, a toll researchers say is likely only a fraction of the total number because repression and armed conflict make many deaths impossible to verify.

The victims included Indigenous people, small-scale farmers and community organizers peacefully protecting forests, farmlands, waterways and other ecosystems from harm posed by companies, criminal syndicates and governments, according to the report released on Tuesday.

Mining was once again the industry most often linked to the killings. Global Witness also identified alleged links to organized crime or contract killings in more than a third of the cases.

In some regions, extractive industries and organized crime target the same territories.

That’s playing out in parts of Colombia, according to the report, which was also released in Spanish. It remained the deadliest country for environmental defenders, with 39 people killed. Nearly half were Indigenous people, and another 15 were small-scale farmers. Many of those victims were caught in conflicts over land, illegal mining and cultivation of the coca plant grown for cocaine. The report pointed to suspected links to organized crime in 17 cases and to contract killings in five more.

The epicenter of the violence was in Colombia’s biodiverse Cauca region, located near the Ecuadorian border and Pacific cocaine-trafficking routes. Coca production there has increased fivefold over the past decade, according to Global Witness, while armed groups are driving deforestation, illegal mining and the destruction of rivers.

Colombia has topped Global Witness’ rankings for several years. But researchers cautioned that the high number is in part a reflection of the nation’s relatively open society, making it easier to track and verify killings compared to more repressive countries such as China, which doesn’t appear on the list at all.

Brazil was the second-deadliest country in 2025, recording 26 killings, double the number reported the year before. All but one case stemmed from land conflicts. Researchers said half of the attacks occurred in the Amazonian states of Rondônia and Pará, where the “agricultural and extractive frontiers continue to encroach on small-scale farming communities, with illegal loggers, miners and cattle ranchers driving incursions, land grabs and lethal violence.”

Brazilian officials’ failure to demarcate and recognize Indigenous land rights has also contributed to the escalating violence, researchers said.

Next on the list are the Philippines and Honduras, which each recorded 12 killings, followed by Mexico with 10, Guatemala with eight, Peru with four and Nicaragua and Ecuador with three each.

In Honduras, 10 of the defenders killed were small-scale farmers. All of those murders were linked to organized crime, while corporate interests were implicated in eight of them, according to the report.

Global Witness has tracked the killings and disappearances of environmental defenders since 2012. The 2025 figures bring the total number of killings documented since then to 2,375. That figure, too, is widely considered a vast undercount.

Environmental defenders are a subset of human rights defenders, people acting peacefully to protect fundamental freedoms and rights. Many environmental defenders resist mega-projects imposed on their communities — such as mines, dams, industrial farming, logging and oil and gas operations — without meaningful consultation or consent. Many communities’ land claims remain unrecognized or are disrespected, setting the stage for conflict.

Global Witness highlighted the case of the Indigenous Dayak peoples, who have lived for centuries in West Kalimantan, a biodiverse Indonesian region of rainforests, peatlands and mangroves. Yet, only a fraction of this area larger than New York state is formally recognized, or in the process of being recognized, as Dayak territories, according to Yetno Budi Wibowo, of Lingkaran Advokasi & Riset Borneo, a nonprofit focused on environmental and human rights issues in West Kalimantan.

author: Redazione_web
title: Stiamo freschi – Il taccuino della crisi climatica. La fisica condanna il capitale
content:
Premessa


La carenza, in primo luogo di chi scrive, di approfondite conoscenze di antropologia biologica e sociale, nonché di termodinamica, induce ad operare delle semplificazioni che, però, ben si addicono ad un articolo che non è destinato ad una pubblicazione su una rivista scientifica ma, semplicemente, si inserisce nella rubrica “Stiamo freschi” come spunto di riflessione e stimolo al confronto sulle tematiche connesse alla crisi climatica.


Prima d’iniziare, vorrei segnalare all’attenzione di chi segue questa rubrica l’opuscolo: “

CRISI CLIMATICA Critiche e prospettive da un punto di vista anarchico

”, curato da un gruppo di lavoro della Federazione Anarchica Italiana. Un documento che inquadra ed approfondisce in maniera più strutturata


il tema dei cambiamenti climatici

che, per il suo carattere globale e per le molteplici implicazioni inerenti a questioni ambientali, sociali ed economiche, non solo assume un interesse riferibile all’intero pianeta Terra, ma permette di sviluppare un’analisi che, inevitabilmente, si riferisce alla complessità della società in cui viviamo.


https://umanitanova.org/crisi-climatica-critiche-e-prospettive-da-un-punto-di-vista-anarchico/


Energia per l’Homo sapiens


Il fenomeno vita, anche nelle sue forme più semplici, gli organismi unicellulari, ha bisogno di energia per svolgere le proprie funzioni fondamentali. Le fonti da cui ricavare energia sono diverse:

 i vegetali sfruttano direttamente l’energia del sole con il processo di fotosintesi; noi umani dipendiamo dall’energia ricavata dalle sostanze nutritive prodotte da altri viventi, apparteniamo cioè alla categoria degli eterotrofi. Se la necessità di alimentarci è, in primo luogo, legata alla sopravvivenza, non possiamo dimenticare che la storia della specie Homo sapiens e della sua evoluzione non solo in termini quantitativi, come numero di individui, ma anche in termini sociali, economici e culturali è strettamente legata allo sfruttamento di diverse risorse energetiche.


Se scorriamo i passaggi più significativi del percorso del genere Homo, dando per scontata l’importanza dell’utilizzo del fuoco (a partire da 1,5 milioni di anni fa), dobbiamo di certo considerare il passaggio

 dai piccoli gruppi di raccoglitori-cacciatori, che usavano solo la propria energia muscolare per la raccolta di vegetali o per la cattura delle prede, all’uomo agricoltore-allevatore, che riesce a ricavare dal lavoro agricolo (fotosintesi controllata) e dallo sfruttamento degli animali addomesticati un surplus alimentare. Tale eccedenza

ha contribuito al primo salto, in termini di disponibilità ed accumulo di energia nella forma delle derrate alimentari. La gestione di forme aggregative più complesse, che ne derivavano, ha favorito una diversa strutturazione dei rapporti sociali, con la definizione di nuovi ruoli e funzioni con la parallela imposizione dei rapporti gerarchici. Se per millenni la fonte di energia per eccellenza è stata rappresentata dal legno, attraverso la sua combustione, e dall’utilizzo degli animali come forza lavoro che in parte sostituisce l’attività muscolare umana, dobbiamo ricordare che a partire dal XVII secolo la domanda di legname, sia per la costruzione di abitazioni, navi, ponti, sia come combustibile, sia per la produzione di carbonella, divenne così elevata da non essere più sostenibile. Dal momento in cui la richiesta superò la capacità di rigenerazione delle foreste, una fonte già conosciuta, il carbone, andò via via aumentando la propria importanza in tutto il corso del XVIII secolo. Un’altra innovazione tecnologica, l’invenzione e il perfezionamento della macchina a vapore (James Watt 1765), determinò un’ulteriore svolta permettendo di sfruttare il carbone su larghissima scala. Il carbone divenne la fonte di energia che rese possibile la prima rivoluzione industriale, con tutte le conseguenze che ben conosciamo: urbanizzazione, accelerazione dello sfruttamento delle risorse umane ed ambientali, rapido sviluppo del sistema capitalista, solo per citarne alcune.


L’inclinazione dell’umanità all’assoggettamento e alla rapina delle risorse naturali non nasce con la rivoluzione industriale né con la nascita delle prime gerarchie proto-statali.

 Homo sapiens

 tende ad ampliare la propria nicchia ecologica dissipando energia residua ogni volta che ne trova l’opportunità tecnica, ma il suo impatto diventa imponente a partire dalla rivoluzione industriale. Infatti,

title: Çözüm burjuvazinin sınırlarında değil
content:
Bu Pazartesi, ODTÜ’de COP31 Başkanlığı ve Birleşmiş Milletler Türkiye ortaklığında “Gençlik İklim Zirvesi” düzenlendi. COP31’e hazırlanan ODTÜ, daha önce de COP’lara dair bir Learn&Connect etkinliği ve METU Climate Talks Pre-COP Webinar serisi düzenlemişti. Zirvede, “gençlerin iklim alanında karar alma süreçlerine katılımı üzerine interaktif bir diyalog gerçekleştirileceği ve COP31 Eylem Gündemi’ne iletilmek üzere bir dizi öneri içeren Gençlik Bildirisi hazırlanacağı” duyuruldu.

Konferans salonunda bulunan gençlerin sayısı 20 civarındaydı (zirveye çevrimiçi katılımın da olduğunu belirtelim). Zirvenin içeriğini tartışmaya gelen ODTÜ Öğrencileri ise Rektörlük konuşması sırasında atanmış rektörün Rant Yolundaki tutumuna ve COP31’in sahici bir çözüm getiremeyeceğine dair söz aldılar. Öğrenciler, “Bir etkinlik yapılıyor ama biliyoruz ki bu etkinliği yapan rektörlük rant yoluna asfalt döküyor”, “emeğimizin, ormanımızın, madenimizin talan planının yapıldığı COP31 Zirvesini kampüsümüzde kabul etmiyoruz; sizin doğa talanınız, sizin emperyalist sömürünüz varsa bizim örgütlü mücadelemiz var”, “ODTÜ Rektörlüğü ile belediye arasındaki protokol derhal iptal edilmeli, Rant Yolunun yapımı acilen durdurulmalıdır” diyerek seslerini yükselttiler.

Gençliğin iklim tartışmalarına ve bu tür zirvelere katılımının teşvik edilmesi değerli gözüküyor. “İklim sorununun çözümü için ne yapabiliriz?” sorusunun cevabını ne kadar kalabalık ararsak, o kadar doğru bir cevaba ulaşacağımızı düşünebiliriz. Ancak önce bu soruyu hangi zeminde tartıştığımıza bakmalıyız. Çünkü işin doğa bilimleri tarafına baktığımızda, sorunun sebebini ve buna bağlı olarak nasıl çözülebileceğini aslında halihazırda biliyoruz. Hükümetlerarası İklim Değişikliği Paneli'nin (IPCC) 6. Değerlendirme Raporu'na göre, küresel ısınmayı 1,5°C'de durdurmak ve sonrasında geri çevirmek için 2030'a kadar atmosfere salınan toplam sera gazlarında %43, 2035'e kadar ise %60 net düşüş sağlanmalı. 2050'ye kadar kömür kullanımı neredeyse tamamen sonlandırılmalı, petrol kullanımı %60-90 oranında, doğal gaz kullanımı ise yarıdan fazla azaltılmalı. Metan salınımı 2030 yılına kadar en az %34 oranında azaltılmalı; bunun için tarım ve hayvancılıktan kaynaklanan emisyonlar düşürülmeli.

Yani buradaki esas tartışma, “Bu çözümleri nasıl uygulayabiliriz?” sorusunda düğümleniyor. Bu da üretimi planlayanların ve yönetenlerin alması gereken aksiyonları gündeme getiriyor. Fosil yakıtlara alternatif olarak öne çıkan sürdürülebilir enerjinin üretimi için bol miktarda nadir toprak elementi gerekiyor. Bugünkü üretimin tamamını karşılayacak sürdürülebilir enerji kaynaklarının ve bunlara ilişkin materyallerin üretimi ise yeryüzünde başka bir talan alanı açıyor. Ayrıca fosil yakıt tekellerinin pazarlarının zayıflamaması için attığı her adımı bir kenara bırakalım; fosil yakıt kullanarak üretim yapan şirketlerin sürdürülebilir enerjiye geçebilmesi için kısa ve orta vadede kârlarının bir bölümünden vazgeçmeleri gerekiyor. Bu ise kimsenin, diğer herkesin de aynı kısıntıyı uygulayacağından emin olmadan göze almadığı bir süreç.

Ancak bu çıkmazların hepsinin temeli, üretimi planlayanların ve yönetenlerin penceresinden bakmaktan geliyor. Üretim üzerinde söz sahibi olan burjuvazinin esas önceliği kendi devamlılığı ve kârı; üretim üzerinde ise topyekûn bir anarşi söz konusu. Dünyanın dört bir yanı üretim fazlasından çöplüğe dönüşmüş durumda. Yani şu anki üretimi karşılamak için gereken enerji miktarından bahsetmek bile burjuvazinin sınırlarını kabul etmek demek. Dünya halkları olarak insanca yaşanılabilir bir dünyaya ve bu dünyayı gelecek nesillere bırakabilmeye ihtiyacımız var. Bu ihtiyaç doğrultusunda hareket edebilmek için ne kadar üretmeye ihtiyacımız olduğunu, bu üretimi nasıl karşılayabileceğimizi ve hangi kaynakları nereye, nasıl yönlendirebileceğimizi tartışmamız gerekiyor. Bunu yapabilmemizin ve uygulayabilmemizin tek yolu ise üretimi planlayanların üreten yığınlar olması. Burjuvazinin sınırları içerisinde gerçekleştirilen iklim tartışmaları bizi bir sonuca ulaştıramaz; sorunu üreten sistemin içerisinde kalıcı bir çıkış yolu bulamayız. Bu yüzden gençliği bu tartışmaların etrafında bir araya getiren girişimler, bizim iklim ve çevre mücadelemizin sorularını burjuvazinin sorularına sıkıştırıyor; mücadelemizi burjuvazinin çizdiği sınırlar içine hapsediyor.

Sermayenin temsilcisi saray rejimi ile atanmış rektörünün kol kola düzenlediği iklim etkinliklerini de bu çerçeveden değerlendirmeliyiz. Rant Yoluna, ülke …

author: Monthly Review Press
title: New! Chris dePloeg’s “The Exterminating Empire”
content:
REVIEWS:


Counterpunch

, “

Capitalism is Waging War on Palestine While Creating a Burning Planet

” by Daniel Falcone:


Daniel Falcone:

What is the central argument of

The Exterminating Empire

 and how is the book structured? It looks as though the book serves as an intervention as well as an addition to current scholarship.  


Chris Kaspar de Ploeg:

 I open the book with some jarring facts that seem paradoxical at first sight. We need about 30 percent of our productive capacity to

give everyone on the planet a good life

. Not just the basics like housing, clothing and healthcare, but also modern appliances like refrigerators, laptops, access to the internet and more. At the same time, that standard of living is denied to about

80 percent of the world population

. Green energy has been cheaper than fossil fuels for years, yet climate breakdown is only accelerating. We could

solve world hunger

 with about 0.03 percent of global GDP, but hunger is only increasing.


That looks like an extraordinarily wasteful system, and it is. The point, however, is that under capitalism, these are not paradoxes at all. In fact, they are signs of capital’s success. Under our current economic system, the primary goal, ruthlessly pursued, is

profit maximization

. That profit maximization is reached through pushing down costs–and we are those costs, our labour, our environments, our lives–and by conquering markets, often through a mix of military and economic warfare. That essentially puts

capitalism on a warpath against life

. The system is working exactly as it is supposed to.


We see, for example, that profit rates are higher in the fossil fuel industry because it essentially

functions through monopolies

, despite the higher costs. We see that the military-industrial complex is growing exponentially, targeting any vestiges of resistance against

US-led global hegemony

, which globalized harsh budget cuts in social welfare, healthcare and education. These very conditions of

structural impoverishment

 then create the conditions of desperation necessary for people and countries to accept their status as sources for cheap labour, resources and land for global corporations, mostly centered in the Global North.


In the book I write about a dialectic between slavery and genocide, and between structural genocide and active genocide. A good way to understand that relationship is by going back to the

We Charge Genocide petition

, which was presented in 1951 at the United Nations by William L. Patterson, on behalf of the

Civil Rights Congress

. He estimated that, since the abolition of slavery, some 10,000 black people had been lynched, often for something as small as looking a white woman in the eyes. These lynchings were not hidden affairs, but were a

public spectacle

, for which neighbors came together, and pictures were spread on postcards across the country.


Patterson

 goes on to argue that this kind of active violence serves a deeper purpose. It was meant to intimidate the black masses to accept lower living standards, functioning as a dehumanized workforce for corporations. At the time, this led 32,000 excess deaths every year among Black Americans compared to white death rates. Patterson charges this as a ‘genocide for profit’, based on the article in the UN convention that lists “

deliberately inflicting on the group conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction

.” Combining two studies that were done since that time, I show that between 1940 and 2020 the total excess death toll of African Americans is 6 million.


Nowadays, scholars tend to call this ‘

structural genocide

’. And I argue that this is a global phenomenon under capitalism. In a sense, the active genocide in Palestine is a lynching aimed at intimidating the Global South into accepting its role as devalued lives for Western profits. The blatant, live-streamed and openly announced nature of that genocide is exactly the point, just as the lynchings of the American South were broadcast widely. It is aimed to intimidate people, because the active genocide serves the broader, structural genocide.


The histories of

genocide and slavery

 are deeply intertwined. In fact, almost every genocide in history also deployed slave labor–even in the archetypical death camp, Auschwitz – and chattel slavery also contained genocidal dynamics of cheapened lives and heightened death rates. In a sense, even in Gaza the …

author: Novara Media
title: The Next Big Shock Is Coming — Green Energy Is the Only Way Out
content:
This summer’s weather has been record breaking in all the wrong ways. Extreme heat, droughts, crop failures, wildfires and thousands of excess deaths have left experts to realise that the climate is destabilising faster than predicted. In the face of this undeniable crisis, what should be done?


Tessa Khan is the founder of Uplift – an organisation that works to challenge the fossil fuel lobby and decarbonise our energy system before it’s too late. The former human rights lawyer realised a decade ago that none of the other social questions matter, if we don’t address the climate crisis. With family in Bangladesh, a nation with 175 million people, that is set to go underwater first, she understands what is at stake better than most. She also understands that Britain is rich in renewables, and the green transition is not just a challenge, but an opportunity to fix our broken economy.


Should Britain drill for more oil in the North Sea, or is this a distraction planted by the fossil fuel lobby? Should the energy system in Britain be nationalised? Are renewables also susceptible to economic shocks? What Can We Learn from the Transition from Oil to Gas? How Does the Ageing Population Impact Climate Politics? And what exactly should Andy Burnham do, on climate change?

author: David Swanson
title: The 3M Fingerprint: How Science Disproves the Pentagon’s Denial of Okinawa PFAS Pollution
content:
Carcinogenic aqueous film-forming foam at US Kadena Air Base coats the parking lot after an overhead sprinkler system in a hangar accidentally discharged on December 4, 2013.

‍ ‍


By Pat Elder,

Military Poisons

, September 13, 2026


Independent water testing around U.S. military installations in Okinawa has exposed a specific chemical signature—a 3M fingerprint—that strips away the Pentagon’s shield of plausible deniability. For years, the United States military and the Japanese central government have deflected requests from Okinawa Prefecture for on-base environmental inspections, citing a lack of causal evidence linking the bases to localized PFAS contamination. However, explosive reporting from the

Asahi Shimbun

 recently revealed that U.S. officials had privately admitted to Tokyo as early as 2023 that aqueous film-forming foam (AFFF) used at Kadena Air Base and Marine Corps Air Station Futenma was the likely source of pollution.


While governments actively concealed this admission from the public, definitive water testing from outside the base fences has cracked the case wide open, tracing the contamination directly back to legacy 3M electrochemical-fluorination chemistry.


Military Poisons’

2023 sampling

 found 28 PFAS compounds in Okinawan environmental samples, not merely PFOS and PFOA. The profile includes PFOS, PFHxS, PFDS, PFOSA, FOSAA, N-EtFOSAA, and N-MeFOSAA—compounds and related precursor materials associated with older PFOS chemistry made by electrochemical fluorination. Before 2000, 3M was the dominant global producer of the PFOS precursor chemistry used in this legacy AFFF formulation.


This profile makes the U.S. explanation of an unspecified source for PFAS contamination implausible. Coupled with the U.S. government’s reported acknowledgment that foam at Kadena and Futenma was likely responsible for PFAS contamination in the Okinawan environment, it establishes a compelling case for what Okinawa has requested for years: independent access, full sampling, and a public accounting of PFAS use, releases, and cleanup inside the bases.


Further proof – Marine Corps Air Station Futenma


142 tons of aqueous film-forming foam from Marine Corps Air Station Futenma

was buried

 at the Kurashiki industrial-waste landfill in 2014-2015. In 2023

Military Poisons tested

 the waters draining from the site and found high levels of PFAS with a distinctive 3M stamp.


The clearest legacy 3M/POSF electrochemical-fluorination (ECF) signature in this sample is the group I marked:


FOSAA — 1.2 ppt


N-EtFOSAA — 23.5 ppt


N-MeFOSAA — 23.1 ppt


PFOSA — 5.3 ppt


Note: POSF is short for perfluorooctane sulfonyl fluoride: C₈F₁₇SO₂F.


These are PFOS-related sulfonamide compounds/precursors tied to the older POSF chemistry that 3M historically dominated. Their presence together is much more meaningful than PFOS by itself.


Supporting, but not distinctive on their own: PFOS (236.5), PFHxS (102.3), PFDS (9), PFBS (81.3), and possibly PFHxSA (9.7). They fit an older ECF/PFOS-related profile.


POSF was the key chemical building block in 3M’s older PFOS chemistry. 3M used electrochemical fluorination to make POSF, then used it to manufacture PFOS and related compounds for products including older PFOS-based AFFF, Scotchgard-type treatments, paper coatings, and industrial surfactants.


In environmental samples, compounds such as PFOSA, FOSAA, N-EtFOSAA, and N-MeFOSAA point back to that larger POSF-derived chemical family. They tend to transform over time into PFOS.


So “a POSF/ECF signature” means a pattern consistent with the older 3M-style PFOS chemical family—not merely PFOS alone. The AFFF from Futenma came from 3M. The Navy/Marine Corps purchased and used massive quantities of AFFF from 3M.


Further Proof – Kadena Air Base


In May of 2024 Rachel Clark and I again joined with Okinawan activists to test waters flowing from U.S. military bases in Okinawa. We followed Ubu stream as close as we could to the point where it drains from Kadena Air Base.


The strongest observation in the Kadena sample is the PFOS + PFHxS pairing: together they are 785.5 ppt, about 60% of all detected PFAS in this sample. 3M’s older electrochemical-fluorination (ECF) – made AFFF is known for

PFOS dominance followed by PFHxS

 with smaller concentrations of  PFHpS and PFBS.


The scientific data gathered from the Ubu stream and the Kurashiki landfill acts as an unalterable forensic record. Because federal military …

title: Police Repression on Adivasis Resisting Mining in South Odisha Draw Condemnation from Citizens Forum
content:
The Odisha government’s use of police force against Adivasi communities resisting mining is intensifying. The Concerned Citizens Forum has condemned the forcible arrest of Niyamgiri Surakshya Samiti president Lada Sikaka, along with the deployment of armed police in the villages, where people have been resisting Vedanta’s Sijimali bauxite mining project.


 


Groundxero Desk


SEP 13, 2026


 


The Odisha government’s use of police force against Adivasi communities resisting mining projects on their land is intensifying. The Concerned Citizens Forum, with lawyers, human rights organizations, trade unions, citizens’ groups, and members of various political parties, has condemned the forcible arrest of Dongria Kandh leader and Niyamgiri Surakshya Samiti president Lada Sikaka by the Odisha police, along with the deployment of armed police in the villages of Kantamal and Talaampadar, where people have been resisting Vedanta’s Sijimali bauxite mining project. The Forum has demanded the immediate release of Sikaka and the withdrawal of armed forces from the villages.


 


Sikaka was reportedly intercepted near Kalyansinghpur on September 10 while returning with his lawyer and friends after securing bail in another case. He was forcibly taken away by an armed police team and, according to the Forum, moved between several locations before being produced in court late that night and sent to jail. The Forum also points to an old 9-year-old case (number 349/2017) against him which it says had been quashed by the Odisha High Court.


Niyamgiri Surakshya Samiti president Lada Sikaka


The arrest, however, is not an isolated episode. It comes amid a sustained campaign by the state- corporate nexus to criminalise Adivasi resistance to mining in South Odisha. Since Vedanta received the Sijimali mining lease in February 2023, villagers in Kashipur and Thuamul Rampur, under the leadership of Ma Mati Mali Suraksha Manch, have been resisting the mining project through peaceful and democratic means.


 


The Forum alleges that, rather than addressing their demands, the local administration with company henchmen has attempted to divide the communities and break the movement through police cases and arrests. It says at least 43 cases have been filed in three years and more than 100 Adivasis and Dalits have been jailed.


 


The Niyamgiri Suraksha Samiti, along with all peoples’ movements of South Odisha, has continuously shown solidarity and support to all these movements, appealing for a united struggle to protect Adivasi land and the hills, forests, rivers and streams.


 


Consequently, the advisor of the Niyamgiri Suraksha Samiti and the national editor of the Socialist People’s Council, Lingaraj Azad, who has been active in both Sijimali and Kutrumali, is still languishing in Bhawanipatna jail since March 25 despite securing bail in one case, while Hiramal Naik, a leading member of the Ma Mati Mali Suraksha Manch, was arrested on August 28 and denied bail after another case was brought against him.


 


For the Forum, the pattern is clear: the criminal justice system is being deployed to clear the ground for mining. As mining projects involving Vedanta, Adani and NALCO spread across the Eastern Ghats, communities defending their land, forests, water sources and cultural heritage are increasingly being treated as obstacles to “development”. The Forum warns that the arrests and police siege are intended to break resistance and facilitate the logistical infrastructure – roads, railway, etc – required for mining. The message the state-corporate nexus is sending is clear:  to raise a voice against mining companies is a crime – and that voice will be crushed.


 


The Forum demands the release of Lada Sikaka, Lingaraj Azad and Hiramal Naik, withdrawal of armed police from the villages of Kantamal and Talaampadar, and cancellation of the bauxite mining leases.


 


The full Press Statement along with the signatories is published below.

Concerned Citizens Forum Condemns Police Raids in Adivasi Villages and the Arrests of Leaders Resisting Mining Companies in South Odisha 


 


Bhubaneswar, Odisha


Date: 12 September, 2026


 


On September 10, 2026, at around 4:30 PM, Lada Sikaka, a Dongria Kandh leader of the Niyamgiri Surakshya Samiti, was returning to his village with his lawyer and six friends after securing bail in one case from Lanjigarh Court, when their vehicle was intercepted near …

author: Moataz Hagag
title: How agricultural reclamation village Al-Ray bel-Rash became beset by weapons, drugs and the informal gold trade
content:
Two armored vehicles, a police car and two small open pick-up trucks entered the Al-Ray bel-Rash village in the Edfu district in northern Aswan in the afternoon of September 5, part of a security campaign targeting the home of Abdallah al-Hugairy. 


An exchange of fire that would last around two and a half hours was about to begin.


Hugairy has repeatedly been implicated in incidents of gunfire and forcefully stealing cars, motorcycles and tuk tuks from villagers and

dahaba

(people who work in informal gold mining), according to  Ahmed al-Bagga, a farmer from the village.

 He also says Hugairy is among those accused of killing a villager about two years ago.


Bagga tells Mada Masr that Hugairy fought most of Saturday’s skirmish alone, before jumping from the roof of his house to that of a neighbor, whose livestock, “his source of livelihood,” was hit and killed by a stray bullet in the fray. Bagga says two police personnel were wounded in the uproar: the assistant investigator at the Edfu district, Mohamed Zidan, and a police conscript. News circulating about the incident recorded Zidan’s injury, without mentioning the conscript or further detailing the raid.


Despite all this, Hugairy managed to escape from the village, while security forces raided another house, killed its owner — whom Bagga describes as a drug dealer — and then withdrew from the area. 


The next day, Hugairy returned to the village, “as if nothing had happened,” Bagga says.


The eruption of violence at the beginning of the month exposes the recurring pattern that has taken root in Al-Ray bel-Rash. The village sank into deprivation in the 1990s, isolated from essential resources and services. Residents describe how these conditions gave space and air to the flourishing of informal and illicit arms and drug trades. 


Occasional security interventions and clashes, increasing over recent years, have done little to break these trades’ entrenchment. 


Instead, the volatile dynamic has deepened the isolation of both the village and its residents.


The village, whose name roughly translates to sprinkle irrigation, was established only around six decades ago as part of a state-sponsored agricultural reclamation project. One of its farmers, Shazly, describes it to Mada Masr as still “the most famous village growing tomatoes in the governorate” of Aswan.


So how has the village become a place whose name, for those in the area, is synonymous with drugs and weapons?


The beginning of the road linking the desert to the village of Al-Ray bel-Rash in northern Aswan, September 2025. Photo: Mada Masr


*

*

*


Al-Ray bel-Rash was established in 1968 as part of an agricultural reclamation project implemented by the

Upper Egypt Agricultural Company

 in Wadi al-Radisiyah.

 


When the company was

liquidated

 in 1990, the lands it had reclaimed from the desert were broken up and re-apportioned to individual farmers — the company’s former employees — at reduced prices per feddan payable with a low interest rate over a 30-year period, on condition that the employees accept their redundancy from the company and be barred from applying to government jobs in the future.


It’s here that the problems begin.

According to an agricultural administration employee speaking to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, when the

Upper Egypt company

was active, it cultivated only around 300 of the roughly 1,500 feddans that fall within the village’s official boundaries.


But when the employees became land owners, they needed to make a living from farming and accumulate money to pay off the land’s cost and the interest. So, they sought to cultivate their new plots to the fullest possible extent.


The village was not equipped to host all of this activity. Wadi Radisiyah begins at the villages of Tunab and Hasaya near the Nile, deepening eastward into the desert and passing through the villages of Bassaly, Zaqlouna, Raiya, reaching Al-Ray bel-Rash and Umm Salama before approaching the Nile again at the neighboring Adwa village.


Al-Ray bel-Rash is more or less in the middle of this stretch, furthest from a water source at either end and surrounded by desert. To reach the village, Nile waters must first make a long journey via lifting stations and canals.


The water that was sufficient for the company to cultivate roughly one-fifth of the village’s total area was no longer enough for the new owners to cultivate the entire tract.

title: Aufruf zu einem Informationstreffen über die Reise-Umarmung für die Sucher*innen,  Dezember 2026 – Januar 2027
content:
Comisión Sexta Zapatista. Mexiko.

Die Comisión Sexta Zapatista lädt Einzelpersonen, Gruppen, Colectivos, Colectivas, Bewegungen und Organisationen – Anhänger*innen der Sexta und der Erklärung für das Leben – sowie alle ehrlichen Menschen guten Herzens ein

zum Informationstreffen über die Reise einer zapatistischen Delegation nach Mexiko-Stadt, die Treffen mit den Sucher*innen und die kollektive Umarmung für diejenigen, welche Wahrheit und Gerechtigkeit für ihre Vermissten suchen.

Dieses wird am 2., 3. und 4. Oktober 2026 im CIDECI in San Cristóbal de Las Casas, Chiapas, Mexiko stattfinden – gemäß folgendem Vorschlag:

.- Ankunft am Freitag, den 2. Oktober.

.- Informationstreffen am Samstag, den 3. Oktober.

Unter Beteiligung von Personen, welche die Sucher*innen-Gruppen, die an den Treffen [in Mexiko-Stadt] teilnehmen möchten, über die Fortschritte informieren werden (Menschenrechtszentrum Fray Bartolomé de Las Casas); [die] über die Finanzen für die Reise [informieren werden] (colectivo »Llegó la Hora«); die Unterkunft und Verpflegung der zapatistischen Delegation und der Gruppen der Sucher*innen (Casa Samir Flores Soberanes); die künstlerischen Kampagnen, die durchgeführt werden, um Fonds zu sammeln; die registrierten Vorschläge zu Aktivitäten innerhalb der Landesmitte im Dezember 2026-Januar 2027 (colectivo Red Universitaria Anticapitalista – RUA); die Aktivitäten, welche verschiedene Musikgruppen, Otroas-AndEre, Stadtteile, Tänzer*innen, Universitätsleute bereits umsetzen (na klar, ohne KI); sowie die Teilnahme der Comisioń Sexta Zapatista, die die Ziele der Initial-Reise der Rundreise für das Leben, Kapitel Mexiko, präzisieren wird (Comisioń Sexta Zapatista).

.- Rückfahrt am Sonntag, den 4. Oktober.

Die Informationstreffen werden im Livestream übertragen. Da es Kosten bedeutet und wegen möglicher ökonomischer, gesundheitlicher und/oder familiärer Probleme oder wegen der Arbeit – wird empfohlen, dass nicht alle kommen, sondern dass Ihr welche schickt, die Euch die detaillierten Informationen übermitteln. Oder dass Ihr welche, die kommen werden, bittet, Euch die Information weiterzugeben sowie während der Pausen Eure Zweifel und Fragen entgegenzunehmen, um diese dann im Präsenztreffen einzubringen.

Nun, es wird ein hybrides Treffen sein: in Präsenz sowie virtuell.

Demnächst werden wir den Link für den Livestream bekanntgeben.

Es ist nicht notwendig, sich zuvor für das Präsenztreffen zu registrieren. Bei der Ankunft im CIDECI kann sich registriert werden.

Aus den Bergen des Südosten Mexikos.

Subcomandante Insurgente Moisés. Mexiko, September 2026.

title: “Voces de las artesanas”:  80 relatos audiovisuales que tejen memoria
content:
80 cápsulas (microdocumental) entretejen memoria, territorios y cosmovisión en torno al arte del witral, de la textilería Mapuche.

“Voces de las artesanas” es una serie de 80 microdocumentales diseñados para redes sociales formato Reels, que dan vida al proyecto “Artesanas textileras de Los Ríos”, impulsado durante 2026 por la Fundación Universo en 6 Colores.

Desde Valdivia, esta organización trabaja en la investigación, rescate y difusión del arte y oficio del witral (arte textil Mapuche) y las memorias, historias de vidas y saberes de mujeres Mapuche en La Araucanía, Los Ríos y Los Lagos.

Se trata de una iniciativa financiada por el Fondo Nacional de Desarrollo Cultural y de las Artes, Fondart Regional de Los Ríos, 2025, del Ministerio de las Culturas, las Artes y el Patrimonio.

Al respecto, la investigadora responsable, Paulina Olivares Ramírez, explica sobre Universo en 6 Colores: “Es la comprensión de una forma de vida que se basa en el ecosistema circundante a cada territorio que habla del arte textil Mapuche. Es hablar de botánica, historias de vida, ética del trabajo, vida social y religiosa, y de todos los rasgos culturales que revelan la profundidad y amplitud de la cosmovisión”.

En tanto, sobre la iniciativa audiovisual, menciona: “En apenas 90 segundos de video, abordamos diversas temáticas vinculadas a la experiencia de vida de las mujeres que ejercen el oficio del tejido Mapuche y toda la cadena productiva que su trabajo implica. Son relatos que hablan de sus trayectorias, técnicas, reflexiones y territorios, además del daño ecológico y problemáticas que existen en los lugares en que habitan y que afectan a su oficio.”

“Cada una de las mujeres tejedoras entrevistadas mostró sus distintos quehaceres en torno a la lana, desde productoras, agrupaciones de hilanderas y tejedoras de telar Mapuche. Uno de los grandes desafíos fue adaptar sus narrativas al formato de micro cápsulas formato Reel, por lo que tuvimos que construir guiones atractivos y ágiles, capaces de captar la atención de las audiencias y transmitir lo que hemos observado durante años de trabajo en terreno”.

Así, finalmente destaca: “Ha sido una experiencia profundamente enriquecedora, porque logramos el objetivo inicial que es visibilizar la realidad de las mujeres Mapuche, “mujeres de la tierra” a quienes admiro profundamente. Como Fundación, comprendemos que el arte textil trasciende su materialidad: es un sujeto activo que nace, se transforma y toma forma en las manos de las tejedoras. En cada pieza habita una cosmogonía viva que relata el origen del mundo, entretejida con una conciencia profunda capaz de traducir los diseños de la naturaleza en hilos que reproducen sus patrones, ritmos y saberes. Nuestro propósito es difundir este arte desde la voz de sus creadoras, visibilizando el vínculo entre la memoria comunitaria, las técnicas tradicionales y los ciclos de producción.”

Desde marzo de 2026, la campaña en línea ha consolidado una estrategia de contenido digital de alto impacto, alcanzando la publicación de más de 50 reels en Instagram y Facebook. Este hito refleja la importancia de integrar nuevos medios de difusión para ampliar el alcance del proyecto y conectar con audiencias cada vez más diversas.

Como resultado, la campaña ha superado 1,4 millones de visualizaciones, generado 20.000 interacciones (comentarios, compartidos y guardados), sumando así 2.000 nuevos seguidores/as en redes sociales y registrando 45.000 visitas al catálogo web, lo que evidencia un crecimiento sostenido en la visibilidad, el compromiso de la comunidad y el interés por los objetivos del proyecto.

El witral en la cosmovisión Mapuche

El witral se fundamenta en el kimün —el saber ancestral Mapuche— en el equilibrio del itrofilmongen —la biodiversidad— y en la mapu, la tierra y el territorio. Este conocimiento, transmitido principalmente por mujeres de generación en generación, se vincula con la identidad, cultura, cosmovisión y espiritualidad, preservando la memoria colectiva y reafirmando la profunda vinculación del Pueblo Mapuche con su entorno natural y espiritual.

Para trabajar el witral, las ngerekafe (tejedoras) siguen un proceso integral que comienza con el cuidado y la alimentación de las ufisha (ovejas), hasta llegar a la esquila. En tanto, se recolectan los elementos necesarios para el teñido, entre ellos cortezas, raíces, flores, barros, barbas de árboles y cenizas. Se utilizan asimismo cáscaras y hojas de árboles como el tineo, pillo …

author: Sachi Kitajima Mulkey
title: She governs a US territory. But she has no say in who mines its waters.
content:
Lou Leon Guerrero, the governor of Guam, learned about the government’s plan to mine her people’s waters the same way everyone else did: by reading the news.


It was November 12, and her advisor had sent her an article link — apparently, a journalist had inquired about it. She opened the page, and was stunned by what she read. The Trump administration planned to lease millions of acres of seafloor around the island to mining companies. 


“I’ll never forget the date,” Leon Guerrero said from her office overlooking Agaña Bay. “I had not heard anything about it.”


She immediately called David Apatang, the governor of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, a neighboring U.S. territory.

“We were both very upset that we didn’t get any kind of warning,” she said. Shortly after, she rang Bill Hague, an official in the Department of the Interior, an agency that handles federal relations with territorial leaders and tribal nations. 


“I know we are a U.S. territory,” Leon Guerrero recalls saying to him. “I know that you as the federal government can just come in and say, ‘I don’t care about what you guys say. We’re going to do it anyway.’” But still, she said, “I want you to know I don’t support this.” Hague reassured her, she said, that mining would never proceed without the community’s support. 


Nearly a year later, that’s exactly what’s happening. 


Read Next


American Samoa says no to deep-sea mining. The Trump administration might do it anyway.


Anita Hofschneider


The Trump administration is moving forward with plans to lease vast swaths of seafloor to mining companies. It is part of a broader push to secure critical minerals and counter China, which dominates the global supply. These resources — including copper, manganese,

nickel

, and

rare earth elements

 — are essential to military technologies and batteries.


First up are America’s Pacific island territories. In July, the Marine Minerals Administration

said

 that it would auction access to 31 million acres of the continental shelf

around American Samoa

 in mid-November. A month later, the agency

announced plans to do the same in December across

 more than 67 million acres

on either side

 of the Marianas archipelago, which includes the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands and Guam. About half of those acres

border a national marine monument

 established by President George W. Bush.


Local leaders and environmentalists staunchly oppose these plans. Recently, Earthjustice, an environmental law nonprofit, filed lawsuits against the Trump administration on behalf of conservation groups in

American Samoa

 and the

Mariana Islands

, arguing that the government does not yet know if seabed mining would harm animals that are protected by the Endangered Species Act, like whales and sea turtles.


The Marine Minerals Administration declined to comment on the ongoing litigation. Brent Lawrence, a spokesperson who responded to Grist’s questions, said that the department would continue “to closely coordinate with territorial leadership” as well as community members in American Samoa, Guam, and the Mariana Islands.


Unlike neighboring Pacific nations, which can decide for themselves whether to allow mining, Guam, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands are subject to federal decisions often made without their approval. Under international law, the Indigenous peoples of these islands have the right to free, prior, and informed consent to projects affecting their lands and waters. The Trump administration, however, says it has the authority to proceed under U.S. law.


That decision is the latest example of how the United States has for more than a century denied the residents of these islands a meaningful voice in decisions that affect them, said Adi Martínez-Román, co-director of Right to Democracy. They cannot vote for president, have no voting representation in Congress, and their right to self-determination is generally ignored, she said.


“The territories are practically invisible to the general U.S. society and to public officials,” said Martínez-Román. “It is an insidious result of the colonial framework.”


Lourdes “Lou” Aflague Leon Guerrero, governor of Guam, attends a a full committee hearing in Washington, DC, alongside other leaders of U.S. territories on June 17, 2026.​

title: Clôture de la rencontre Arts, Résistances et Rébellions au Caracol Jacinto Canek, Chiapas
content:
Après 29 jours, et avec plus d'un millier de participants venus de presque 40 pays différents, vient de s'achever la série de présentations, d'ateliers et de performances que les camarades zapatistes ont convoqués et organisés sur leur territoire. Ils nous ont annoncé la présence de 1111 zapatistes à Mexico, 20 ans après leur dernière venue, pour se tenir aux côtés des Mères et Pères cherchant sans relâche leurs proches disparus* à travers tout le pays.


Textes et photos par : Alexis & Piankov


Traduction de l'espagnol : Claudio


Après 29 jours, et avec plus d'un millier de participants venus de presque 40 pays différents, vient de s'achever la série de présentations, d'ateliers et de performances que les camarades zapatistes ont convoqués et organisés sur leur territoire. Ils nous ont annoncé la présence de 1111 zapatistes à Mexico, 20 ans après leur dernière venue, pour se tenir aux côtés des Mères et Pères cherchant sans relâche leurs proches disparus* à travers tout le pays.


Durant toute la rencontre, et jusqu'à sa clôture, ont eu lieu des performances musicales, de la poésie et de la prose, tant de la part des zapatistes eux-mêmes que des participants extérieurs. Les ateliers furent variés : impressions de sérigraphie sur t-shirt ou papier, auto-défense féminine, marches en territoire zapatiste pour explorer la biodiversité et les paysages volcaniques caractéristiques des montagnes du sud-est mexicain, entre autres.


Sur la scène centrale s'est tenue la représentation d'un groupe de jeunes zapatistes autour de la pièce «

 

Le commun et le jour d'après

 

», qui renoue avec les principes d'une vie harmonieuse entre les membres d'une communauté et la nature, à travers l'organisation. Avec une emphase sur l'abolition des violences patriarcales, de la propriété privée et des vieux travers de l'ancienne société. Se sont cultivés le partage, la solidarité et l'empathie en faveur d'une vie commune pour éliminer le système capitaliste.


Cette œuvre nous invite à réfléchir sur les jours à venir, sur la force et l'organisation que nous devons avoir pour ne pas permettre au capitalisme de ressurgir. Car nous savons que, comme une maladie, il sera latent pendant plusieurs années, à nous guetter

 

; et que sûrement les survivants qui n'auront pas commencé tout de suite à s'organiser autrement reproduiront les mêmes logiques qu'auparavant, simplement car il n'auront pas su faire autrement. Mais il nous faut etre plus fort et astucieux. D'où l'importance de réaliser de telles rencontres, qui nous permettent de continuer à nous confronter à d'autres réalités, d'échanger des connaissances et de maintenir vivant l'espoir.


En plus de la pièce et de la force d'organisation que nous ont démontrés nos camarades zapatistes lors de cette rencontre, ils nous ont laissé dans le cœur leur grande générosité et un exemple pour faire les choses différemment. Les soirées à danser, les journées radieuses avec les enfants jouant et illuminant tout sur leur passage. Des mères, des pères, et toute une communauté prenant soin collectivement les uns des autres. Femmes et hommes jouant au basket, aux échecs, échangeant des blagues avec les étrangers. Cette rencontre nous aura laissé la montagne et la pleine lune dans les bras, la nourriture, la nature, et au loin le Winikton (l'homme de pierre) observant nos pas.


Sans aucun doute, tout ceci a constitué un espace de formation à travers la culture. Des anciens combattants chantant sur la prise de San Cristobal jusqu'au jeunes poètes chantant à la liberté, les expressions artistiques ont appuyé le fait que les luttes en commun pour les communs sont des outils pour sauver ce qui nous reste d'humanité et arriver au jour d'après.


Finalement, lors de la clôture de l'évènement, le sous-commandant Moisés a insisté sur la nécessité de nous organiser chacun sur son territoire, de faire du «

 

buen vivir

 

» (du «

 

bon vivre **

 

») un art - que le système capitaliste nous a dénié -, de l'importance de partager les savoirs, de la convergence de nos actions, et surtout de la persévérance dans cette lutte qui avance lentement mais sûrement.


*Les personnes disparues au Mexique constituent un phénomène massif, en lien avec la violence du crime organisé.
