title: Osman: Kurds should pursue their struggle politically and diplomatically in the new period
content:
At a time when political balances are being reshaped in the Middle East, significant developments are also taking place in the regions where Kurds live. In Iraq, discussions are underway about the future of armed groups and the state’s role in security, while the region’s political and security balances are being reassessed. In Rojava, meanwhile, the future of the gains achieved by Kurds through years of struggle, education and language policies, and the integration process with the administration in Damascus have come to the fore. The political process underway in Turkey regarding a solution to the Kurdish issue is also bringing discussions about a new period, alongside regional developments.


Former Iraqi parliamentarian and Kurdish politician Muhsin Osman assessed the developments facing Kurds in the new period and the methods of struggle they should pursue. Addressing a range of issues, from the future of Sinjar and the gains in Rojava to the relationships Kurds have established with different states in the past and the importance of political and diplomatic struggle, Osman stressed that Kurds need to develop their own political strategy in the new period and protect the gains achieved in different areas.


Persistence on education in Kurdish in Rojava is necessary


Osman said that an important struggle has been waged for years in Rojava in the fields of education and language, describing the establishment of Kurdish as a language of instruction as one of the important gains of this struggle. Recalling that Kurds had fought for many years for the right to receive education in their own language and with their own identity, Osman stressed that the new political conditions emerging today also require a new form of struggle.


“A gain has been achieved, but this gain needs to be made permanent,” Osman said, emphasizing that recognition of Kurdish as a “national language” in the new Syria is important, but that this alone is not sufficient and Kurdish should be recognized as an official language. Osman noted that the limited inclusion of Kurdish in the educational curriculum has created a new debate regarding the education system developed in Rojava over the years, and said that the struggle must continue to protect and guarantee the gains that have been achieved.


Pointing out that this struggle now needs to be pursued not only in the field of education but also within the political and legal structure of the new Syria, Osman said that Kurds should develop political and diplomatic methods suited to the new circumstances while protecting the gains they have achieved in the past.


Osman said that Kurds had for many years been subjected to efforts to shape them around the question of “What is a Kurd, and what should a Kurd be?” and stated that education and assimilation policies had been important aspects of this struggle. Saying that the gains emerging in Rojava should not be viewed merely as the result of the struggle waged in the past, Osman stressed that securing these gains in the new period is also part of the struggle.


Warning against provocations


Osman said that developments in Rojava and the political process in Turkey affect one another, and stated that Kurds should be cautious about provocations in the new period and should not be drawn back into a period of conflict. Saying that discussions in Turkey concerning democracy and peace should be considered together with developments in Rojava, Osman stressed the importance of making use of the political space that has emerged, saying, “The struggle in the new period should be political and diplomatic.”


Osman said that Kurds need to reassess their methods of struggle in the new period, adding that it is important to make more effective use of political and diplomatic channels alongside armed struggle. Recalling that Kurds have developed relationships at different times with the United States, the Soviet Union, France, Turkey, and other regional powers, Osman said that states’ policies can change depending on circumstances and, therefore, Kurds should not shape their own policies according to the positions of other powers.


“It is necessary to correctly determine who is a friend and who is an enemy,” Osman said, adding that dialogue and negotiation are also part of the struggle. He stressed that Kurds should pursue a form of struggle suited to the conditions of the new period by making effective use of political and diplomatic channels.

title: Berwari: Kurds must develop a common will and strategy
content:
The Middle East is going through a new struggle over power and influence, placing Kurds at a critical juncture. A new wave of attacks is targeting the gains Kurds have achieved across different parts of Kurdistan, while regional balances of power are being reshaped.


Dr Kamuran Berwari spoke to ANF about developments in the region and said Kurds must build their own national policy, defence capacity and common political will rather than seeking a place within balances shaped by other powers.


There can be no disarmament without guarantees


Berwari said discussions over laying down arms and the future of the armed struggle in the process with Turkey should not be reduced solely to the question of “disarmament”. He stressed that the debate must also address how the national and political gains achieved through decades of struggle will be protected, what guarantees will safeguard them and how Kurds will defend themselves in the period ahead.


Berwari underlined the need to establish a constitutional and legal framework before any formal agreement is reached with Turkey, stressing that Kurdish interests must be guaranteed within such a framework. He said the necessary laws and regulations must be introduced, political mechanisms put into operation and a diplomatic dimension incorporated into the process, emphasising that the question of disarmament cannot be considered separately from these issues.


Berwari said the states concerned are pursuing discussions on the “disarmament” of the Kurdish Freedom Movement as part of a specific project and plan, which he said aims to eliminate Kurdish defence capabilities altogether. If this project is carried through as intended, he said, Kurds would be deprived of forces capable of defending them across Northern Kurdistan (Bakur), Southern Kurdistan (Başur), Rojava, Rojhilat (Eastern Kurdistan), Shengal and Maxmur. He stressed that the consequences would not be limited to the military sphere but would also directly affect the political position of the Kurds and the gains they have achieved.


Berwari said this strategy targets the national and political gains of the Kurdish people, adding: “There is a major plan against the Kurds. It is a plan targeting their national and political gains.”


Ending armed struggle is not the same as surrendering arms


Berwari said he is not opposed to a ceasefire, reconciliation, the pursuit of political solutions or the introduction of legal reforms, but stressed that seeking a political solution must be distinguished from Kurds relinquishing their capacity for self-defence. He noted that armed struggles in different countries have taken different forms over time and underlined the distinction between “ending the armed struggle” and “surrendering arms”. Methods of struggle may change, he said, but this should not mean completely eliminating the means through which Kurds can defend themselves.


The conditions that gave rise to the guerrilla must not be forgotten


Berwari said any discussion about the future of arms must take into account the conditions that gave rise to the guerrilla, stressing that the historical and social circumstances behind the armed struggle of the Kurdistan Freedom Movement cannot be ignored. He recalled that Kurds were deprived of freedom, the right to self-government and national rights when the guerrilla emerged, and said the armed struggle developed in an environment in which the political and social demands of Kurds living under the sovereignty of the Turkish state went unanswered. Treating the guerrilla merely as a military force, he said, would therefore mean disregarding both the circumstances in which it emerged and the decades-long struggle that followed.


Berwari said the guerrilla emerged within a broader struggle centred on the political, social and national demands of the Kurdish people, stressing that the current debate must also be approached with this historical background in mind.


Berwari pointed to decades of repression, military operations, attempts at political elimination, deception and plots involving different powers, arguing that the political and national gains achieved over the course of this struggle must be taken into account. He warned that dismantling Kurdish defence capabilities before those gains are secured would create new risks, stressing that the future of arms cannot be separated from guarantees for the political and national rights of the Kurdish people.

title: „Linke ausrotten“: Der neue ultrarechte Präsident Abelardo de la Espriella ist eine Gefahr (nicht nur) für Menschenrechte und Friedenspolitik in Kolumbien
content:
Dossier


„

Eine Gruppe von 21 internationalen Menschenrechtsorganisationen, darunter das Internationale Büro für Menschenrechte in Kolumbien (Oidahco), warnt vor der bevorstehenden Politik des ultrarechten gewählten Präsidenten Abelardo de la Espriella. Sie befürchten einen möglichen Abbau von Menschenrechten, Rückschritte bei der Umsetzung des Friedensabkommens von 2016 und der Friedenspolitik sowie eine Aushöhlung der Rechte von Frauen und LGBTIQ+-Personen. (…) Sein „Sofortplan“ sieht vor, den Einflussbereich bewaffneter Gruppen durch weitläufige Militäroperationen in den ersten 90 Tagen seiner Regierung zurückzudrängen. (…) Die unterzeichnenden Menschenrechtsnetzwerke fordern die Europäische Union und ihre Mitgliedstaaten sowie die Schweiz, Norwegen und das Vereinigte Königreich daher auf, die künftige Regierung De la Espriellas zur Einhaltung der Verpflichtungen des kolumbianischen Staates aus dem Friedensabkommen von 2016 zu bewegen

…“

Artikel von Pablo Schröder vom 26.06.2026 in amerika21

 und mehr zum Thema:


Präsident in Kolumbien stellt mit der Erlaubnis der Polizei zum Zugang zu Hochschulen die Autonomie der Universitäten infrage


„Der kolumbianische Präsident Abelardo de la Espriella hat angekündigt, dass die Polizei öffentliche Universitäten betreten darf, wenn es zu terroristischen Handlungen, Vandalismus oder Gewalt kommt. Ein entsprechender Einsatz soll auch dann legal sein, wenn nach Ansicht der Regierung entsprechende Taten vorbereitet werden. Die Maßnahme soll von einem landesweiten Protokoll begleitet werden, das friedliche Proteste von Handlungen unterscheidet, die die Regierung als gefährlich einstuft oder die öffentliche Ordnung in außergewöhnlicher Weise beeinträchtigen. (…)


Die Ankündigung hat bei den Hochschulleitungen Zweifel ausgelöst. Der Rektor der Universidad Nacional, José Ismael Peña, stellte klar, dass die Autonomie nicht bedeute, dass die Universität außerhalb des Gesetzes stehe. Wenn eine Straftat begangen werde, könne die Polizei ohne Genehmigung der Hochschulleitung eingreifen. Seine Sorge gelte vielmehr den Auswirkungen eines pauschalen Polizeieinsatzes. Ihm zufolge könnten sich diejenigen, die Gewalttaten verüben, unter Studenten mischen und die baulichen Gegebenheiten der Universitätsgelände ausnutzen. Er betonte jedoch: „Wir haben hier täglich 25.000 Menschen, und es kann kontraproduktiv sein, wenn ein Polizeipanzer auf den Campus fährt, weil dadurch viele andere Menschen verletzt werden können.“ Im Kern geht es um die Frage, was universitäre Autonomie bedeutet. Artikel 69 der kolumbianischen Verfassung erkennt sie als institutionelle Garantie an. Das bedeutet nicht, dass Universitäten außerhalb des Gesetzes stehen oder Gebiete mit Immunität sind. Öffentliche Universitäten sind Teil des Staates, unterstehen aber nicht der hierarchischen Leitung der Regierung. Ihre Autonomie soll die Unabhängigkeit von Lehre, Forschung und kritischem Denken gegenüber der politischen Macht schützen. (…)


Kolumbien hat historische Gründe, skeptisch zu sein. 1954 betrat die Polizei den Campus der Universidad Nacional. Im Rahmen des Einsatzes wurde der Student Uriel Gutiérrez Restrepo getötet. Am folgenden Tag schossen Soldaten des Batallón Colombia auf Demonstranten und töteten elf Menschen, darunter zehn Studenten. 1971 endete eine weitere Auseinandersetzung an der Universidad del Valle nach Angaben der Universität mit dem Tod von 15 Menschen. 1984 folgte auf einen Protest ein Einsatz der Sicherheitskräfte an der Universidad Nacional, der ebenfalls in einem Gewaltexzess kulminierte. Der Jurist Camilo Blanco ist der Ansicht, dass De la Espriella von der rechtlich korrekten Feststellung ausgeht, dass die Autonomie nicht über der Verfassung steht, daraus aber eine falsche Schlussfolgerung zieht. Laut Blanco „bedeutet das nicht, dass öffentliche Universitäten der freien Verfügung der Sicherheitskräfte unterliegen oder dass eine präsidiale Anordnung die verfassungsmäßigen Garantien ersetzen kann“.“


Beitrag von Sven Hanfstängl Reuss vom 16. September 2026 in amerika21

author: Ash Sarkar
title: Can’t Persuade Voters? Tom Watson’s New Palantir Job Shows You Can Just Buy Their Democracy
content:
Back in the halcyon days of Corbynism, I spent a lot of time thinking about Tom Watson. The then-deputy leader of the Labour party was

the right’s man on the inside

; either a noble fighter in service of the moderate cause, or a committed wrecker, who weaponised antisemitism allegations to 

undermine his own party

. He resigned from the post, and stepped down from the House of Commons, just one month before the 2019 general election.


What’s he been up to these days, I hear you ask? Well, six years after being elevated to the House of Lords by Keir Starmer, further congratulations are in order. Watson’s just been appointed as

Palantir’s newest senior vice-president

, working closely with Louis Mosley (grandson of Oswald, and the second-worst Mitford sister). A hero of the working man, a Labour titan, through and through.


Watson’s new job is more of a promotion than a big move: the Baron of Wyre Forest had been a member of Palantir’s advisory board since 2024. According to the company – named, reassuringly, after the evil and corrupting magic seeing stones from The Lord of the Rings – Watson’s role will be to increase the “social and economic value” of its work through public services, jobs and skills. Translation: this former minister will help grease our way to the government teat.


The assistance of an ex-Westminster big dog couldn’t come a moment too soon for Palantir. The company is facing pressure on PM Andy Burnham to cancel its £330m NHS contract, and is in a legal dispute with London mayor Sadiq Khan over his blocking of a £50m Metropolitan police AI contract. Palantir’s involvement with

US immigration enforcement

 (ICE) and work with the Israel Defence Force 

during the genocide

 has made the tech giant a flashpoint for protesters.


What’s more, polling shows that the

overwhelming majority of Brits

 are in favour of regulating AI more tightly. There’s a growing sense that AI has 

more risks than benefits

, and more than three-quarters of people cite the use of personal data without consent as a negative impact of the technology on their lives.


The task for Watson, then, is to convince the prime minister and his cabinet to ignore campaigners and voters alike, and hand over lucrative government contracts to Palantir with as little fuss as possible. If Palantir was after a man who’s had practice going to bat for morally-compromised causes, they could have chosen no better: since stepping down as an MP, Tom Watson went onto advise

Flutter Entertainment

, which owns Paddy Power, Betfair and SkyBet. Steel-trap memories may recall Watson once having been an ardent voice for betting regulation in the House of Commons.


To be fair to Watson, he’s hardly the first man through the revolving door. Nick Clegg, another former deputy prime minister, headed for the sunshine of Silicon Valley after leaving government, taking a job with Meta (then-Facebook). Ex-PM Rishi Sunak has taken roles with Anthropic and Microsoft since leaving government, and former chancellor George Osborne leapt into bed with

OpenAI

.


And hey, maybe these guys are just fabulous workers: diligent, industrious, indefatigable. Or maybe, just maybe, it’s not their character that’s valuable, so much as their contact books. The point of hiring politicians, from a tech-oligarch’s point of view, is to wear away at political resistance. Why persuade voters, when you can just buy democracy out from under them?

author: Unknown
title: CONFERENCE GESTICULEE : Qui a tué Issam ?
content:
En marge de la mobilisation nationale contre le «

 

permis de tuer

 

»


Venez découvrir cette puissante conférence gesticulée :


18 septembre 19h30 - Voix Machine, Fontenay sous Bois


19 septembre 18h30 - Centre Paris Anim Place des Fêtes


Entrée libre au chapeau - prévoir de l'espèce pour rémunérer l'artiste


Affiche : Qui a tué Issam


Accompagnant des personnes détenues et ex-détenues, j'ai été marqué par de nombreuses trajectoires de vie qui, souvent, faisaient écho au mien.


Qu'est-ce qui pousse une partie de la jeunesse vers la prison

 

? D'où vient cette violence qui tue si jeune

 

? Quelles sont les structures qui nous abîment, et que devient cette violence lorsqu'elle est retournée contre nos propres semblables

 

?


Le déclencheur a été le décès d'un jeune que je suivais, tué dans une fusillade. Il avait à peine 20 ans.


À travers un récit intime, cette conférence gesticulée ou spectacle politique plonge au cœur des violences structurelles qui façonnent les vies des jeunes dans les quartiers populaires. Marqués par la pauvreté, les déterminismes sociaux et l'absence de perspectives, beaucoup voient leurs choix réduits à néant, enfermés dans des logiques de survie, de marginalisation et de délinquances multiples. Quels rôles tiennent les institutions – école, justice, police – comme rouages d'un système qui reproduit l'inégalité et écrase les trajectoires dès l'enfance

 

? Les violences policières, loin d'être des bavures, participent d'un contrôle social bien ancré, traversé par un racisme systémique. Cette conférence gesticulée est une prise de parole pour comprendre, dénoncer, et résister.

title: Rassemblement - Dimanche DETER ! Pour la Ferme ! Pour les Terres !
content:
Le

CPTG

 - Collectif pour le triangle de Gonesse (avec le soutien des Soulèvements de la Seine - de

FNE


IDF

 -

FSU

 95 - Amis de la Terre 95 -

MNLE

 93 - de Terre de Liens) organise un rassemblement le Dimanche 27 septembre de 10 h 30 à 18 h sur le Triangle de Gonesse pour s'opposer à l'urbanisation des terres agricoles, la destruction de la seule ferme et la construction d'une cité scolaire de 2315 élèves (collège/lycée) avec internat et 20 logements de fonction - alors que le site est interdit à l'habitat permanent à cause des nuisances aériennes

 

!


Invitation au rassemblement du 27 septembre - Recto


Invitation au rassemblement du 27 septembre 2026 - Verso


Ce rassemblement est organisé par le

CPTG

 - Collectif pour le Triangle de Gonesse - et s'inscrit dans le cadre de la Saison

II

 des Soulèvements de la Seine dont il est l'Acte 3. Il est soutenu par

FNE


IDF

 - Les Amis de la Terre Val d'Oise - le

MNLE

 93 et la

FSU

 Val d'Oise ainsi que par Terre de Liens et la

CGT


IDF

.


Depuis 15 ans le

CPTG

 mène une lutte contre l'urbanisation de 670 ha des excellentes terres agricoles du Triangle de Gonesse. Après avoir fait échouer l'installation d'un méga centre commercial EuropaCity en 2019, la lutte continue contre la nouvelle

ZAC

 (Zone d'Aménagement Concerté) de 122 ha qui couperait les terres agricoles en plein milieu, avec démolition de la seule ferme existante et l'implantation en plein champ, loin des habitations, d'une cité scolaire de 2300 élèves (collège, lycée général, lycée agricole) avec un internat pour 200 élèves et l'installation de 20 logements de fonction... alors que le site est interdit à l'habitat permanent à cause des nuisances aériennes intenses

 

!


La MRAe (Autorité environnementale régionale indépendante) a donné un avis négatif à l'installation de cette cité scolaire à cet endroit. De même la Commissaire-enquêtrice, lors de l'enquête publique sur la création de cette nouvelle

ZAC

, a émis un avis négatif pour l'installation de cet établissement scolaire sur ce site... mais le Préfet du Val d'Oise, le Conseil départemental, les élu·es locaux... maintiennent ce projet scandaleux

 

!


Vouloir installer 2300 élèves dans des conditions inacceptables d'apprentissage et de conditions de vie (le bruit est reconnu comme facteur négatif tant pour les apprentissages que pour la santé) relève d'une forme de racisme environnemental : ces conditions ne choquent personne pour des élèves de l'Est du Val d'Oise, de milieux souvent défavorisés

 

!


Le

CPTG

 se bat non seulement pour la préservation des terres agricoles mais aussi pour que la Cité scolaire soit construite sur un site plus approprié : près des habitations et pas sous le bruit maximum des avions qui la survoleraient à très basse altitude puisque le site est en bout des pistes des aéroports de Roissy et du Bourget

 

!


Nous voulons le maintien de l'agriculture, le maintien de la ferme et la réorientation de la

ZAC

 en Coopérative alimentaire territoriale pour la restauration collective 100

 

% bio.


Venez participer à l'ensemble de la journée et à la chaîne humaine autour de la ferme en fin d'après-midi.


Tous les renseignements sur le tract et le site du

CPTG

 - le programme détaillé est mis à jour au fur et à mesure.


Voir sur notre site :

https://ouiauxterresdegonesse.fr/


Nous vous attendons nombreuses et nombreux pour cette action

 

! Les canicules se sont succédées cet été : il est plus que jamais important de prendre conscience de l'impérieuse nécessité de se battre pour conserver les champs : outre leur fonction nourricière, ils sont des puits de fraicheur incomparables

 

!

title: Death toll from Kobanê prison fire rises to 10
content:
Mesud Hemo Reşo, a prisoner injured during the fire at the Kobanê prison, lost his life late at night at a hospital in Aleppo where he was being treated.


Nine prisoners had lost their lives and 17 people were injured as a result of the fire that broke out in the prison on 12 September.


The nine people who lost their lives were laid to rest during a mass ceremony held in Kobanê on Saturday (14 September). The investigation launched following the fire is ongoing.

author: Unknown
title: İsrail ordusu Lübnan'ın güneyindeki beldelere saldırılar düzenledi
content:
Lübnan resmi haber ajansı NNA'nın haberinde, İsrail ordusunun, ülkenin güneyindeki Nebatiye el-Fevka, Kantara ve Talluse beldelerini hava saldırılarıyla hedef aldığı ifade edildi.

Haberde, İsrail ordusunun saatler önce de Lübnan'ın güneyindeki Ayta eş-Şaab beldesinde büyük çaplı bir patlama gerçekleştirdiği belirtildi.

Saldırılarda can kaybı ya da yaralanma olup olmadığına ilişkin bilgi verilmedi.

Lübnan Sağlık Bakanlığından yapılan açıklamaya göre, İsrail'in 2 Mart'tan bu yana Lübnan'a düzenlediği saldırılarda 4 bin 386 kişi hayatını kaybetti, 12 bin 407 kişi yaralandı.

İsrail'in 8 Ekim 2023'ten bu yana Lübnan'a yönelik saldırılarında ise toplam can kaybı 8 bin 953'e, yaralı sayısı 30 bin 643'e ulaştı.

İsrail ordusu, Lübnan'a 2 Mart'ta yoğun hava saldırıları başlatarak ülkenin güneyinde onlarca beldeyi işgal etmişti.

Lübnan hükümeti bu sürede, ülkede yerinden edilenlerin sayısının 1 milyonu aştığını açıklamıştı.

Lübnan ile İsrail arasında 17 Nisan'da yürürlüğe giren ateşkes daha sonra birkaç kez uzatılmıştı.

Washington'da İsrail ile Lübnan arasında yürütülen doğrudan müzakerelerin 5. turunun ardından ise 26 Haziran'da Lübnan ile İsrail arasında çerçeve anlaşması imzalanmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Месть строителей: что будет, если их кинуть
content:

Строительство — отрасль, где хуже всего соблюдают права работников. Здесь зачастую отсутствуют трудовые договоры, а риск получить травму и даже умереть крайне высок. Помимо этого, работая на стройке, вы с большой вероятностью столкнётесь с тем, что работодатель просто не выплатит вам ваши честно заработанные деньги. Просроченная задолженность по зарплате крупных и средних компаний в сфере строительства в России на 30 июня 2026 года составила порядка 1,5 млрд рублей. Эта сумма за год удвоилась и составляет более половины от общей задолженности по всем отраслям. title: Operasyon sonrası Beşiktaş’tan Tera hamlesi: Forma değişti
content:
Beşiktaş, UEFA Avrupa Ligi’nde Olimpik Marsilya ile oynadığı karşılaşmaya daha önce forma sırt sponsoru olan Tera’nın logosunun yer almadığı formayla çıktı.

İstanbul’da mali suçlara yönelik yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında Tera Holding’e operasyon düzenlenmiş, Tera Holding Genel Müdür Yardımcısı İbrahim Bekçi gözaltına alınmıştı. Tera Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Emre Tezmen’in de aralarında bulunduğu bazı kişiler hakkında yurt dışına çıkış yasağı tedbiri uygulanmıştı.

SPK kararı sonrası portföy şirketlerinden peş peşe açıklamalar

Beşiktaş ile Tera Yatırım Holding arasında Mayıs 2026'da 2026-2027 sezonundan itibaren geçerli olmak üzere iki yıllık forma sırt sponsorluğu anlaşması imzalanmıştı. Kulüp, ağustos ayında yapılan lansmanda anlaşmanın futbol ve erkek basketbol takımını kapsadığını duyurmuştu.

Ancak siyah-beyazlı takımın Avrupa Ligi’nde Marsilya ile oynadığı karşılaşmada formanın sırt bölümünde Tera logosunun bulunmadığı görüldü.

Tera Holding’e yönelik operasyonun ardından gelen bu değişiklik dikkat çekerken, Beşiktaş’ın Tera ile sponsorluk ilişkisinin sona erip ermediğine ilişkin kulüp tarafından ayrıca bir açıklama yapılmadı.

Tera Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Emre Tezmen ise operasyon öncesinde yaptığı açıklamada, şirketin yaşanan süreci “geçici bir likidite sıkıntısı” olarak değerlendirdiğini belirtmişti.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Kilikvak Kabloona joins National Council for Reconciliation
content:
A former CEO of Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. has been named to the group responsible for monitoring whether Canada is meeting its reconciliation commitments.


Kilikvak Kabloona is joining the National Council for Reconciliation.


“It’s a real honour,” Kabloona said in an interview Thursday.


Prior to working at the NTI, she was the Government of Nunavut’s associate deputy minister responsible for quality of life, a position focused on responding to the territory’s suicide crisis.


There, she helped secure funding for the Aqqusariaq Recovery Centre in Iqaluit, she said, a project that aligns with one of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission’s calls to action to improve Indigenous Peoples’ access to healing.


“Over my career, I’ve seen how progress can be made toward a healthier, more vibrant society through the implementation of these types of reports,” Kabloona said.


Health care in Nunavut still needs to get better, she said. More Inuit need to be working in that field and there needs to be more training available, which was also identified as a call to action, she said.


“These things will take time, it is a process and it’s important that we continually work on reconciliation. It is not a check box exercise,” she said.


Joseph Murdoch-Flowers, who joined the inaugural board in March 2025, says he has a deep respect for Kabloona, for whom he worked as a senior advisor on suicide prevention.


“She has immense competence and a deep commitment to the work that is required for reconciliation. She has the personal connections to the colonial history that gave rise to the need for this work,” said Murdoch-Flowers.


The national council exists to track Canada’s compliance with the 94 calls to action in the report of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, which, in 2015, documented the history and impacts of residential schools. 


The independent and Indigenous-led oversight body is required to publish reports on Canada’s progress on an annual basis. It formed in 2025 and

released its first report earlier this summer.


That report concluded that Canada has made progress toward meeting many calls to action, through the introduction of

rights-based legislation, child welfare discrimination settlements, increased investment and expanding distinctions-based partnerships.


However, inequities in child welfare, education, income, health and justice still persist, according to the report. 


Murdoch-Flowers said many structural changes still need to be addressed. He mentioned a lack of consistent, long-term program funding from government as one example.


“We also know that there is a rising denialism in the country,” he added.


Kabloona is one of three new directors joining the board, which is now permanent, said chairperson Julie Ann Wriston in a news release.


“Establishing the first permanent Board of the National Council for Reconciliation is a meaningful step forward. We welcome this role with gratitude and a deep sense of responsibility,” Wriston said.


Also joining are Barbara Filion, a member of the Innu Nation of Mashteuiatsh in Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean and a member of the Canadian Commission for UNESCO, and Kluane Adamek–Aagé, a former Assembly of First Nations Yukon Regional Chief from Kluane First Nation.

author: Aaron Mackey
title: California’s “Addictive Feeds” Law Violates Teens’ First Amendment Rights
content:
A California law that prohibits teens from receiving recommended social media content from other social media users violates their First Amendment rights, EFF argued this week.

The case, Meta v. Bonta, challenges SB 976, which requires that teen social media users get their parents’ permission before seeing other users’ recommended speech on their social media feeds. The legal challenge to SB 976 has largely centered on how the law violates social media services’ First Amendment rights to curate user-generated content and present it as they see fit.

But the friend-of-of the-court brief EFF filed along with the Center for Democracy & Technology and the Wikimedia Foundation shows that the law violates teen users’ First Amendment rights, too.

“SB 976 frustrates young people’s ability to use the internet to its full potential, prohibiting them from relying on tools that disseminate their speech and help them view and interact with other users’ speech,” the brief argues.

Recommendation systems have a dual purpose on social media: they help all users discover speech and content by other users, and to get their own speech in front of a wider audience.

“SB 976 creates significant, constitutionally violative, burdens on young users’ ability to read and comment on the news, discuss politics, find and share art, share their religious beliefs, or even practice their religion with fellow members of their faith,” the brief argues. “There is simply too much content on services for users to sift through manually, and young users may not know what to search for or even how to find content.”

Because SB 976 creates such broad burdens on teens’ ability to distribute and receive speech, it should be struck down on First Amendment grounds. But as EFF’s brief argues, the First Amendment doesn’t stop California and other states from passing laws that help all users, regardless of age, avoid major social media services’ harmful surveillance business models.

“One could imagine a law that required services to minimize the amount of data they collect, or limit using more invasive data analysis practices, such as tracking users across multiple services, analyzing keystrokes, and other surveillance-intensive practices,” the brief argues. “Such restrictions likely would serve the state’s aim of protecting all internet users—including minors—and would be more narrowly tailored to addressing the harms those practices cause than SB 976.”

author: Luke Goldstein
title: Democrats Backed by Industry Super PACs Are Writing the Party’s AI Plan
content:
Members of the commission received outsized financial support that seems intended to shape the party’s policy response.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Democratic House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) took to ABC’s Sunday morning show to assure the public that the Democratic Party is taking strong measures to combat the AI Doomsday threat roiling the country. His prime example: a Democratic House commission on artificial intelligence stacked with lawmakers who’ve received a bonanza in campaign funding from Big Tech.

In the interview, Jeffries said the purpose of the Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy, convened last December, was to “evaluate the steps that needed to be done and then present an aggressive framework … so that Congress can act.”

But according to a review of campaign finance records by The Lever, that five-person commission is filled with Democrats who have received outsized financial support this election cycle from AI-linked super PACs, executives, and investors.

The spending seems intended to shape the party’s policy response to AI, particularly if Democrats win a majority in November.

“If it was tone deaf in December to think that the favorite Democrats of tech oligarchs should lead the way on the biggest issue in our political economy, it is a failure of each and every one of the five senses to retain those people in a year of ever increasing anger at data centers and alarm about the good faith of the industry,” said Jeff Hauser, executive director of watchdog group Revolving Door Project, which criticized Jeffries’ appointments to the commission last year because of the members’ longstanding record of deference to Silicon Valley.

The commission’s members are Reps. Ted Lieu (D-Calif.), Valerie Foushee (D-N.C.), Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.), Frank Pallone Jr. (D-N.J.), and Zoe Lofgren (D-Calif.).

Lofgren, who represents a safe blue California district, has long aligned with the tech industry’s power players. Among the five largest campaign contributors to her all-but-certain reelection efforts this cycle is the tech investor Ron Conway, known as “the Godfather of Silicon Valley.” Conway and his wife have donated $44,000 to Lofgren’s fundraising committee, Lofgren Victory Fund, as well as $14,000 directly to her campaign committee, according to a review of campaign finance records.

Just this week, amid calls for an AI slowdown, Conway launched a new policy initiative, Project Blueprint, with the explicit purpose of mending fences between the AI sector and the Democratic Party. One of its new hires is Jay Carney, former press secretary for the Obama White House, who later sold his services to Big Tech giants like Amazon.

Conway is also a top backer of Leading the Future, a super PAC that launched last year to champion the AI industry. OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale, and Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz of venture capital firm A16z are also among the super PAC’s largest donors.

Armed with a $100 million war chest, Leading the Future has sought to topple candidates who favor AI safety legislation, including Alex Bores, who, as a state assembly member, authored New York’s AI safety law. This summer, when Bores ran in the Democratic primary for New York’s 12th Congressional District, the PAC spent more than $8 million to defeat him.

Following an Anthropic whistleblower sounding the AI Doomsday alarm this week and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s subsequent quasi-heel turn on safety measures, Bores blasted the company’s hypocrisy for opposing regulations and financing Leading the Future.

“Never thought I’d live to see the day when OpenAI gov affairs claims to have supported all the bills they lobbied against,” Bores posted on X.

Gottheimer, co-chair of the Democrats’ AI Commission, has also received campaign backing from Leading the Future, which endorsed his candidacy in April even though he didn’t face a primary challenge this year. The congressman also received a modest contribution from OpenAI’s lead congressional lobbyist, Justin Oswald.

At the same time, another AI political action network, Public First Action, has sung Gottheimer’s praises. author: Wanessa Celina
title: Pessoas negras são alvo da maioria dos gastos com prisões em 25 estados e DF, diz estudo
content:
A cada R$ 10 gastos com prisões no ano passado, em 26 unidades federativas do país, R$ 6 foram dirigidos ao encarceramento de pessoas negras. Essa é uma das conclusões do estudo realizado pelo Centro de Pesquisa Justa sobre investimentos em

segurança pública

 nos estados brasileiros. Segundo o levantamento, divulgado nesta quinta-feira, 17 de setembro, o investimento no sistema prisional dos estados chegou a R$ 22,3 bilhões, valor que não abrange apenas o Acre, que não forneceu os dados ao Justa. Desse total, R$ 13,7 bilhões foram gastos tendo como alvo pessoas pretas ou pardas.


“Cria-se uma falácia de que pessoas negras cometem mais crimes, por isso que estão presas. Mas isso é uma falácia. Na verdade, essas pessoas estão sendo selecionadas pela polícia e, depois, na frente do juiz, que poderia parar esse processo de seletividade penal, [e também frente ao] Ministério Público. [Essa] engrenagem vem sendo construída dessa forma, essas pessoas estão sendo o alvo dessa política de segurança”, explica a advogada do

Justa

, Sofia Fromer, doutora em saúde coletiva da Faculdade de Ciências Médicas da Santa Casa (FCMSC) de São Paulo. Para ela, o encarceramento da população negra confirma, mais uma vez, a existência de lógica punitivista e uma seletividade penal.


Egressos: um orçamento 5.423 vezes menor


Para a advogada, a medida mais eficiente para transformar a lógica do sistema carcerário seria investir em políticas públicas de reinserção para egressos do sistema prisional.

 Essa medida, entretanto, está longe de ser priorizada pelos estados brasileiros. Segundo o Justa, para cada R$ 5.423 gastos em 2025 com as polícias estaduais (militar, civil e técnico-científica), apenas R$ 1 é dirigido às políticas para egressos.


Na comparação com o ano anterior, o investimento permaneceu praticamente o mesmo, passando de R$ 18 milhões, para políticas exclusivas aos egressos em 2024, para R$ 19 milhões no ano passado. O valor corresponde, em média, a 0,001% de seus gastos totais levantados pelo estudo.


Entre as 26 unidades federativas avaliadas, 19 delas (72%) não investiram em políticas exclusivas para egressos.

 Tocantins teve dotação aprovada na Lei Orçamentária Anual, mas não utilizou os recursos. Rio Grande do Sul e Santa Catarina registraram investimentos pela primeira vez em 2025, com R$ 414 mil e R$ 177 mil, respectivamente. Alagoas e Tocantins deixaram de investir. São Paulo foi o estado que utilizou o maior recurso, R$ 13,3 milhões, seguido pelo Ceará, com R$ 3,8 milhões. Mato Grosso investiu R$ 781 mil, enquanto a Bahia despendeu R$ 482 mil.


Para Fromer, políticas para egressos são multissetoriais, envolvem saúde, educação, assistência social, além do campo do direito, “para que essas pessoas possam criar novas rotas e que não seja uma possibilidade que elas precisem voltar para as prisões”, salienta.


A advogada lembra que não existe pena perpétua no Brasil, portanto, o Estado precisa pensar como as pessoas egressas “vão conseguir um trabalho, renda, ter uma casa, ter os seus documentos. Ter o contato, por exemplo, [no caso] de mulheres presas, com os filhos que deixaram sob o cuidado de uma outra pessoa”, explica.


Policiamento ostensivo recebe a maior parcela do dinheiro


Polícias militares recebem a maior parte do orçamento em segurança pública dos estados analisados, 58,6% do total


O estudo também demonstra que se os recursos com a política para manter as pessoas fora das prisões são baixos, os gastos com a repressão são os mais altos. O total de investimentos envolvendo os 26 territórios foi de R$ 103,5 bilhões no ano passado, e a maior parte desses recursos foi para as Polícias Militares, R$ 60,7 bilhões, 58,6% do total, responsáveis pelo policiamento ostensivo da população. Já as Polícias Civis, que devem investigar os crimes, receberam R$ 22,2 bilhões (21,5%), e as Polícias Técnico-Científicas ficaram com a menor parcela, R$ 2,8 bilhões (2,7%), mesmo sendo responsáveis por atividades como perícia e produção de provas.


“Quando o investimento em policiamento ostensivo cresce sem que a investigação e produção de provas avancem na mesma proporção, o sistema amplia sua capacidade de prender sem necessariamente fortalecer sua eficiência para esclarecer os crimes.

É uma lógica que ajuda a sustentar um modelo de encarceramento em massa, marcado por fragilidades na apuração da autoria e na produção de evidências

”, avalia Luciana Zaffalon, diretora-executiva do Justa.

title: Sînemok: A village where history and nature meet at the foot of Qandil Mountain
content:
Located at the foot of Qandil Mountain, the village of Sînemok stands out not only for its natural beauty but also for its historical structures. Situated next to the village of Suredê on the slopes of Qandil Mountain, the village is home to vineyards and gardens filled with numerous fruit trees surrounding both old and new buildings.


Resembling a forest surrounded by fruit trees, Sînemok draws particular attention for its old structures. Villagers are committed to preserving these buildings, which bear traces of their history and culture. For the village elders, these structures also hold important memories of the past.


Although the exact date when the village was founded is unknown, according to accounts from elderly villagers, Sînemok’s history dates back at least a hundred years.


Mam, one of the oldest residents of the village, describes its history and life as follows: “I was born in this village. My father and grandfather were also born here. It is an old and ancient village. Sînemok’s history goes back many years. I am not old enough to remember when the village was founded.”


Mam also recounts a story he heard from his elders about the origin of the village’s name, although he says he does not know whether it is true:


“There was once a wedding in Sînemok. A dengbêj came from Rojhilat (East Kurdistan) for the wedding. He was impressed by the beauty of the village women, and many of the songs he performed at the wedding were about their tall and graceful figures. After that, the village came to be known as Sînemok. That is how the name of the village spread.”


It is said that in the Mukriyan dialect, Sînemok means “the chest of the mountain.”


Work in the village is carried out collectively and communally


Sînemok stands out as a small and charming village. There are not many houses in the village, and residents make their living through gardening, agriculture and livestock farming. The village has no madrasa, hospital or school. Various agricultural products were grown there in the past, and work in the village is carried out collectively and communally.


As soon as you enter the village, the warm welcome and hospitality of the villagers stand out. The villagers’ deep connection to and love for life are also reflected in their social relations. The village elders, in particular, evoke a sense of reaching into the depths of history. Their life experiences seem to be reflected in the expressions on their faces.


‘I want our children to stay in their own country’


Hanîfe Mîne, who lives in Sînemok, describes her feelings about life in the village and its social relations as follows:


“The population in the cities has increased, and people visit the villages less often. In the past, social relations were stronger and work was done together. It was very beautiful. Now, people in the cities are more occupied with education and work. But here in the village, we are more involved in agriculture.”


Hanîfe Mîne also expresses her concerns and expectations regarding the threats facing village life and culture in the following words:


“I want Kurdistan to always remain beautiful. I hope efforts will be made so that our young people do not have to go abroad. I want our children to stay in their own country, to have opportunities here and not be forced to leave their homeland. Every time a child leaves, a mother’s heart aches. Young people lose their lives because of the hardships involved in going abroad. A mother may not even be able to receive her child’s body. If there are opportunities here, none of them will go abroad.”


‘Qandil has been a stronghold for all four parts of Kurdistan’


Mam Hecî Resul, who lives near the village of Sînemok, said that he was born at the foot of Qandil in 1968 and described the significance of Qandil for the Kurdish people as follows:


“Qandil has been a stronghold for all four parts of Kurdistan throughout every period and every stage of history. All the achievements of the Kurdish people have taken place in Qandil. For this reason, Qandil has played a very significant role. So many heroic peshmerga, prominent figures and people committed to the struggle have emerged from these villages. No matter how much we speak about the history of these villages, it would never be enough. I hope that the struggle for freedom and the peace project will succeed and that Leader Apo (Abdullah Öcalan) will be free, so that greater service can be rendered to the cause of the Kurdish …

author: Unknown
title: Uçum says commission in which Öcalan will take part has been determined
content:
Presidential Chief Adviser and Deputy Chair of the Presidential Legal Policies Board Mehmet Uçum met with journalists at the Turkish Press Federation and made statements regarding the peace and democratization process.


Uçum stated that four subcommittees had been established under the Monitoring and Evaluation Board, which was formed within the scope of the Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion.


One of these bodies is the Subcommittee on Disarmament and Strategic Coordination, Uçum said, adding that Abdullah Öcalan would also take part in this subcommittee.


Uçum said that this should not be interpreted differently. He noted that the working space established on İmralı had also been arranged to enable the Kurdish leader to fulfill his role in the process.


October and November could be critical in the next stage of the process, Uçum said, adding that if developments on the ground show progress, the National Security Council (MGK) decision on the process could be finalized by November.


The "Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion,” known as the “Framework Law,” was passed by parliament with a record number of votes on the night of August 10. For the 12-article legislation to enter into force, the National Security Council (MGK) must determine and confirm that all organizations affiliated with the PKK/KCK have dissolved themselves and that arms have been completely laid down. If this condition is met, the legislation provides for the postponement of investigations, prosecutions and finalized convictions in relation to the offences covered by the proposal. The legislation excludes from its scope people who received aggravated life sentences before 2005 or who were convicted of offences carrying an aggravated life sentence.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish child ‘tortured for murder confession’ after IRGC Intelligence arrest
content:
Arzhin Jondi, a 16-year-old Kurdish child from the village of Kuper in Piranshahr, has been arrested by the Intelligence Organisation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and is being tortured and pressured into making a forced confession to involvement in the killing of an IRGC member, an informed source in Piranshahr told the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN).


The source said: “After his father died, the 16-year-old lived with his uncle’s family in the village of Kuper. On the evening of 11 September, an IRGC member named Eslam Kak-Darvishi was killed in the village when unidentified armed individuals opened fire on him.”


According to the source, following the killing, Kak-Darvishi’s family destroyed the home of Jondi’s uncle and claimed that the child had been involved in his killing. However, a group called Khori Hiwa had claimed responsibility for the attack.


The source said Jondi had travelled to another village to visit his mother when he was summoned to the local office of the IRGC Intelligence Organisation in Piranshahr on 12 September. He reported to the office accompanied by a family member and was subsequently arrested.


Around the time of his arrest, Iranian state media reported that IRGC Intelligence Organisation forces had arrested the “killer” of the IRGC member, but did not identify the arrested individual.


The source added that Jondi has been denied access to a lawyer and family visits since his arrest and is being tortured and pressured into confessing to involvement in the killing.

author: Unknown
title: Uçum points to 16 April for the 2028 elections: Erdoğan to run again
content:
Mehmet Uçum, Chief Advisor to the President and Deputy Chair of the Presidential Council for Legal Policies, discussed the 2028 elections during a meeting with journalists at the Turkish Press Federation.


Uçum said he expects the elections to be held on 16 April 2028, stating: “This date is the anniversary of the referendum through which we transitioned to the presidential system. It has symbolic significance.” Uçum also said that Recep Tayyip Erdoğan would run for the final time.


According to Uçum’s statement, holding the elections on April 16 would mean bringing the existing electoral timetable forward by approximately three weeks. While the regular date for the next general elections is calculated as 7 May 2028, Uçum had previously said that this should not be considered an “early election,” but rather a change of date resulting from the Grand National Assembly of Türkiye (TBMM) deciding to renew the elections.


For the elections to be held on 16 April, the TBMM would need to decide to renew the elections with the votes of 360 members of parliament. Uçum said such a decision could be made in February 2028.


There have previously been different statements from figures within the governing bloc regarding the election date. MHP Chairman Devlet Bahçeli said that the regular election calendar puts the date at 14 May 2028, while arguing that the term “renewal of elections” rather than “early election” should be used for an earlier date.

title: Following in grandma’s footsteps

title: İsveç'te oyların tamamı sayıldı: Merkez sol blok kazandı, Başbakan istifasını sundu
content:
İsveç'te 13 Eylül'de yapılan genel seçimi, Sosyal Demokratlar liderliğindeki Merkez Parti, Yeşiller Partisi ve Sol Partiden oluşan merkez sol blok 3 sandalye farkla kazandı. Resmi olmayan sonuçların paylaşılmasının ardından sağ blokta bulunan Ilımlı Muhafazakar Parti lideri ve mevcut Başbakan Ulf Kristersson istifa etti.

İsveç Devlet Televizyonu SVT, resmi olmayan sonuçlara göre oyların tamamının sayıldığını, Sosyal Demokratlar liderliğinde Merkez Parti, Yeşiller Partisi ve Sol Partinin oluşturduğu merkez sol blok oyların yüzde 49,5'ini alarak 349 sandalyeli parlamentoda (Riksdag) 176 sandalye kazandığını aktardı.

İktidardaki sağ blok partileri Ilımlı Muhafazakar Parti, Hristiyan Demokratlar, Liberaller ile mevcut hükümete dışarıdan destek veren İsveç Demokratlarının oy oranı ise yüzde 48,8 oldu, sağ blok parlamentoda 173 sandalye elde etti.

Ulusal medya, Sosyal Demokratlar lideri Magdalena Andersson'un bloktaki diğer partilere hükümet kurma görüşmeleri için davet gönderdiğini belirtti.

İsveç Demokratları lideri Jimmie Akesson'un ise muhalefette yer almaları durumunda parti liderliği görevine ara vermesinin beklendiği aktarıldı.

Başbakan Ulf Kristersson sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda, İsveç Parlamentosu Başkanı Andreas Norlen'e istifa mektubunu sunduğunu belirterek, "Yeni hükümetin kurulmasına yönelik adımlara Meclis Başkanı Norlen öncülük edecek" ifadesini kullandı.

İsveç'te genel seçime ilişkin resmi sonuçların hafta sonu açıklanması beklenirken, yeni parlamentonun 28 Eylül'de toplanacağı kaydedildi. Kayıtlı 8 milyon civarında seçmenin bulunduğu İsveç'te 13 Eylül'deki genel seçime katılım oranı yüzde 84,4 olmuştu. İsveç'te seçmenler, 349 sandalyeli parlamentonun (Riksdag) yanı sıra 21 bölgesel meclis ve 290 belediye meclisi üyesini belirlemek için de oy kullanmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Caught Reviewing Plan to Demolish Kennedy Center in Air Force One
content:
Through the windows of Air Force One, he was pictured holding a poster that seemingly says “Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED.”

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A photographer captured extraordinary pictures of President Donald Trump looking at a seeming plan to demolish the Kennedy Center through the windows of Air Force One on Wednesday evening, as the president has repeatedly vowed to impose his will on the 55-year-old cultural building regardless of court orders against him.

The pictures, captured by Washington, D.C. photojournalist Brendan Smialowski, show Trump sitting inside his presidential plane looking at a large poster that appears to say “Kennedy Center DEMOLISHED” on top. The poster, which is partially obscured, shows a view of the building with excavation and construction equipment around it.

Other pictures showed Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte carrying poster boards while descending the steps of the plane, which had just landed at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland. As Pulte exits, he is carrying the posters in a way that only shows the blank backs, hiding their contents. Pulte also seems to be present in the photo of Trump reviewing the poster.

Trump has taken steps to demolish or close the center if he isn’t allowed to rename it after himself, after losing a series of court battles barring him from placing his name on the building or doing major renovations or reconstructions.

“I think that the Trump administration should certainly have recognition. Because frankly, if we don’t do that, it’s going to close. It’ll end up being ripped down,” the president said to reporters before boarding Air Force One in North Carolina on Wednesday.

This comment came after a member of the legal team fighting the Trump administration on the Kennedy Center maneuverings submitted court testimony that, on Wednesday, she witnessed a forklift repeatedly ramming a column of the building.

Bridget Kennedy-Bailey, a staff member of the counsel in the case, said that she visited the Kennedy Center and attempted to enter on Wednesday morning. This was a day after Trump’s handpicked Kennedy Center board decided to close the building for a two-year renovation, just hours after a federal judge blocked Trump from putting his name on the building.

Kennedy-Bailey said that the security guard barred her from entering, telling her that the center was closed. She then said that black metal fences were quickly erected during the remainder of that morning, and that forklifts were bringing more gates that resembled those using construction sites.

“I saw a forklift carrying what appeared to be a more permanent form of fencing drive over to the north side of the building. I saw the forklift run into and hit the pillars on the building several times,” Kennedy-Bailey said. “I declare under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true and correct.”

Lawyers for the legal group, representing Rep. Joyce Beatty (D-Ohio), submitted the pictures of Trump viewing the poster in a court filing, as well as Trump’s comments from the tarmac. The court has evidently ordered the Trump administration to explain its actions with regard to the latest developments — but the administration has been openly defying court orders in the case, closing the building earlier this week despite a federal judge having barred it from doing so.

title: Kanada Başbakanı Carney, AB'nin ortak üyelik önerisini memnuniyetle karşıladı
content:
Kanada Başbakanı Mark Carney, Avrupa Birliği (AB) Komisyonu Başkanı Ursula von der Leyen'in Kanada'nın AB'nin ilk "ortak üyesi" olmasına yönelik önerisini memnuniyetle karşıladıklarını söyledi.

Strazburg'da düzenlenen Avrupa Parlamentosu (AP) Genel Kurulunda milletvekillerine hitap eden Carneu, Von der Leyen'in bir gün önce AB ile Kanada arasındaki Kapsamlı Ekonomik ve Ticaret Anlaşması'nın (CETA) ötesine geçen bir gelecek ittifakı kurulmasından söz ettiğini hatırlatarak "AB Komisyonu Başkanı von der Leyen, Kanada'nın AB'nin ilk ortak üyesi olmasına kapıyı açtı. Kanada bu hedefi memnuniyetle karşılıyor" dedi.

Carney, Kanadalıların büyük çoğunluğunun Avrupa ile daha yakın ilişkiler kurulmasını desteklediğini belirtti.

Kanada ile AB'nin ortak değerlere ve birbirini tamamlayan ekonomik güçlere sahip olduğunu dile getiren Carney, "Kanada ve Avrupa, kritik mineraller, savunma sanayi kapasitesi, yapay zeka ve bilgi işlem, enerji güvenliği, uzay ve ödeme sistemleri dahil bütün stratejik alanlarda derin işbirliği yaparak stratejik özerkliklerini güvence altına almalıdır" diye konuştu.

Güçlü bir ekonominin kendi başına amaç değil, adil bir toplum oluşturmanın aracı olduğuna inandıklarını belirten Carney, refahın paylaşıldıkça büyüdüğünü söyledi.

Carney, dünyada egemenlik ile ekonomik açıklığı bağdaştırmanın giderek zorlaştığına işaret ederek, "Ekonomik bütünleşme artık bir silah olarak kullanılıyor. Tarifeler baskı kurmak, finansal mekanizmalar ise zorlama amacıyla devreye sokuluyor. Tedarik zincirleri, istismar edilebilecek zayıf noktalar haline geliyor" ifadelerini kullandı.

Teknolojinin savaşın niteliğini, ekonomilerin yapısını ve devletlerin yönetme kabiliyetini değiştirdiğini anlatan Carney, Kanada ile AB'nin birlikte hareket ederek ortak değerlerini ve egemenliklerini daha güçlü biçimde koruyabileceğini vurguladı. Carney, günümüzde egemenliğin yalnızca gıda, enerji ve savunma ihtiyaçlarını karşılayabilmek anlamına gelmediğini belirterek, "Artık yapay zekaya, yarı iletkenlere, kritik minerallere, ödeme sistemlerine, temiz enerji teknolojilerine, aşılara ve uzay tabanlı iletişim sistemlerine güvenli erişimi de gerektiriyor" dedi.

Ülkelerin stratejik alanlardaki eksikliklerini tek başlarına kapatamayacağını dile getiren Carney, Kanada ve Avrupa'nın birlikte daha güçlü olacağını ifade etti.

Tarım dışı mallar ve geniş bir hizmet yelpazesinde kesintisiz dijital ticarete geçilmesi gerektiğini vurgulayan Carney, gençlerin Atlantik'in iki yakasında daha kolay çalışmasına, eğitim görmesine ve yaşamasına imkan sağlanmasını istedi.

Kanada'nın Erasmus eğitim programına katılmasının öğrencilere yeni fırsatlar sunacağını ifade eden Carney, yeni nesil Horizon Europe araştırma programına üyeliğin de ileri teknolojilerde ortak çalışmalar yürütülmesine katkı sağlayacağını söyledi.

Kanada'nın enerji dönüşümü açısından önem taşıyan 34'ten fazla kritik mineral rezervine sahip olduğuna dikkati çeken Carney, ülkesinin Avrupa'nın güvenilir ham madde tedariki arayışına katkı sağlayabileceğini belirtti.

Carney, Kanada'nın yeni liman altyapıları geliştirerek Avrupa'nın enerji güvenliğini desteklemek üzere büyük miktarda sıvılaştırılmış doğal gaz (LNG) ve hidrojen sağlayabileceğini kaydetti.

Tarafların yapay zeka güvenliği protokolleri hazırlayabileceğini, ortak standartlar geliştirebileceğini ve bütünleşmiş bir finansal hizmetler pazarı oluşturma imkanını değerlendirebileceğini aktaran Carney, Kanada ile AB'nin güçlü yönlerinin birbirini tamamladığını dile getirdi. Kanada'nın AB'nin ortak savunma tedarik programı SAFE'e katılan ilk Avrupa dışı ülke olduğunu hatırlatan Carney, CETA'nın da ilişkilerin geliştirilmesi için güçlü temel oluşturduğunu söyledi.

Carney, önerdikleri ittifakın diğer büyük güçlere rakip olacak üçüncü bir blok kurmayı amaçlamadığını vurgulayarak, hedeflerinin kimsenin açık pazarlarını kontrol edemeyeceği, egemenliklerini zedeleyemeyeceği veya özgürlüklerini tehdit edemeyeceği bir dayanıklılık oluşturmak olduğunu ifade etti.

AB'de mevcut durumda "ortak üyelik" adı altında hukuken tanımlanmış resmi bir statü bulunmuyor. Tarafların bu kavramın kapsamını ve hukuki çerçevesini gelecek görüşmelerde belirlemesi bekleniyor.

ABD Başkanı Donald Trump ise AB'nin Kanada'ya yönelik "ortak üyelik" yaklaşımını eleştirerek, bunu "düşmanca bir hareket" olarak değerlendirmesi halinde Avrupa'ya ciddi tarifeler uygulayabileceğini veya birçok alanda ticareti durdurabileceğini söylemişti.

author: Scot Nakagawa
title: Being a dissident is a capacity, not a calling
content:
This article

Being a dissident is a capacity, not a calling

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


This article was originally published on

The Anti-Authoritarian Playbook

.


We tend to imagine the dissident as a particular kind of person, one who’s born unafraid, temperamentally a rebel, built from some sterner material than the rest of us. It’s a comforting story, and it’s comforting in a way that quietly lets us off the hook. If dissidents are simply made differently, then their courage is admirable but not instructive. We can applaud it, but we are excused from it.


The great gift of Gal Beckerman’s “How to Be a Dissident” is that it dismantles that story, gently and completely. Beckerman — a staff writer at 

The Atlantic

 who has spent a career studying how change actually begins — went looking for what dissidents across history and around the globe have in common. What he found is not a personality type. It’s a set of practices. Dissidence, in his telling, is not a calling reserved for the few. It’s a human capacity, and capacities can be cultivated.


The book is organized as 10 imperatives — among them Be Pessimistic, Be Funny, Be Reckless, and Be Immortal — and under each, Beckerman gathers figures who could not seem more unlike one another: Socrates and Ai Weiwei, thinkers like Hannah Arendt and Iris Murdoch, the famous and the nearly forgotten. It is part intellectual history, part biography, part field manual. Its through-line is a journey every reader can recognize: the solitary moment of seeing a truth clearly, the frightening decision to say it out loud, and the long question of what that act leaves behind.


Some of the imperatives are bracing precisely because they cut against what we expect. “Be Pessimistic,” as I read it, is no counsel of despair — it’s the insistence that the dissident does not need optimism’s permission to act. You don’t have to believe you’ll win in order to refuse to comply. “Be Funny” recovers humor as a serious instrument, the thing that punctures the false solemnity on which authoritarian power depends. These are not slogans. They are, genuinely, instructions.


But the book’s most empowering move is subtler than any single chapter. It’s Beckerman’s steady attention to the fact that most of the people in these pages were, for most of their lives, conformists. They were not waiting for the barricades. They held jobs, kept their heads down, made the small daily accommodations everyone makes. And then something — a death, a lie too large to swallow, a knock on a neighbor’s door — moved them across a line they hadn’t planned to cross. Dissidence, Beckerman shows, usually begins not with heroism but with a refusal: a single moment when a person decides that they will not, this time, betray what they know to be true.


That reframing matters, because it relocates courage. Courage is no longer the possession of the extraordinary. It’s a decision available, in principle, to anyone, including the version of each of us who has spent years being reasonable, being careful, being quiet.


Nowhere is this clearer than in the book’s account of the Madres de Plaza de Mayo — the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo — and it is, for me, the heart of the book.


They weren’t activists. They were ordinary Argentine women whose children had been “disappeared” by the military junta in the late 1970s — seized, tortured, killed and erased, while a terrified country was instructed to notice nothing. Public assembly was forbidden. So the mothers did something almost absurdly modest: they went to the plaza in front of the presidential palace, and because the police told them they couldn’t stand still there, they walked. They walked in a slow circle, week after week, wearing white headscarves made from their children’s cloth diapers, some embroidered with a missing child’s name.


That was the whole of it, at first — a handful of women walking in a circle. It looked like nothing. It was, in fact, one of the bravest acts in the modern history of the hemisphere. The junta could disappear individuals in the dark; it could not so easily explain away mothers grieving in broad daylight, in the most public square in the country, refusing to leave. The Madres made the regime’s central lie — that nothing was happening — impossible to sustain. Their persistence drew the eyes of the world. And their small circling walk became one of the moral forces that stripped the dictatorship of its legitimacy …

author: Redação
title: Agência Pública lança e-book gratuito sobre desinformação e notícias falsas
content:
A

Agência Pública

 lançou um e-book gratuito sobre desinformação na era digital, desenvolvido pela jornalista Natalia Viana, diretora executiva e cofundadora da

Pública

, e pelo tecnólogo Babak Fakhamzadeh. O material explica o que é desinformação, como funcionam as fake news e quais estratégias estão por trás da criação e circulação desses conteúdos. Também apresenta um guia prático com seis passos para identificar notícias falsas e aborda o método jornalístico, a inteligência artificial e os novos desafios para reconhecer informações na internet.


O e-book pode ser baixado gratuitamente. Basta se inscrever nas newsletters da

Pública


neste link

 para receber o material diretamente no e-mail. 


O guia apresenta diferentes tipos de desinformação, explica a estrutura de uma campanha para circular conteúdos falsos e os diferentes atores envolvidos em sua produção e distribuição, além de discutir os interesses que podem estar por trás disso.


O e-book é destinado para quem busca compreender melhor como a desinformação funciona e aprender a reconhecer conteúdos falsos ou enganosos. E pode ser utilizado por educadores, estudantes, organizações, jornalistas e outras pessoas interessadas em desenvolver ferramentas para reconhecer informações falsas e conteúdos manipulados.


O material foi desenvolvido a partir da oficina “Como diferenciar notícias falsas de verdadeiras”, ministrada pela jornalista Natalia Viana e pelo desenvolvedor Babak Fakhamzadeh. A atividade aconteceu no Centro de Pesquisa e Formação do SESC, dentro da programação comemorativa dos

15 anos da Agência Pública

.

title: Süper Lig ve 1. Lig yayın ihalesi ne zaman? TFF tarih verdi
content:
Türkiye Futbol Federasyonu (TFF), Süper Lig ve 1. Lig yayın haklarının devrine ilişkin düzenlenecek ihalenin tarihini açıkladı. İhale, 13 Ocak 2027 Çarşamba günü gerçekleştirilecek.

TFF Başkanı İbrahim Ethem Hacıosmanoğlu ile kulüp başkanları, 2026-2027 sezonu ve devam eden sezonlar için Süper Lig ve 1. Lig müsabakalarının yayın haklarının devrine ilişkin düzenlenecek ihale kapsamında Riva’da bir araya geldi.

TFF Hasan Doğan Milli Takımlar Kamp ve Eğitim Tesisleri’nde gerçekleştirilen toplantıda, yeni ihale dönemine ilişkin yol haritası ele alındı.

Toplantının ardından TFF, yayın ihalesinin 13 Ocak 2027 Çarşamba günü yapılmasının kararlaştırıldığını duyurdu.

TFF’nin açıklamasında, ihale kapsamında oluşturulan yayın ihalesi kurulunun 15 günlük periyotlarla toplantı yapmasına da karar verildiği belirtildi.

TFF açıklamasına göre, futbolda önde gelen ülkelerin sağladığı yayın gelirleri de karşılaştırmalı olarak ele alındı.

Toplantıya TFF Başkanı İbrahim Ethem Hacıosmanoğlu’nun yanı sıra Türkiye Süper Lig Profesyonel Futbol Kulüpleri Birliği Vakfı ve Trabzonspor Başkanı Ertuğrul Doğan, 1. Lig Futbol Kulüpleri Derneği ve İstanbulspor Başkanı Ecmel Faik Sarıalioğlu, Beşiktaş Başkanı Serdal Adalı, Galatasaray Başkanı Dursun Özbek, İstanbul Başakşehir FK Başkanı Göksel Gümüşdağ ve Göztepe Onursal Başkanı Mehmet Sepil katıldı.

Toplantıda ayrıca Galatasaray Başkan Vekili Abdullah Kavukcu, TFF Başkan Vekilleri Mecnun Otyakmaz ve Fuat Göktaş, TFF Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Fazlı Çilingir ile TFF Genel Sekreteri Abdullah Ayaz ve Genel Sekreter Yardımcıları Özcan Şepik ile Erkan Kıraç da yer aldı.

author: Jon Queally
title: US Once Again Denies Palestinian Officials Visas to Attend New York UN Meeting
content:
Palestinian Authority leader Mahmoud Abbas will have to deliver remarks and participate in meetings via video link.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

For the second year in a row, the US government under President Donald Trump has denied diplomatic visas for Palestinian Authority leader Mahmoud Abbas and other Palestinian officials — a move condemned by the PA and outside critics as counter to international peace efforts.

Abbas, who leads both the PA and the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO), was to attend meetings at the United Nations in New York City next week, but the move by the US State Department means he will have to deliver remarks and participate in meetings via video link.

In a statement, the foreign ministry of the PA called the refusal of visas “an unjustified measure that runs counter to efforts to rebuild trust, develop Palestinian-US relations, and create the necessary political climate for implementing the two-state solution and achieving peace and stability.”

The US State Department said the refusal of visas was justified, in part, because of the efforts by Palestinian leaders to seek redress for crimes against their people carried out by the Israeli government by pursuing actions through both the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ) as well as for efforts toward “unilateral recognition” with UN members states.

They should move UNGA to Geneva https://t.co/tDBBdxBlYn

Palestinian pursuits at the ICC and ICJ, the State Department charged in a statement, constitute “taking actions to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict.” While the US has steadfastly backed Israel politically and armed its military during recent years while it has carried out what experts, including those backed by the UN itself, have characterized as “genocide” in Gaza and grave crimes in the Occupied West Bank, the US accused Palestinian leaders of “glorifying terrorism” to justify the visa bans.

Critics of the US move called it a betrayal of its obligations as host nation of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), headquartered in New York City.

Mohammed Maree, head of media and public opinion studies at the Egyptian Center for Strategic Studies, an independent research institution, said that denying Abbas entry to attend the UNGA “confirms that Washington has effectively abandoned its supposed role in the Middle East peace process and fully embraced Israel’s agenda.”

The move, added Maree, “once again exposes the stark contradiction between Washington’s rhetoric about peace and its actual policies. In the medium term, it will become clear that attempting to eliminate the two-state solution in line with Israel’s wishes will bring neither stability nor the peace the region desperately needs. Instead, it will only fuel further escalation and uncertainty.”

In its statement, the PA Foreign Ministry rejected the US stance.

“Resorting to international institutions and international law is a legitimate right of the State of Palestine and a peaceful, legal means to protect the Palestinian people and their rights,” it stated. “This cannot be equated with the policies of occupation, settlement expansion, annexation, displacement, and settler violence [by Israelis] — actions that pose the real threat to the two-state solution and prospects for peace.”

The ministry further called for the Trump administration to reconsider its decision and “halt the policy of sanctions and restrictions, and engage in a direct, serious Palestinian-US dialogue to address any points of contention.”

“The State of Palestine,” the statement concluded, “will continue to fulfill its national and international obligations, pursue its reform program, and utilize peaceful political, diplomatic, and legal means to defend its people’s rights, stressing that it will not relinquish their right to self-determination, freedom, and stability.”
